**Pages 179-182 — Udbodhan (Opening Address)**

1. Many a sakhi and word have been spoken, yet the mind does not hold itself steady. So Jivana speaks this request: listen, you, to Ramkabir. ||1||

The teaching that Jivanji Maharaj gave in the course of his conversation with Nana Gopaldas has been gathered into these sakhis. In the Prabodh ka Ang, Jivanji Maharaj states that great effort has been made, through sakhis and through hymns, to explain bhakti (devotion) to everyone. But for one who falls into confusion on seeing so many kinds of worship and devotion, whatever is said to him and whatever counsel is offered, still the mind does not become steady enough to keep unshakable faith. So I make this humble request: give your attention only to that devotion to the name of Ramkabir which I am showing you.

Kabir has said:

1. In a single word everything has been said; consider the whole meaning of it. Sing the praise of Ram night and day, and abandon all thought of sense-objects. ||1||

(Kabir's own verse carries its own number 1; the address's own numbering continues below.)

Das Kabirji says that in just a few words he has set out the final, supreme conclusion: night and day sing the praise of Ram, and give up the corruptions of sensual craving. When, in his last hour, the devotees asked Jivanji Maharaj, "Have you anything to say?", he said:

2. What I had to say, I have said. Now what more shall I say — Ram be praised. Serve the sants, O Jivana, and Raghupati (Ram) will come to your help. ||2||

Jivandasji Maharaj said that whatever he had to tell them he had told them up to now; beyond that, what more should he say? But he would tell them one thing: serve the sants, and God will help you.

Looking at Jivanji Maharaj's line of thought in his sakhis, his ultimate aim is bhakti. Attracted by the worship, recitations, parayans (recitations of a whole text) and the rest that go on in the world, we get entangled in all manner of hymns, mantras and forms of worship, in vows, japa (repetition of the Name), austerities, pilgrimages and so forth. But looking at Jivanji Maharaj's aim, what he has shown is only devotion to the name of Ramkabir and the devotion of kirtan (hymn-singing). We therefore do not wish for what people of other communities do, who perform samput parayan (recitation with a repeated refrain) or japa and austerity for the sake of desire-driven devotion. That is why we have not given importance to the parayan or the ritual recitation of the sakhis. But if we reflect deeply on what Jivanji Maharaj has shown, then through the sakhis Jivanji Maharaj has drawn our attention toward prem-lakshana bhakti (devotion whose distinguishing mark is love). So, without holding desire-driven feeling in view, we should read the sakhis with a view to pondering and contemplating them. Do not make it your aim to finish a whole vishram (division of the text); read even a few sakhis, but it is necessary that you make the effort to understand them. There is no meaning in reading merely for the sake of having read.

Do not interpret the sakhis arbitrarily, each to suit himself. Knowing full well the inner sense of a sakhi, do not twist and wrench it into a contrary meaning. Follow the Sadguru's teaching and your welfare will follow. We have not held any intention of doing desire-driven recitation and parayan; therefore, as our samput (repeated refrain) we have chosen the sakhi about what Ramanand spoke, with the intention that devotion to Ram may be attained. The Sadguru takes care of everything of ours.

3. From the Sadguru's teaching comes entry into even half of the Name. Let the ocean of worldly existence be wiped away, O Jivana, and we shall come to that abode of yours. ||3||

If, in discussion with Jivanji Maharaj, we make the effort to follow even a little of the teaching, then we too shall cross the ocean of worldly existence and come to your divine abode.

Nana Gopaldas was bound to Jivanji Maharaj by an intimate relationship. In these sakhis he asks pardon for any shortcoming on his part in honouring Jivanji Maharaj as he deserved.

4. Gopaliyo is an offender; the Sadguru is not [unclear — the printed second half-line appears incomplete]. Pardon my fault, O Jivana; I am in the shade of your lotus feet. ||4||

Nana Gopaldas says: I am an offender; fitting service of the Sadguru has not been done by me, and I confess it. But be gracious to me and pardon my fault; I remain in the shelter and refuge of your feet.

He has shown us devotion to the divine name Ramkabir and told us to perform the devotion of kirtan; apart from that there is no need to fall into other long entanglements. Jivanji Maharaj has said:

5. By reading the books he became a reciter; by reading the scripture he became a qazi. Such a one is outside the company of the harijans (devotees of Hari), O Jivana — his is forever another man's service. ||5||

Jivandasji Maharaj says that a man may have become a learned pandit by reading the volumes of the scriptures, the books, the shastras and the puranas, and may have become a qazi by reciting the Book, the Quran; even so he is not counted among the harijans, the devotees of God. For such people perform another's service and devotion. In what way? Having read the shastra he behaves according to the shastra; having read the purana he acts according to the purana. All of that counts as words spoken by other people, and does not count as the vani (utterance) from the Guru's own mouth. Kabirji too has said:

6. Kabir says: by reading and reading they became reciters, but they made no reflection on the truth. They quarrelled with the devotees of Hari and made friends with the world. ||6||

Das Kabirji says that by reading the books they reached the rank of reciter, but no real reflection came of it; and they envied and were jealous of the simple, guileless devotees of God, turned their faces away from bhakti, and kept the company of the world's delusion and maya (illusion) — and that is all in vain.

All speech other than the vani from the Guru's mouth is called vyabhicharini (adulterous, faithless).

7. All speech is adulterous wherever the Guru's word is not the authority. The vani from the Guru's mouth, O Jivana — that is welfare upon welfare. ||7||

Jivandasji Maharaj says that any speech other than that which has been sanctioned from the Guru's mouth is vyabhicharini, corrupted speech. Therefore, when the vani has been spoken from the Guru's mouth, it is by that alone that our welfare and only welfare comes about, that our good and auspiciousness comes about. May all loving devotees walk in the understanding of this teaching of the Guru's vani, and may the endless grace of Sadguru Jivanji be showered — this alone is my prayer.

Well-wisher,
Swami Jagdishchandra Yadunath's
respectful and loving Ramkabir

(With grateful acknowledgement, from the first edition of Vaishnav Jivandasji's Sakhi)

sections.translation:
**Page 186 — || Sakhi ||**

1. Showing compassion upon the Kanam region, he appeared in the village of Gahej. Having held the samagam (holy gathering) at Shahpar, he came to Puniyad Dham. ||1||

2. To redeem the Kanbi lineage, Jivan took birth (avatar). Hearing of the grace shown to Krishnadas, Dhana too made himself ready. ||2||

3. To break Bhoja's delusion, to be a help to Keshav, and to wipe away Rambai's sorrow, he came from the Dvapar age into the Kali age. ||3||

4. He gave refuge to Sant Gopal, and the longings of that heart were fulfilled. Such a Sadguru did Jivan become, that the bonds of worldly existence were loosed. ||4||

5. He set out in the company of Nana Gopal and came to Puniyad Dham. Uda says: the dharma that has risen is the name of Ramkabir. ||5||

sections.translation:
**Page 187 — heading**

The aarti (lamp-hymn) to be recited at the beginning of the parayan (recitation of the whole text).

**First Aarti — of Sadguru Jivanji**

1. This is the aarti of Sadguru Jivji; let all the sants together sing his glory.
2. Boarding the boat of the Name he carries us across; he accomplishes the work of countless souls.
3. He made the Name and the Form firm in everyone; all the sants together sang the qualities of Hari.
4. Keep the company of sants day and night; drink the elixir of Ram every single day.
5. Das Dayal is at the refuge of the Sadguru, and by that the coming and going of birth and death is ended.

**Second Aarti — of Ramkabir**

1. Perform the aarti of Ramkabir — Hari, Hari — where endless millions of sants are seated.
2. The light of love fills all things to the brim; this Saheb (Lord) is the radiance within the sants.
3. He fulfils the desires of all the sants; in the Treta age it was Ram who came.
4. Destroyer of the wicked, redeemer of the sants — the name of Krishna is the deliverance of the soul.
5. Waving the offering over that beautiful face, mother Yashoda performed the aarti.
6. All the gopis together make the ras dance; Krishna, Kabir and Jivan come.
7. He plays his lila (divine play) within Vrindavan; Das Dayal rests in the shade of his feet.

**Page 188 — Third Aarti**

1. An aarti of bliss, and joy is ours: the harijans (devotees of Hari) have come, the support of my life.
2. The darshan of the sants removes my three afflictions; carry me across the ocean of birth and death.
3. Together partake of the meal of vegetables and cooked food; together in the company of sants sing the qualities of Hari.
4. House after house there is auspicious rejoicing and congratulation; there Janjivan offers himself over and over again.

**|| Samput (the refrain repeated with each reading) ||**

1. What Ramanand spoke, Das Kabir heard. That same thing the Sadguru said, O Jivana: worship Raghuvir, the lord of Sita. ||1||

Uda Uda sab ko kahe | suno Udaki sakh ||
An-dev bahe nahi Jivana | Raghupati lina rakh ||65||
Shesh sahasra mukh je jape | so sala lakhyo Hanuman ||
So sadguru kahyo Jivana | je Goripatiko dhyan ||66||
Shaligram sevu nahi | nahi swarupsu kam ||
Sadguru samjhayo Jivana | je Sitapatiko nam ||67||
Aisa guru kije Jivana | jake rup na rekh ||
Sitapati bin aur kahe | to mukh marvavun mekh ||68||
Pothi Parbrahm namki | sadguru diya batay ||
Aad avinashi Jivana | ra re ma me chit lay ||69||
Bhiksha magat Jivana | data bhaye sab sant ||
Sadguru vachane paiye | keval Kamala-kant ||70||
Maranko dar Harinam bin | dise sab sansar ||
Harijan ubare Jivana | so sadguruke upkar ||71||
Jivan sab jug bah gayo | ham hate ta mahin ||
Kaha janun re kachhu bhaya | sadguru pakadi banhi ||72||
Kripanidhan sab kahat hai | e pratit nahi mohi ||
Gurukripa bin Jivana | par na pohota koi ||73||
Dakshin disha ravi tape | uttar shashiko bhav ||
Chahudish hamare Jivana | sadguru batayo dav ||74||
Sant samagam Jivana | na jane Shankar Shesh ||
Neti neti nigam kahe | so sadgurue diyo updesh ||75||
Pakh chhuti dohodish gai | rahyo sant samagam sar ||
Sadguru shabde Jivana | utariyun pele par ||76||
Van trikha pani piye | van kshudha khaye khir ||
Guru mukh chhandi Hari bhaje | Jivan so bepir ||77||
Ko kahe Hari sun akashmen | ko kahe Hari ghat ghat mahin ||
Sadguru batayo Jivana | Shri Bansivatki chhanhi ||78||
Sajan hamare Jivana | sadguru diya batay ||
Shir mor mugat mukh morali | Vrindavan chare gay ||79||
|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Sadguru Jivan Shamalo | das Kabirji Ram ||
Antar to eto padyo | kalya kou nahi jay ||80||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Do aksharke antare | Ram Kabira ek ||
So samjhat hai Jivana | jake sadguru diyo vivek ||81||
Mel mugat bhai Jivana | jab sadguru diyo updesh ||
Sarag narak Vaikunthalu | jyun dar upade kesh ||82||
Bar skandh Shukji kahyo | lahyo na eke maram ||
Janak Videhi guru kiye Jivana | tab payo atam dharm ||83||
Dipak dina Jivana | jahan sadguru shabd vishvas ||
Andhiyara sab jagatkun | jahan karm dharmki as ||84||
Sain kahena sahel hai | kahene bohot vichar ||
E sab sahelo Jivana | jab sadguru hoy kripal ||85||
Apne apne padkun | raji hai sab koi ||
Sadguru padkun Jivana | chihne virla koi ||86||
Dasatan sab manmate | gurumate koi nahin ||
Gurumate te Jivana | je Hari charan kamalki chhanhin ||87||
Pragat pasaro Jivana | sadguru diyo batay ||
Sant samagam jhilvo | Raghuvar dulaho gay ||88||
Jag tarvekun Jivana | Ramnam Rambaan ||
Shankare sunayo narkun | so sadgurue kahyo praman ||89||
Chhelo janam bhayo Jivana | jab sadguru diyo updesh ||
Sant samagamman malyo | Ayodhya tano naresh ||90||
|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Chanderiye vase vasu | Jivan pragate ay ||
Sitapati Raghunathko | dino nam batay ||91||
Jab the Jivan pragate | tab the bhayo kalyan ||
Raksha bhai Gopalkun | ab chumbego Jamran ||92||
Gam hamaro Sahaparo | jahan sakal sant sukhdham ||
Sadguru hamare Jivana | sol kalasu Sham ||93||
Takiya tinun bahara | jahan Sitapatike sant ||
Sadguru mile Gopalkun | tab paya nam anant ||94||
Gai gavave Jivana | kahi sunave ap ||
Chidi chun jyun det hai | aise sadguru bap ||95||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Mole pani na chadhe Jivana | jo kotik mile lohar ||
Prem vina bhakti na upaje | jo ap male kartar ||96||
|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Sadguru kartan Jivana | magre viho jay ||
Bhav bandhan karm katke | keval Hari jash gay ||97||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Hari det hai ham let hai | tame nahi kisiko pad ||
Jivke to ek Jivana | jo sadguru bhaye sahay ||98||
Sabke sadguru Kabirji | mamat karo jin koi ||
Or duniyakun Jivana | sadguru gharki joi ||99||
Guru pir nahi Jivana | bhagati kare sab koy ||
Nir valove premsu | luni kaise hoy ||100||
Ajar jare nahi Jivana | jyun kukarkun khir ||
Nak chhant hoi nisare | jake nahi gurupir ||101||
|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Apa upar adare | le sadguruka ban ||
Navtu kare Jivana | to chhodve chare khan ||102||
Mir marun mere Jivana | phoj sabe bhagi jay ||
Andar basre kya kare | apa diyo uthay ||103||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Jahan lagi ek karam hoy | punarapi chho nav thay ||
Apo ubho Jivana | tahan sadguru na hoy sahay ||104||
Apo mite apda | sakal rog mit jay ||
Gurumukh hoy ke Jivana | nam nirmal jash gay ||105||
Karme kukar avataryo | pan antarjami ek ||
Sapne na janyo Jivana | sadguru tano vivek ||106||
Nam chintamani Jivana | santan diya batay ||
Tera rakhya nav rahe | jo sadguru nahi sahay ||107||
Svarg narak donun taje | nahi Vaikunthki as ||
Ramnam bhaj Jivana | jahan sadguru shabd vishvas ||108||
|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Sadguru sandesa mokala | kachabachan sab av ||
Nam chintamani Jivana | je bhave so pav ||109||
Sarasvati bichari kaha kare | jo nahi guru vachan praman ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | bhatke chare khan ||110||
Vani sab vyabhicharini | jahan nahi guru vachan praman ||
Gurumukh vani Jivana | so kalyane kalyan ||111||
To vani dhunki Jivana | sant samagam mahin ||
Mohe Sitapatiko asaro | ke Girdhariki chhanhi ||112||
Kathi gumare kaha kidhun Jivana | nahi guru vachan praman ||
Guru vachan je chinse | viran te pramane praman ||113||
Gai gumare kaha kiya | guru vachan hi praman ||
Atamne gauthayke | bhatke chare khan ||114||
So jojan lu dharan the | uncho sayar man ||
Dhasi jal lope nahi Jivana | name karvo kel ||115||
Gadyo raho Gopaliyo | sadguru shabdke bich ||
Sant samagamman Shamalo | jahan jam kinkar nahi mich ||116||
Madan jagayo manani | same ven bajay ||
Aise sadguru Jivana | ham sute liye jagay ||117||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Donun gai re Jivana | jog aur aadesh ||
Sadya dharam chhandi diya | na janyo guru updesh ||118||
Mua marda jivaye ke | amrit sinche aay ||
Aise Harigun Jivana | Sadguru bhaye sahay ||119||
Ghat ghat vyapak Jivana | pan antarjami ek ||
Main balihari ta daaski | jahan Sadguru shabd vivek ||120||
Sadguru samjhayo Jivana | gupt pragat je baat ||
Ek roop ghat ghat vase | ek Sitapati Raghunath ||121||
Ghat ghat vyapak Jivana | Sitapatiko roop ||
Guru krupa ta daaskun | ja ghat naam swaroop ||122||
Prem piyasi sundari | rahi kinare laag ||
Guru krupa bin Jivana | jalmen dekhe aag ||123||
Van govale Jivana | dhor gaye sab fail ||
Lathi le Sadguru khada | so laye apne gel ||124||

Karm dharam sab thak rahyo | thak rahyo brahmagyan ||
Guru prasade Jivana | jab samro Sitaram ||125||
Karm kohade kapiyan | jagman Jivandas ||
Sadguru samjhaiyo | je kahi Kabire das ||126||
Doodhe valu Jivana | so Sadguru tano partap ||
Ved dharam sab chhas hai | mohe bado lagyo tho paap ||127||
Sagan sambandhi bahi gayan | Sadguru shabdman haar ||
Naam chintamani Jivana | bhav jal kadhe par ||128||
Aafaniye adtun rahe | je samre Sitaram ||
Guru parsade Jivana | fite tako thaam ||129||
Mat melavo bichhdo | tat gayo bad bhag ||
Sitapatiko Jivana | jab Sadguru kahyo avaj ||130||
Sabal sanghati Shamlo | Sadguruke updesh ||
Aur sanghati Jivana | jaise dholo kesh ||131||
Varsha Parbrahm naamki | sada hot akhand ||
Guru krupathi Jivana | badal bhaye sab sant ||132||

|| Sakhi Bhetki ||
Charan pasaye Jivana | ham gavat gun Gopal ||
Ramnamki mauj hai | so Sadguru pale lad ||133||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Dakshanavant payo Jivana | Janak sutako naho ||
Riddhi siddhi mukti bhakti de | te Sadguru charan pasay ||134||
Antargatki Ramji | sabkun bhari bhari det ||
Hamhi mage Jivana | Sadguru kahyo so het ||135||
Jhabak jhooth kaha kare | jo Sainya dini ot ||
Sadguru vachane Jivana | kabahu na lage chot ||136||
Ram Krishna do Jivana | soi hamare pir ||
Sadguru vachane paiye | Sarayu Yamuna tir ||137||
Antarjami aapno | Sadguru diyo batay ||
Lakshmi charan seva kare | so Gokul charave gay ||138||
Ek mukh keti ek kahun | Shesh na pave par ||
Sadguru samjhayo Jivana | je Ramnaam aadhar ||139||

Hast mastak ave nahi | ghat ghat vyapak Ram ||
Sadguru samjhayo Jivana | je samro Sitaram ||140||
Bhali bhai ab Jivana | Sadguru diya batay ||
Antarjami aapno | raho prem laulay ||141||
Bhali bhai re Jivana | Sadguru bhaye sahay ||
Antarjami yun kahai | bhaj Sitapati Raghuray ||142||
Ham janyo Hari dhunkdo | Vaikunth peli par ||
Vebhi nedo Jivana | jo Sadguru hoy krupal ||143||
Hoti aai Jivana | panth puratan saar ||
So Sadguru sat tattva kahyo | bhaj Janaksuta aadhar ||144||
Kali kichman gad rahi | Jivan dubri gay ||
Aap bale nikse nahin | jo Sadguru na hoy sahay ||145||
Char khan bhamyo eklo | kahi na pamyo thaam ||
Hari bhajvekun Jivana | Sadguru diya e kaam ||146||
Thaam diya hai Jivana | kidhi Sadgurue saar ||
Ram bhaktikun anusaro | utro peli par ||147||

Par utare Jivana | Sadguru pakde banhi ||
Ajamil gunka tari | patthar tare tanhi ||148||
Jamuna tire Jadavo | Sarayu tire Raghuvir ||
Sadguru samjhayo Jivana | dono ek sharir ||149||
Age sanyasi guru kiya | tene adhyatam diya batay ||
Ta chhandke Jivana | samro Raghupati Ray ||150||
Sadguru Das Gopalji | je satya hi diya batay ||
Sant samagam Jivana | je Hari ras piyo aghay ||151||
Jin panth sab Jivana | jahan karm dharmki aash ||
Ajamil gunka tari | te Sadguru shabd vishvas ||152||
Sab jag dhundhyo Jivana | mua na rove koy ||
Shir upar Sadguru khada | je kare so hoy ||153||
Sadguru hamare Jivana | je boli baiyan naar ||
Bhajvekun Sitapati | je khele Nand dvar ||154||

|| Sakhi Bhetki ||
Sadguru hamari vinati | suniyo Jivandas ||
Par triya sun lalchayo | kabahun na mite pyas ||155||
|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Sarasvati shodhi Shahapare | jaiso Dhadharko nir ||
Sadguru vachane Jivana | koi ek pave tir ||156||
Je sajaniya sukhe podhte | so jan gaye Kedar ||
Guru shabd bin Jivana | mile na duji var ||157||
Raghupati Jadupati Jivana | doy hamare Ram ||
Guru krupathi paiye | sant sangat vishram ||158||
|| Sakhi Bhetki ||
Sadguru hamari vinati | tum suniyo sant krupal ||
Ham rank charanki chhany hai | Jivan tum pratipal ||159||
Gunegar Gopaliyo | Sadguru seva nahin ||
Guno bagso Jivana | ham sant charanki chhanhi ||160||

|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Prempaliti Jivana | jare moh ahankar ||
Ramnamki mauj bhai | te Sadguruke upkar ||161||
Man gayo miti aapda | bhavsagar sagar bahu hath pado ||
Jan Jivanki bhai rakhvali | shir upar Sadguru khado ||162||
Vrukhbhansuta Nandlal par | varu tan man pran ||
Guru krupathe Jivana | paiye jug jug dhyan ||163||
Sab sakha Brijnar sun | arogo Jadupatiray ||
Juthan pave Jivana | te Sadguru tane pasay ||164||
Sadguru taruvar bhaye Jivana | pat bhaye sab sikh ||
Ek avat hi ek jat hai | tame kaisa dokh ||165||
Tun tun tun tun hot hai | hun nahi ek var ||
Sadguru antare Jivana | so japat hai Rarankar ||166||
Sadguru Das Gopalji | jine diyo abhepad daan ||
Ved van sab Jivana | kati kiyo maidan ||167||

Na guru bhaya na shish bhaya | man mataka khel ||
Tal kodar pise Jivana | nahi ghens aur tel ||168||
Sabhi kalki dadhman | man mane tab khay ||
Harijan ugre Jivana | jake guru sahay ||169||
Pothi bandhi khinchke | manman bhayo anand ||
Guru seva bin Jivana | rahe galo jyun chand ||170||
Mala tilak banayke | manmen ho rahyo sadh ||
Guru seva bin Jivana | jaiso untko pad ||171||
Mero tero Jivana | prakruti tako naam ||
Jab Sadguru krupa kare | to fite tako thaam ||172||
Vari Harike naam par | diyo manav janm avtar ||
Sadguru par vari Jivana | utare bhav jal par ||173||
Lakhte lakhte sab likha | shastra ved puran ||
Sadguru seva bin Jivana | dub bhandko gan ||174||
Brahma Shesh Mahesh lu | sabhi hadman ghay ||
Sadguru sabad bin Jivana | jyun andho aarsi pay ||175||
Na guruke na pirke | nahi ved Kuran ||
Jug jug bhatke Jivana | jyun hadkayo shvan ||176||
Jahan Sadguruka dava nahi | tahan Jamka dava hoy ||
Ram bharunse Jivana | bharam pado mat koy ||177||
Hari bhaje Hari na paiye | sab aap aapkun dhay ||
Guru samsa bin Jivana | kal jhapete jay ||178||

|| Iti Shri Gurudevka Ang ||1||
|| Iti Shri pratham vishram sampurna ||
sections.translation:
|| Here begins the section on the Guru-Deva (the divine Guru) ||

1. My name is Jivan; I was born in the Kanbi (farmer) lineage. My Lord is Ramji, and my sadguru (true guru) is Das Gopal.

2. Sadguru Das Gopalji, who is an incarnation of the line of Janak. He showed Jivan Raghupati (Ram, lord of the Raghus), who is the adornment of Vrishabhanu's daughter (Radha).

3. Choose a guru with careful thought - one who will show you Ram: Ram of the bank of the Sarayu, of the city and township of Ayodhya.

4. My Lord is Ramji, whose brothers are Bharat and Shatrughna; with Sankarshan (Lakshman) and with Janki (Sita) at his side - Jivan, he is the father of this world.

5. The sadguru made me understand, Jivan, and then the mind became steady. "I found the milk and went round the shrine" [unclear] - so said Das Kabir.

6. What had never been seen and never been heard, the sadguru pointed out. Now why do you lie sleeping, Jivan? Sing a little of the spotless Name.

7. Let go of the world and the Vedas; let go of earth and sky. Abide in the sadguru's word, Jivan, where the light of love and bhakti (devotion) shines.

8. The one and only is great bliss; the second is the sadguru, the supporting vine; the third is Raghupati, Jivan - with the Name, make your sport.

9. All turned out well, Jivan, when the sadguru took hold of my hand. For countless births, without the name of Ram, I had embraced only the thorn tree.

10. The betel-roll of sixty-four leaves - the sadguru revealed it. This is the boon I ask, Jivan: the grace of the saints' feet.

11. What Ramanand spoke, Das Kabir heard; and the same the sadguru has told Jivan: worship Sitapati (Sita's lord), Raghuvir.

12. The essence hidden in the three worlds - the sadguru revealed it. The twenty-eight pits (hells), Jivan, he has freed his servant from.

13. The "ola jhola" [unclear] the sadguru pointed out to Jivan: Raghupati, whom the Vedas kept concealed inside rites and duty (karma and dharma).

14. Father and [unclear: "badhu"] are not to be forsaken - Kanhaiya (Krishna) at Yashoda's neck. The sadguru explained it, Jivan; then what is honour and what is comparison?

15. Opposition to the Veda arose, Jivan, when the sadguru became my helper. The Veda says: worship the formless Niranjan; but we sing of Raghuvar as the bridegroom.

16. Make your birth fruitful, Jivan - repeat the name of Sitapati. The Veda spoke of a form of pure light, but by it not one purpose was accomplished.

17. No one is your own, Jivan - I have looked through my own land and foreign lands. There is only the shelter of Sitapati, or the teaching of the sadguru.

18. What can the poor guru do if the disciple is arrogant and dull? Give milk-pudding to a dog, Jivan - it will not stay in his belly for a moment.

19. He became a devotee of Hari out of mere enthusiasm, and the guru he found was a fool. Like matched with like, Jivan - as a donkey rolls in ashes.

20. Slowly, slowly, Jivan - the way a chameleon moves its feet. Now, leaving my own country, I have taken [unclear: "vea"]; the sadguru said, "Come."

21. Yama (death) was proved false, Jivan, when the sadguru gave his testimony: "This one is your own soul - Raghupati, take him into your keeping."

22. The sadguru's word became the stake of trial, and the saints became the guardians. I will not let it be, Jivan - a Creator without support (a formless God).

|| Sakhis (couplets) of the meeting ||

23. The sadguru is stubborn, Jivan - he plays his own move. Wherever he sees ego (aapa), there he plants his foot.

24. The sadguru stands with steel in hand, sounding the drum and banner of the Name. Ego trembled and shook, and fled wherever it could, Jivan.

|| Sakhis from the holy mouth ||

25. Everyone says "guru, guru", but the body's bondage is not wiped away. The Holy Mouth says: listen, Jivan - the guru is the valiant one of the field (Khetaiya) [unclear].

26. It all comes to a zero, Jivan, if I do service to some other god. The sadguru declared the very truth-essence: Raghupati is the true God.

27. The meaning of the sadguru's teaching is entry into the Name. When the ocean of existence is wiped away, Jivan, we shall come to that land.

28. In the swing of Hari, Jivan, I forgot all other company. The grace of Raghunath came when the sadguru took hold of my hand.

29. Half-formed is the seeker's doctrine where the hope rests on Parbrahm (the impersonal Supreme). The full doctrine is there, Jivan, where there is trust in the sadguru's word.

30. Offer the mind at the guru's feet; the body stays among the family and the five (elements). Brahma and the other gods went astray, Jivan - in that way one is not called a devotee of Hari.

31. Offer body and mind to Ram, and he gives you the abode of Vaikunth. Offer them at the guru's feet, Jivan, and you find rest at the lotus feet.

32. A man without a head - where does Jivandas see one? He who has handed over his head at the guru's feet and stays detached from the world.

33. The eight siddhis and the nine treasures are there, Jivan, where there is trust in the sadguru's word. The dark Lord with his sixteen kalas (full digits of power) is where Hari's own servants are.

|| Sakhis of the meeting ||

34. Sadguru and Jivan surge with joy, like dark clouds massing thick. Drink the nectar that trickles from the unfailing spring, gazing on the youthful divine pair.

|| Sakhis from the holy mouth ||

35. The Veda blocked up the little path, the landing-place of liberation and devotion. By the guru's grace, Jivan, a kick sent it flying.

36. The path opened and I came out into the company of the saints. Cross the ocean of existence, Jivan, by the arm of Sitapati.

37. Striking the mouth of the Vedas and throwing dust in their eyes - by the guru's grace, Jivan, go and take hold of your own root.

38. Remember the sadguru, Jivan, who broke the spell of the Vedas. Above all religion stands the unfathomable writ of the saints.

39. What is written is not erased, Jivan - whatever destiny has been written. The sadguru erased the writing; then I found the One beyond all writing (alekh).

40. The sadguru showed the unseeable (alakh), Jivan - Sitaram. The rites and duties the Veda prescribed, I threw away as useless.

41. Everyone says "Ram, Ram", but the true Name alone is the essence. I obtained the name of the Nameless, Jivan, by the sadguru's kindness.

42. Everyone calls Ram true; no one calls him false. But without the guru's grace, Jivan, the true turns into the false.

43. Who has crossed over by Krishna's grace? By the guru's grace even a thief crosses. Otherwise one wanders age after age, Jivan, like cattle without an owner.

44. In the ocean of existence, Jivan, great distress has come. The sadguru sent this message: "Come quickly, Raghuvir."

45. Cries of victory rose, Jivan, when the sadguru gave his teaching. As I was drowning in the ocean of existence, he seized me and pulled me out by the hair.

46. Trade in diamonds, Jivan, now that the sadguru has become the broker. Testing and testing I have tested it: the name of Ram is the essence of the essence.

47. The sadguru pointed out the chamber of Hari's diamonds. Bathe in the company of the saints, who sing of Raghuvar as the bridegroom.

48. Rajas, tamas, sattva - the world lies within these three qualities. The fourth quality, Jivan, belongs to the sadguru's household.

49. They look like drunkards, intoxicated with the guru's word. Do not be afraid, Jivan - Kamala's lord (Hari) is over your head.

50. This is a game staked on the head; come, if you can play it. There is no coaxing here, Jivan - the sadguru has shown the move.

51. Who is worthy and who unworthy, Jivan - the sadguru points it out. Vibhishan bowed his head low [unclear: "nik shish"], and Raghupati became his help.

52. When the true sadguru is met, he lifts the ego away. The road by which the saints have gone out, Jivan - that road he shows.

53. When the true sadguru is met, trust in the Name is born. By the fire of longing separation (virah), Jivan, karma is destroyed.

54. Let them lie beaten aside now, Jivan - repetition, austerity, pilgrimage, charity. The sadguru's blade swept through and cut the field clear.

55. The crop dried up, Jivan; nothing ripened well. It sprouted, but it was never watered - without the water of the guru's word.

56. Delusion spread out over the proud, and the whole world went under. The devotees of Hari were saved, Jivan, playing the sadguru's move.

57. For Jivan the sadguru is the dark Lord himself; for Das Kabirji he is Ram. Among Ramanand's disciples, Kabir found Ram, the abode of bliss.

58. In the Ramanandi sampraday (tradition), Jivandas soared. He gave up caste, rites and observances, and set his hope on Ram's feet.

59. He flew and leapt, Jivan, clear over repetition, austerity, pilgrimage and charity. The path of the Veda was left behind, and he went and found the Name of Hari.

60. He flew and leapt, Jivan - he made one single bound. In the company of the saints he found him: the king of Ayodhya.

61. Uda was of Hanuman's kind: he made a single leap and seized the fruit that is Hari, Jivana - and that was the grace of the sadguru (true guru).

62. He gave up all pilgrimage and fasting - Uda is his name. He set aside caste-custom and ritual works, Jivana, and remembers only Sitaram.

63. Uda's religion rose up plain and open: no dealings with any other god. Remembrance of Sitaram, and along with it the company of the saints, without a shadow of doubt.

64. Uda and the monkey, Jivana, are both of one species. But Uda remembered Raghupati, while the monkey keeps company with ghosts.

65. Everyone says "Uda, Uda" - now hear Uda's own sakhi (couplet, testimony): he clings to no other god, Jivana; Raghupati has kept him as his own.

66. What Shesha chants with his thousand mouths, that Hanuman perceived ["sala" in the original is unclear]. The sadguru said, Jivana, that this is the meditation of Gauri's lord (Shiva).

67. I do not serve the shaligram stone, nor have I any business with images. The sadguru made me understand, Jivana, that it is the Name of Sitapati (Sita's lord, Ram).

68. Make such a one your guru, Jivana, as has neither form nor outline. If he tells of any other than Sitapati, then let a spike be driven through that mouth.

69. The sadguru pointed out the book of the Name of Parbrahm - the primal, imperishable one. Jivana, fix your mind on "Ra" and on "Ma" (the syllables of Ram).

70. Going out to beg alms, Jivana, all the saints became my givers; but only by the sadguru's word is Kamala's lord (Hari, Lakshmi's husband) obtained.

71. Without Hari's name the whole world is seen to live in fear of death. Hari's devotees are carried across, Jivana - and that is the sadguru's grace.

72. All the ages have flowed past, Jivana, and we were there within them. What do I know of what has become of me - the sadguru caught me by the arm.

73. Everyone calls him the treasury of compassion; that conviction is not in me. Without the guru's grace, Jivana, no one has reached the far shore.

74. In the southern quarter the sun burns; in the north is the moon's temper. All four directions are ours, Jivana - the sadguru has shown us the move.

75. Satsang (the company of saints), Jivana, is not known even to Shankar and Shesha; the scriptures can only say "not this, not this" (neti neti). That is the teaching the sadguru gave.

76. Partisanship fell away and went off to both sides; what remained was the essence - the company of saints. By the sadguru's word, Jivana, I crossed to the far shore.

77. Drinking water without thirst, eating kheer (milk pudding) without hunger - such is he who forsakes the guru's word and worships Hari: he is a man without a master, Jivana.

78. Some say Hari is in the empty sky; some say Hari is within every vessel (every heart). The sadguru showed him to me, Jivana, in the shade of the holy Bansivat (the banyan of the flute, at Vrindavan).

79. Our beloved, Jivana, the sadguru pointed out to us: a peacock-crown on his head, the flute at his mouth, grazing the cows in Vrindavan.

|| Sakhi of the meeting ||

80. Sadguru Jivan is Shyam himself; his servant Kabirji is Ram. Such is the whole difference that has fallen between them - and no one can discern it.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

81. By a difference of two letters, Ram and Kabir are one. He understands this, Jivana, to whom the sadguru has given discernment.

82. Union and liberation came about, Jivana, when the sadguru gave his teaching: heaven, hell and Vaikunth were lifted away as lightly as one plucks out a hair.

83. Shukji recited the twelve cantos, yet the inner secret of even one was not grasped. When Janak of Videha made himself a guru, Jivana, then he attained the religion of the soul.

84. A lamp has been given, Jivana, wherever there is faith in the sadguru's word; and there is darkness for the whole world wherever the hope rests on rites and merit.

85. To say "Sain" (Lord) is easy, but in the saying there is much to ponder. All of this becomes easy, Jivana, when the sadguru turns gracious.

86. Everyone is pleased with his own station. But the station of the sadguru, Jivana, only a rare one recognizes.

87. All servitude is rendered after one's own mind; no one goes by the guru's mind. Those who go by the guru's mind, Jivana, are in the shade of Hari's lotus feet.

88. The manifest expanse, Jivana, the sadguru pointed out: bathe in the company of the saints and sing of Raghuvar the bridegroom.

89. To cross over this world, Jivana, the name of Ram is the unfailing arrow. Shankar recited it to his consort, and the sadguru declared it the authority.

90. This has become the last birth, Jivana, since the sadguru gave his teaching: in the company of the saints I met the king of Ayodhya (Ram).

|| Sakhi of the meeting ||

91. I dwell in my home at Chanderi; Jivan came and manifested there, and gave me the Name of Sitapati Raghunath.

92. From the moment Jivan manifested, from that moment came deliverance. Gopal was granted protection; now Yamraj (the lord of death) [unclear].

93. Our village is Sahapar, where all the saints have their abode of joy. Our sadguru, Jivana, is Shyam in all his sixteen digits.

94. The three takiyas (saints' resting-seats) stand outside, where Sitapati's saints are. There Gopal met the sadguru, and then obtained the endless Name.

95. He sings and makes us sing, Jivana; he speaks and makes us hear. As a bird gives grain to its young, such is the sadguru, our father.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

96. Steel takes no temper for a price, Jivana, though ten million blacksmiths gather. Without love, bhakti (devotion) does not arise, even were the Creator himself to be met.

|| Sakhi of the meeting ||

97. On taking a sadguru, Jivana, fear is left behind. He cuts the bondage of worldly karma, and sings nothing but the glory of Hari.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

98. Hari gives and we receive; in that there is no one's obligation. For the soul there is only this one thing, Jivana - that the sadguru became its help.

99. Kabirji is the sadguru of all; let no one make him a private possession. As for the rest of the world, Jivana, the sadguru is the very woman of one's own house [the sense of "joi" here is uncertain].

100. Where there is no guru, no pir, Jivana, everyone still performs devotion; but churn water however lovingly - how shall butter come of it?

101. What cannot be digested is not digested, Jivana - like kheer given to a dog: it comes spraying back out of the nose, in the man who has no guru, no pir.

|| Sakhi of the meeting ||

102. He who takes the sadguru's arrow and aims it at his own ego - if he does [navtu: unclear], Jivana, he escapes the four wombs of birth.

103. Kill the chief, my Jivana, and the whole army runs away. What can those dwelling inside do then? The ego has been uprooted.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

104. So long as a single self-willed act remains, you come into being again and it does not end. Where the ego stands upright, Jivana, there the sadguru is no help.

105. When ego is erased, calamity is erased and every sickness goes. Become gurumukh (turned toward the guru), Jivana, and sing the glory of the spotless Name.

106. By his karma he was born a dog, yet the Indweller is one and the same; not even in a dream did he know, Jivana, the discernment the sadguru gives.

107. The Name is the wish-fulfilling gem, Jivana; the saints have pointed it out. What you keep for yourself will not remain, if the sadguru is not your help.

108. Give up both heaven and hell, and keep no hope even of Vaikunth. Repeat the name of Ram, Jivana, where there is faith in the sadguru's word.

|| Sakhi of the meeting ||

109. The sadguru has sent his message far and wide: come, all you raw young ones. The Name is the wish-fulfilling gem, Jivana - take of it whatever you please.

110. What can poor Sarasvati do, where the guru's word is not the authority? Without Sitapati, Jivana, one wanders through the four wombs of birth.

111. All speech is adulterous where the guru's word is not the authority. The speech that comes from the guru's mouth, Jivana, is welfare upon welfare.

112. That speech drew near, Jivana, within the company of the saints. Mine is the shelter of Sitapati, or else the shade of Girdhari.

113. What did you accomplish by expounding in pride, Jivana, when the guru's word is not your authority? He who recognizes the guru's word - brother, he is authority upon authority.

114. What did you achieve by singing in pride? The guru's word alone is the authority. Having [gauthayke: unclear] his own soul, he wanders through the four wombs of birth.

115. Reckon the sea to stand a hundred yojans higher than the earth: even so its waters do not rush in and overwhelm it, Jivana. Make your sport in the Name.

116. Gopal stays sunk deep within the sadguru's word. In the company of the saints is Shyam, where there is neither Yama's servant nor death.

117. Madan (the god of love) awoke the proud lady by sounding the flute before her; just so, Jivana, the sadguru took us who were asleep and woke us.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth (the master's own couplets) ||

118. Both have been lost, O Jivan - yoga and the ascetic's "adesh" (the renouncer's greeting and calling). He abandoned the true dharma outright and never grasped the guru's teaching.

119. He revives the dead and the dying, as though coming and sprinkling nectar on them. Such are the virtues of Hari, O Jivan - the Sadguru (true master) became my helper.

120. He pervades every vessel, O Jivan, yet the Inner-Knower is one alone. I am a sacrifice to that servant in whom there is discernment of the Sadguru's word.

121. The Sadguru made Jivan understand the matter, both hidden and manifest: one single form dwells in every heart - the one Sitapati Raghunath (Ram, husband of Sita).

122. Pervading every heart, O Jivan, is the form of Sitapati. The guru's grace comes to that servant in whose heart the Name has taken form.

123. The lovely woman thirsting for love stands clinging to the bank. Without the guru's grace, O Jivan, she sees fire in the very water.

124. With no cowherd, O Jivan, the cattle all scatter and stray. The Sadguru stands with staff in hand and brings them back onto his own track.

125. All ritual works and religious duty came to a standstill; even the knowledge of Brahman came to a halt. By the guru's grace, O Jivan, now remember Sitaram.

126. Karma was felled with an axe here in the world, O Jivandas. The Sadguru explained what the servant Kabir had said.

127. My evening meal is milk - that is the Sadguru's majesty; Vedic religion is all mere buttermilk. A great sin had clung to me.

128. Kinsmen and relations were all swept away, O Jivan; in the Sadguru's word lies the true garland. The Name is a wish-fulfilling gem that carries one across the water of worldly existence.

129. The sense of "my own" keeps catching and clinging to the one who remembers Sitaram. By the guru's grace, O Jivan, its foothold is wiped away.

130. The mother's company was parted, the father departed - and that was great good fortune, when the Sadguru spoke aloud the name of Sitapati, O Jivan.

131. The strong companion is Shamlo (Shyam, the dark Lord), given through the Sadguru's teaching. Every other companion, O Jivan, is like a hair gone white.

132. The rain of Parbrahm's Name falls always, unbroken. By the guru's grace, O Jivan, all the saints have become its clouds.

|| Sakhi of offering (the disciple's answering couplet) ||

133. By the grace of your feet, O Jivan, we sing the praises of Gopal. There is the delight of Ram's Name, and the Sadguru fondles us with a parent's affection.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

134. As my offering-gift I received, O Jivan, the husband of Janak's daughter (Ram). He grants prosperity, attainment, liberation and bhakti (devotion) - all by the grace of the Sadguru's feet.

135. Ramji, who knows what is within, fills and gives to everyone. We too ask, O Jivan, only for that love of which the Sadguru spoke.

136. What can a flash of falsehood do, when the Lord himself has given shelter? By the Sadguru's word, O Jivan, no blow ever lands.

137. Ram and Krishna, the two, O Jivan - they alone are our guide. By the Sadguru's word one reaches the banks of the Sarayu and the Yamuna.

138. The Sadguru pointed out to me my own Inner-Knower. He whose feet Lakshmi serves is the very one who grazes the cows in Gokul.

139. With one mouth, how much can one tell? Even Shesh (the thousand-hooded serpent) finds no end to it. The Sadguru made Jivan understand: the Name of Ram is the support.

140. No hand or head of his comes into view - Ram pervades every heart. The Sadguru made Jivan understand: remember Sitaram.

141. It has turned out well now, O Jivan - the Sadguru has shown the way. He is our own Inner-Knower; stay absorbed in love of him.

142. It has turned out well, O Jivan - the Sadguru became my help. The Inner-Knower says this: worship Sitapati Raghuray.

143. I had thought Hari to be near, and Vaikunth to be on the far shore. That too is close at hand, O Jivan, if the Sadguru be gracious.

144. It has come down from of old, O Jivan - the ancient path is the essence. The Sadguru declared that true principle: worship him who is the support of Janak's daughter.

145. The lean cow is sunk fast in the mire of the Kali age, O Jivan. By her own strength she cannot get out, if the Sadguru does not come to her aid.

146. I wandered alone through the four kinds of birth and nowhere found a resting place. To worship Hari, O Jivan - that is the task the Sadguru gave me.

147. He has given me a resting place, O Jivan; the Sadguru did what was needed. Follow devotion to Ram and cross over to the far shore.

148. The Sadguru grasps the arm and carries one across, O Jivan. Ajamil and the courtesan were ferried over; there even stones were made to float.

149. On the bank of the Yamuna, the Yadava (Krishna); on the bank of the Sarayu, Raghuvir (Ram). The Sadguru made Jivan understand: the two are one single body.

150. Earlier I took a sannyasi for my guru, and he expounded the doctrine of the inner self. Leaving that aside, O Jivan, remember Raghupati Ray.

151. The Sadguru Das Gopalji showed me the very truth. In satsang (holy company), O Jivan, drink the nectar of Hari till you are filled.

152. All those sects, O Jivan, where the hope rests on ritual works and duty - yet Ajamil and the courtesan were carried across, and that by faith in the Sadguru's word.

153. I searched the whole world, O Jivan: when a man dies, no one really weeps for him. The Sadguru stands over my head; whatever he does, that comes to pass.

154. Our Sadguru, O Jivan - [unclear: "je boli baiyan naar"]. Worship Sitapati, who plays at Nand's door.

|| Sakhi of offering ||

155. Sadguru, hear our petition - listen, Jivandas: whoever craves another man's wife, his thirst is never quenched.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

156. I searched for the Saraswati at Shahapar - she is like the water of the Dhadhar stream. By the Sadguru's word, O Jivan, some rare one reaches the shore.

157. Those dear companions who used to sleep at ease - those people have gone to Kedar (departed from this life). Without the guru's word, O Jivan, one does not meet them a second time.

158. Raghupati and Jadupati, O Jivan - both of them are our Ram. By the guru's grace one finds rest in the company of saints.

|| Sakhi of offering ||

159. Sadguru, hear our petition, O gracious saint. We are poor folk living in the shade of your feet; Jivan, you are our sustainer.

160. Gopal is an offender - he has not served the Sadguru. Pardon the offence, O Jivan; we take the shade of the saints' feet.

|| Sakhi from the holy mouth ||

161. The fuse of love, O Jivan, burns up delusion and egotism. The delight of Ram's Name has come - and that is the Sadguru's kindness.

162. Pride departed and calamity ceased; in the ocean of worldly existence much stubborn hardship fell to my lot [the line repeats "sagar" - ocean - in the source]. The servant Jivan was kept safe: the Sadguru stands over his head.

163. Upon Vrishabhanu's daughter (Radha) and Nandlal (Krishna) I offer up body, mind and life-breath. By the guru's grace, O Jivan, one gains their contemplation age after age.

164. With all his companions and the women of Braj, Jadupati Ray takes his meal. To receive his leavings, O Jivan, comes by the Sadguru's grace.

165. The Sadguru has become the tree, O Jivan, and all the disciples its leaves. One is coming even as another goes - what fault is there in that?

166. "You, you, you, you" - so it keeps saying; not once "I". Within the Sadguru, O Jivan, that one is repeating the Rarankar (the resounding primal sound of "Ra", the Name of Ram).

167. The Sadguru Das Gopalji gave the gift of the fearless, undivided state. The whole forest of the Vedas, O Jivan, he cut down and turned into open ground.

168. He became neither a guru nor a disciple - it was all a game of his own mind's opinion. He grinds sesame and kodra millet together, O Jivan, and gets neither porridge nor oil.

169. Everyone is in the jaws of Death; whenever it pleases him, he eats. Only the devotee of Hari escapes, O Jivan - the one whose guru is his help.

170. He ties up his book-bundle tight and feels delight in his mind. But without service of the guru, O Jivan, he wastes away like the waning moon.

171. Putting on rosary and forehead-mark, he has become a holy man in his own mind. Without service of the guru, O Jivan, it is like a camel's wind.

172. "Mine" and "yours", O Jivan - prakriti (primal nature) is its name. When the Sadguru shows grace, its very foothold is wiped away.

173. I am a sacrifice to the Name of Hari, which granted this human birth. I am a sacrifice to the Sadguru, O Jivan, who ferries one across the water of existence.

174. Writing and writing they wrote it all - shastras, Vedas, Puranas. Without service of the Sadguru, O Jivan, it sinks; it is a mere buffoon's song.

175. Brahma, Shesh and Mahesh too - all of them are struck down within their limits. Without the Sadguru's word, O Jivan, it is like a blind man getting a mirror.

176. He belongs neither to a guru nor to a pir (a Muslim spiritual master); he has neither the Vedas nor the Quran. Age after age he wanders, O Jivan, like a mad dog.

177. Where the Sadguru has no claim, there Death has his claim. Merely trusting to the word "Ram", O Jivan, let no one fall into delusion.

178. By repeating "Hari" one does not obtain Hari; everyone is running after his own self. Without the guru's own hint, O Jivan, one is snatched away by Death.

|| Here ends the Section on the Divine Guru ||1||
|| Here ends the First Vishram (resting-chapter), complete ||

Ram pita sab jivka | Harijan jake nahi ||

sant darshankun Jivana | Kashi karvat le aap ||

Sain hamara Ramji | je Dasharath sut Raghuvir ||
sab santan mali Jivana | kiyo hamare shir ||17||
sab santanman Jivana | karigar Kabir ||

nirbhay khaat Kabirki | sab santan lini baant ||

januni aisa putra janamiye | jaisa das Kabir ||
bhakt khambh Govind kahai | dagan bandhave dhir ||20||
jag julahe jitiya | sabahanka shir ||
naam batai Jivana | jakun jaisi dhir ||21||
Ram swarupi naam hai | naam swarupi sant ||
kali kalman Jivana | bhajvekun do meet ||22||
ja thorse jiv upno | ralmal tahan samaay ||

ke sove ke baith rahai | Sitapatiki chhahi ||24||
sant samagam Jivana | aapa de chhodaay ||

kaha jogi kaha sevda | kaha pandit kaha joshi ||
sant sangat bin Jivana | Ram bhakti na hosi ||26||
do bal hamare Jivana | bhaktaraj randhir ||
Raghuvar to raksha kare | sant bandhave dhir ||27||
je bhav kar arpe Jivana | sant mukh hokar paau ||
kotik jagan koi kare | main seet na chakhan jaau ||28||
kalike bhagat par Jivana | varun tan man pran ||
van dekhe mokun bhaje | kar sant swaroop praman ||29||
kotik Vaikunth upare | Shri Vrindavan sukhdham ||
tathe niki Jivana | sant sangat vishram ||30||
aag jalo Vaikunthman | jahan sant samagam nahi ||
tathe niki Jivana | Shri Bansivatki chhahi ||31||
aag jalo Vaikunthmen | jahan sant samagam nahi ||
bhagat viyoge dukhiyo bhayo | uhan jan to aave nahi ||32||
Gokulmen vase vasu | surte kaaj saraau ||
apni soje Jivana | Braj taji anat na jaau ||33||
Braj taj anat na jaau | eh hamari tek ||
bhutal bhaar utarva | dharun roop anek ||34||
apni soje Jivana | main harun Kansko pran ||
Gokul Mathura Dwarka | karun bhagatanki aan ||35||
main Gokulman vaas vasu | kabhu Shesh sukhasan gam ||

tahan Ayodhya jahan Raghupati | Kanhad tahan Gokul gam ||
saptapuri tahan Jivana | jahan sant sangat Hari naam ||37||
atanki murat Jivana | seve ko ek sant ||
tanki puthe tarafde | so van kripa Bhagwant ||38||
deval dekhyo Jivana | atanki murat mahi ||
Radharavan Sitapati | Das Kabirki chhahi ||39||
dal deval kar Jivana | murat Parbrahm naam ||
kalpavriksh Kabirji | aatam tahan vishram ||40||
dal dariyav kar devla | murat Parbrahm naam ||
kalpavriksh Kabirji | Jivan jan vishram ||41||
paaye lagun Harike jan | soi hamare dev ||
naak liti karun Jivana | jo duji karun sev ||42||
sab santan mali Jivana | kiyo ek vichar ||
Sitapati bin or kahe | take modhe chhaar ||43||
alarasi Jivana | sant dware jaay ||
kabahu sanmukh dekh hai | tab kripa kare Raghuray ||44||
Prahlad raksha kari Jivana | tab apne vichar ||

ab aisi karun Jivana | sant vachan praman ||

sant sangat jahan Jivana | tahan Sitapatiko naam ||47||
sanso mit gayo sajna | je samare Sitaram ||
prem ras pive Jivana | sant jan tako naam ||48||

sant bhagatki kaha kahun | charan kamal nij dham ||53||
sathi bhulyo Jivana | samarya nahi Raghupati ray ||
sant samagam chhandke | chalyo so apne bhaay ||54||
aap swarath Jivana | nari kino rosh ||

janam janam e Jivana | magun eh pasav ||
sant samagam prem ras | aur na dujo bhav ||56||
kahna tha so kah liya | ab kaha kahun samjhaay ||
sant seva karo Jivana | je Raghupati hoy sahay ||57||
duniya sab naguri bhai | kare ankorki aash ||

virhini bilakhat fire | samare Sita Ram ||
sant sangat bin Jivana | janam gayo bekaam ||59||

sant trapta nahi Jivana | Shamlo kabahu na aghaay ||60||

prem ankush gopi bhai | tode nigam kapaat ||62||
vaat ughadi nisro | sant samagam mahi ||
bhavsagar tar Jivana | Sitapatiki banhi ||63||
uthat baithat Jivana | samro Sita Ram ||

sir Sanakadik Jivana | chhodo Vaikunth mahi ||

|| Sakhi Bhetki ||

kaam ratni kamni | naame kare prakash ||
sant samagam santro | jahan baithe Jivandas ||66||
sant na aaye Jivana | ham to dekhat baat ||
Sadgurke parvar bin | kyon kar paiye ghaat ||67||
kali manav ne Bharat khand | Sadguru Jivan valivali ||
naam rupe je jan malya | sant shiromani mandali ||68||

|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||

sant samagam Jivana | jahan Sitapatiko naam ||
akhe unmani prem ras | jahan Vrindavan sukh dham ||69||
e pad hamare Jivana | Sitapatiko naam ||
guru seva jan bandagi | sant sangat vishram ||70||
kuldevi hamare Janaki | pitrudev Raghuvir ||
sant sangat kar Jivana | paap na rahai lagir ||71||
dipak pragatyo Jivana | jab darshan payo sant ||
bhanu ugyo timir gayo | kate karm anant ||72||
adha mata kaun kamka | je pave Vaikunthko dham ||
tathe jagat bhali Jivana | kabahu sant sangat vishram ||73||
je ang parsya santkun | so ang bhaya sanath ||
aur kalhe Jivana | hamahi rahe anath ||74||

shun shun sabko kahe | shun na chinhe koy ||

|| Iti Shri Santko Ang Sampurna ||2||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter on Saints, the second.

1. The sakhi (couplet) is full of savour, Jivan; within it are both Form and Name. Bathe in the company of saints — that is the abode of the Ocean's daughter (Lakshmi).
2. Having found satsang (holy company), Jivan, let us sing His qualities and His songs. Sharing even gruel and dry bread there, one receives the love of the Supreme Lord.
3. Having found satsang, Jivan, drink the unmixed essence of love — that very nectar the cowherd women drank in the bowers of Shri Vrindavan.
4. Raghupati (Rama) gives the fruit of liberation, but the nectar of love lies with Hari's devotees. Knowing this, Jivan, I have made my dwelling in the company of saints.
5. At the saint's door, Jivan, everyone is honoured. To worship Raghupati age after age — that is japa (repetition of the Name), austerity, pilgrimage and almsgiving.
6. Japa, austerity, pilgrimage, Jivan, worship with leaf and with love — apart from holy company and the singing of Hari's praise there is no other observance.
7. For the sight of a saint, Jivan, even Vaikunth (the Lord's heaven) longs. And what standing has poor Vaikunth, when Kamalakanta (Vishnu, Lakshmi's lord) Himself desires that sight?
8. Taking the water that has bathed Vishnu's feet, untimely death is averted. Take the charanamrit of the saints (the water from their feet), Jivan, and one attains the undying supreme state.
9. He who takes up poverty of spirit and lays down pride, and does service to the saints — for the sight of such a one, Jivan, gods, sages and celestials long.
10. All perform bhakti (devotion) to Rama — Brahma, Shankar, Shesha. Yet without the company of saints, Jivan, the country of Hari is hard to reach.
11. By worshipping Hari, Hari is obtained: this is the substance of all sayings. But he who forsakes the saints and worships Hari, Jivan, will have to bear many a kick.
12. Rama is the father of every living creature, but he who has no devotee of Hari with him — such a one, left outside the devotees' fold, Jivan, is dragged off by Yama (death).
13. One may touch Hari in all his sixteen kalas (full aspects) and yet not touch His devotee. [Says the Lord:] "I shall give the fruit of liberation, Jivan, but the fruit of bhakti is not mine to give."
14. For the sight of a saint, Jivan — instead men take the saw at Kashi (the old rite of self-severance there for release). The Vedas called it a field of liberation; [says Kashi:] a great sin has been fastened upon me.
15. "Some devotee of Hari will come among us and cut away our karma." But he who nurses a craving for us, Jivan — he is no devotee of Hari.
16. He who is free of craving, Jivan — his name is devotee of Hari: one who lets go of heaven, hell and Vaikunth alike and remembers Sitaram.
17. Our master is Ramji, Raghuvir the son of Dasharath. All the saints together, Jivan, have set Him upon our head.
18. Among all the saints, Jivan, Kabir is the craftsman. He shaped so lovely a vessel that Raghuvir Himself was won over.
19. Kabir's fearless cot — all the saints have shared it out among themselves. But nothing of it comes, Jivan, to him whose mind holds a twist.
20. O mother, bear such a son as Kabir the servant of God — Govind calls him the pillar of the devotees, who steadies those who falter.
21. The weaver conquered the world and stood above them all. He shared out the Name, Jivan, to each according to his steadfastness.
22. The Name has the very form of Rama, and the saint has the very form of the Name. In the Kali age, Jivan, these two are the friends by whom to worship.
23. From whatever place the soul arose, let it mingle and merge back there. Without the Name and the Form, Jivan, the world is cheated in the swindler's game.
24. Make your birth fruitful, Jivan, within the company of saints — whether you sleep or sit, stay in the shade of Sitapati (Sita's lord, Rama).
25. The company of saints, Jivan, makes a man let go of his own ego. Brahma and the other gods were deluded, walking only the road of the Vedas.
26. What of the yogi, what of the mendicant, what of the pandit, what of the astrologer? Without holy company, Jivan, devotion to Rama will not come about.
27. Two are our strengths, Jivan — [the Lord] and the king of devotees, unshaken in the fray. Raghuvar gives protection, and the saint fortifies our courage.
28. Whatever is offered with true feeling, Jivan, I receive it through the mouth of a saint. Though a man perform ten million sacrifices, I do not go even to taste the leavings.
29. For the devotee of the Kali age, Jivan, I give away body, mind and life-breath: without ever seeing Me he worships Me, taking the saint's form as his proof.
30. Above ten million Vaikunths stands Shri Vrindavan, the abode of bliss; and finer than that, Jivan, is rest in the company of saints.
31. Let fire burn in that Vaikunth where there is no company of saints. Finer than it, Jivan, is the shade of Shri Bansivat (the flute-tree of Vrindavan).
32. Let fire burn in that Vaikunth where there is no company of saints. [Even the Lord] grew sorrowful, parted from His devotees — for there no devotee ever comes.
33. [Says the Lord:] I dwell in Gokul as my home, and through remembrance I accomplish my people's tasks. This is my own choosing, Jivan: leaving Braj I go nowhere else.
34. "Leaving Braj I go nowhere else" — this is my fixed vow. To lift the burden of the earth I take on many forms.
35. Of my own choosing, Jivan, I take the life of Kansa. In Gokul, Mathura and Dwarka I make good my devotees' pledge.
36. I dwell in Gokul; sometimes on the easy couch of Shesha; sometimes in Vaikunth, Jivan; sometimes in the city of Ayodhya.
37. Where Raghupati is, there is Ayodhya; where Kanha (Krishna) is, there is the village of Gokul. And there stand all the seven holy cities, Jivan, where there is holy company and the Name of Hari.
38. The unchiselled image, Jivan — only some rare saint serves it. He who flounders after the chisel is without the Lord's grace.
39. I have seen the temple, Jivan, within that unchiselled image: Radha's lord and Sita's lord, in the shade of Kabir the servant.
40. Make of the depths a temple, Jivan, and let the image be the Name of Parbrahm (the Supreme). Kabirji is the wish-granting tree; there the soul finds its rest.
41. Make the temple as wide as the ocean, and let the image be the Name of Parbrahm. Kabirji is the wish-granting tree — there, Jivan, the devotee finds his rest.
42. I fall at the feet of Hari's devotees; they alone are my deity. Let my nose be rubbed in the dust, Jivan, if I serve any other.
43. All the saints together, Jivan, came to one conclusion: whoever names another than Sitapati — ashes upon his mouth.
44. [unclear], Jivan — go to the saint's door. One day He will look upon you face to face; then Raghuray will show His grace.
45. He protected Prahlad, Jivan, then by His own resolve. Now the saints teach thus: get across to the far bank before the water rises.
46. Now I shall do this, Jivan: hold the saint's word as my authority. In Gokul, Mathura and Dwarka I make good the devotees' pledge.
47. The wish-granting jewel and the wish-granting tree are both in one place: where there is the company of saints, Jivan, there is the Name of Sitapati.
48. Doubt is wiped away, my friend, for the one who remembers Sitaram. He who drinks the nectar of love, Jivan — his name is holy man.
49. For one, the service of the saints; for another, the work of the household. The labour is one and the same, Jivan, but the ease and rest they give are different.
50. The Word draws near, Jivan, within the company of saints. Mine is the refuge of Sitapati, or the shade of Giridhari.
51. Our master is Ramji, and the Word is His servant. Wherever there is the company of saints, Jivan, there it shines out for ever.
52. A shout of victory went up, Jivan, when he came among the saints. Give up every other god and stay in the shade of Sitapati.
53. For Hari's devotees, Jivan, the four kinds of liberation are only a resting-place. And what shall I say of the saint-devotee? His own dwelling is the Lord's lotus feet.
54. The companion went astray, Jivan; he did not remember King Raghupati. Forsaking the company of saints, he walked off after his own liking.
55. Out of self-interest, Jivan, the wife grew angry; so he fell away from holy company — and on whom is the blame to be laid?
56. Birth after birth, Jivan, I ask this one favour: the company of saints and the nectar of love, and no other longing.
57. What was to be said I have said; what more shall I explain? Serve the saints, Jivan, so that Raghupati may be your help.
58. The whole world has become guru-less; it goes on hoping for gifts. The gift is complete, Jivan, when one has come near the saints.
59. The parted lover wanders lamenting, remembering Sitaram. Without the company of saints, Jivan, the birth has gone to waste.

60. Supach and Krishna, the two of them; the Pandavas going to the Himalaya. The saints are never sated, Jivan, and the dark Lord is never filled.
61. The path of the Vedas is hard, and that suffering cannot be borne. The company of saints, Jivan, sets one free of it in a moment.
62. Hari is like an elephant, Jivan, and all the saints have become his mahouts. The gopis became the goad of love, and they break open the doors of the Vedas.
63. The road lies open — go out into the company of saints. Cross the ocean of worldly existence, Jivan, by the arm of Sitapati.
64. Rising and sitting, Jivan, remember Sitaram. Bathe in the company of saints; this is no time for sleep.
65. With Sanaka and his brothers at their head, Jivan, give up even a place in Vaikunth. If the company of saints does not come even in a dream, how is the supreme state to be attained?

Sakhis of the Meeting

66. A woman lost in desire is made luminous by the Name. Blessed is the company of saints, Jivan, where Jivandas takes his seat.
67. The saints have not come, Jivan; we go on watching the road. Without the household of the Sadguru (true teacher), how is the landing-place to be reached?
68. In the Kali age, in human birth, in the land of Bharat — Sadguru Jivan, again and again. Those souls who have met in Name and Form form a company crowned by saints.

Sakhis from the Lord's Own Mouth

69. The company of saints, Jivan, is wherever the Name of Sitapati is. There is unbroken unmani (the mind's absorbed stillness) and the nectar of love; there is Vrindavan, the abode of bliss.
70. This is our station, Jivan: the Name of Sitapati, service of the guru, reverence for His devotees, and rest in the company of saints.
71. Janaki (Sita) is our family goddess, Raghuvir our ancestral deity. Keep the company of saints, Jivan, and not a trace of sin remains.
72. A lamp was kindled, Jivan, when I received the darshan (sight) of a saint. The sun rose, the darkness went, and endless karma was cut away.
73. Of what use are half-held opinions, even if they win the abode of Vaikunth? Better than that is this world, Jivan, where now and then there is rest in the company of saints.
74. The limb that has touched a saint — that limb has found its master. The rest cry out, Jivan: we are left masterless still.
75. The lovely One did not come to dwell in the breast, and "Ram" never came out of the mouth. Without the company of saints, Jivan, the birth has gone to waste.
76. The natural Void is greater than all, where delusion and ego fall away. Beyond it lies the state of Hari, Jivan, which has neither this shore nor the farther shore.
77. Everyone says "Void, Void", but no one recognizes the Void. He who lets go of his own self and worships Hari — he is what is called the Void.
78. He who enters the natural Void — no one can keep him in a household. Worship the state of nirvana, Jivan, and one does not come round into rebirth again.
79. Everyone says "Void, Void", but no one recognizes the Void. Kanha in Yashoda's lap — that is what is called the Void.
80. The sphere of the Void is Shri Vrindavan, where the unbroken, imperishable light shines. To fulfil His devotees' longing, Jivan, He took up His dwelling in the Yadu clan.
81. Though stones and rocks are flung at it, the wish-granting tree gives fruit in return. Such are the devotees of Hari, Jivan — they give even to the one who runs away from them.

Here the Chapter on Saints, the second, is complete.
