Kahuke man Hari base | kahuke Shiv Hanuman ||
hamare man Jivana | Das Kabir nij nam ||100||
Manu payo paiso | Sitapatiko nam ||
kharchat hi khute nahi | Jivan jug bekam ||101||
Dharanidhar adhar rahyo | Balidvare adhin ||
Indre kaha diyo Jivana | Bali kaha liyo chhin ||102||
Dharanidhar adhar rahyo | Bali dvare adhin ||
sarvas arpyo Jivana | Hari bhaye lolin ||103||
So gali Shishupal dai | chakra katachyo tab shish ||
tej samano apmen | so jan Jivanke Ish ||104||
Hoti ai Jivana | so hosi nirdhar ||
Dhruv Prahlade je bhajyo | so moko pran adhar ||105||
Kali mardyo Kahanve | Indra utaryun man ||
Ravan dash shir chhede Jivana | soi hamare Ram ||106||
Kab Raghupati kab Yadupati | kab Shesh sukhasan dham ||
ek rup sab Jivana | pan jude jude nam ||107||
So sain hamara Ramji | je nathyo Kalinag ||
ta charansun Jivana | sada rahun so bhag ||108||
Dekh tamaso Jivana | bale kiyo kam ||
badhik kaha sukrit kiyo | kaha bal chalyo haram ||109||
Ajamil apradhi ek | gunka kiyo ghar vas ||
aisi bohot ki Jivana | pan Ram charanki ash ||110||
Ajamil gunka tari | so Jivan hamare Ram ||
charane Ahalya odhari | je sagarsutako dham ||111||
Sakh shabd tum det ho | dhiraj nahi man manhi ||
itni binati Jivana | tum suniyo hirde manhi ||112||
Anjanisutke Ish par | jan Jivan bali jay ||
vat ghat raksha karo | aise Raghupati ray ||113||
So sain hamare Jivana | Raghukul Yadukul vir ||
Saraju tire khelke | ayo Kalindi tir ||114||
Mule mithun mahelvane | kopyo bhekh anant ||
tun jin par darpe Jivana | shir par Kamalakanth ||115||
Man gayo jab male Jivana | Hariko nam rude dharo ||
apo tharhar kampiyo | tab ravisut to rito padachyo ||116||
Garud chhandi main Jivana | dhayo gajki vahar ||
ab shankh chakra Baldev sun | Garud vahan sant dvar ||117||
Harijan upar Jivana | mero jiv karun kurban ||
murakh man samjhe nahi | ganat vahalanki han ||118||
Samran Sitaramko | je kije so labh ||
bahuri na paiye Jivana | manav janamko dav ||119||
Main shankh chakra dharyo Jivana | so apne janke kaj ||
e birad kaise chhand hun | yun kahat hai Brijraj ||120||
Jaman jati ke birpar | jiv karun kurban ||
Vedokun sadka diya | so Jivan nam Rahman ||121||
Ja charan kamal barshata | sada prem prakash ||
Sitapatike das par | bali bali Jivandas ||122||
Lanka balyo satorane | bal na vanko thay ||
Anjani sutke Jivana | Raghupati sada sahay ||123||
Varah varu dhar dhara | vasudha kidhi thar ||
daitya sankashtthi chhodavi | so Jivan pran adhar ||124||

|| Iti Shri Daska Ang ||3||
|| Iti Shri dvitiya vishram sampurna ||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter of the Servant ||3||

1. Wherever Kabir's shade falls, there dwells Sitapati (Ram, the lord of Sita). He who does not forget the Name even for a moment - Jivan, he is a true servant.

2. To be a servant is hard; to be a master is easy talk. To live without Ram's Name, Jivan - both of these are nothing but ruin.

3. The "I" does not go, Jivan, even for holy men like Sanak and his brothers; Brahma and the other gods wore themselves out and died - the ego is the great affliction.

4. That Lord is ours, Jivan - He who is Dasharath's son Raghuvir. One who leaves Him and worships another is to be called shameless.

5. The worshipper of the formless worships Niranjan; Radha's beloved is Kanha. This is our glory, Jivan - the two Names, Ram and Krishna.

6. He never proves false, Jivan; He is the ever-imperishable light. For the sake of His own servants Raghupati made His glory shine out.

7. By His Name, by His deeds, by His form one is carried across; the dust of His feet destroys the greatest sins. Such is Raghupati, Jivan - why then would He cast off even a sinful man?

8. He showed grace to Kali (the serpent Kaliya) when He set His foot upon his head. Now do the same for me, Jivan - O Lord of Janak's daughter.

9. Our Ram is Niranjan, whom the Vedas cannot fathom. With the ocean's daughter is our Lord, Jivan - He who sports in Radha's bower.

10. He neither enjoyed it nor spent it, Jivan, though he had some wealth in hand. One who leaves Raghupati and worships another - his wealth serves only a paramour's son.

11. Ram and Kabir are one, in whose heart the Name has entered. Do not make the body your home, Jivan - His country is in the unsupported sky.

12. My master is Ramji, He who is the cowherd in Gokul. He answered Ambarish's cry for help, Jivan - Hari who takes the ten avatars.

13. In the Kali age plenty of showy piety is met with, but not one true devotee of Hari. If a devotee of Hari were met, Jivan, then I would weep out my sorrow to him.

14. It sprouts without rain, without soil, without seed. Such is bhakti (devotion), Jivan - the seed that is a seed without any seed.

15. By the one Name alone, Jivan, one is freed from the twenty-eight hells. Such are You, Raghupati - and yet every fault lies in us alone.

16. That Lord of ours is Ramji, He who subdued the serpent Kaliya. At His feet, Jivan, may I remain forever - that is my good fortune.

17. Sitapati is the dark-hued one, Raghuvir who bears the bow; He plays the flute at His lips - Jivan, the cowherd at His play.

18. Into the mass of light, into the radiance, the servant Kabir went. That Lord is ours, Jivan - Sitapati Raghuvir.

19. Some worship the one with form, some the formless in His own abode. This is our vow, Jivan - the Name of Sitapati.

20. Brahma, gods and men all repeat the formless in His own abode. This is our vow, Jivan - the Name of Sitapati.

21. The world keeps its vigil, Jivan, with japa, austerity, pilgrimage and charity. The devotee of Hari keeps vigil with the Name - that is the Sadguru's word, and it is the measure.

22. Shesh with a thousand mouths and two tongues repeats the Rarankar (the sound of Ram's Name). Shiv and Shakti became immortal by it - that, Jivan, is the support of life.

23. The foot by which Ahalya was delivered, from which the stream fell upon Shiva's head - that foot was set on Kali's head, Jivan, that foot where Kamala (Lakshmi) sports.

24. The dust of the feet that delivered Ahalya - that very one is our Ram. As for the rest of the world, Jivan, let it prattle on to no purpose.

25. The wedded pair, the two together, Jivan - Janak's daughter and Raghuvir. May that image dwell in my heart, with Shesh (Lakshman) the steadfast companion in battle.

26. Kaag Bhushundi took the morsel of bread, and the hand reached out across the three worlds. That Lord is ours, Jivan - Sitapati Raghunath.

27. In the Dwapar age Kanha appeared, in the Treta age Raghuvir. In the Kali age, Jivan, the servant Kabir appeared.

28. On the Yamuna's bank the Yadav (Krishna), on the Sarayu's bank Raghuvir; on the Ganga's bank, Jivan, the servant Kabir appeared.

29. It shimmers and shimmers - the light of Parbrahm (the supreme Brahman). With the ocean's daughter is our Lord, Jivan - He who fills all Brahman to the full.

30. Though the eye does not see Him, Jivan, let the ear hear His Name; and then utter it with a full mouth - Sitapati Raghuram.

31. The perfect Brahman fills everything, as the sun fills the sky. That Lord is ours, Jivan - Sitapati, the imperishable.

32. "I made every delight, Jivan, for the sake of My own people; afterwards I took their leavings - and then I gained the name Brijraj."

33. "I was the imperishable one from the beginning, but I did not have the name 'lover of devotees'. I became the lover of devotees, Jivan, when I came to the village of Gokul."

34. Giving two for two and fourfold besides - no one has been seen to give like that. Jadupati (Krishna) gave in that measure, Jivan - look, Sudama is the witness.

35. [unclear] Its span of life is ten billion (years) - so says Jivandas.

36. "I offer every delight, Jivan, wherever My own servant is. What talk is there of two or four, when it is the devotee I long for?"

37. Three ages went by wasted, without devotion to Ram and to no purpose. Now in the Kali age Kabir has appeared; Jivan, he has established the reign of the devotee.

38. To wipe away the stain of the Kali age, the servant Kabir appeared. He made the guru pure, Jivan, and revealed Raghuray.

39. The Kali age has come, Jivan, and with it the light of nirgun (formless) devotion. In Satyug, Treta and Dwapar the hope lay in rites and duty.

40. "In Satyug, Treta and Dwapar I stayed close to My own devotees. Now in the Kali age, Jivan, I am the servant of the simple-hearted devotee."

41. In Satyug Hari was white, in Treta Hari was yellow; in Dwapar Hari was dark of hue, and in Kaliyug His form is the reverse of all these.

42. "In Satyug and Treta, Jivan, Vaikunth was My dwelling; in Dwapar I dwelt in Gokul; in the Kali age I dwell wherever My own servant is."

43. Nal the vanar held it in his heart - such are Hari's servants. They cross the ocean of worldly existence, Jivan, by faith in the shelter of the Name.

44. The Lord is met at the price of one's own head - so said the servant Kabir. All else is a false show, Jivan, the mockery of the ages.

45. Bearer of the earth, upholder of the sky, beyond all reckoning, imperishable - of Sitapati Raghunath, age after age, Jivandas is the servant.

46. My companion from birth, Jivan, is Sitapati Raghuvir - He creates, He sustains, and He gathers back; and He steadies the faltering step.

47. The earth would go to dissolution, if there were not such servants. By the dhun (continuous chanting) of the Name, Jivan, the very sky is held up.

48. When the great dissolution comes, Jivan, the world is drowned in delusion; but the devotees of Hari hold fast to the Name - they are in the shade of His lotus feet.

49. Air, water, earth and fire - all merge back into their own source. The devotees of Hari will remain, Jivan, absorbed in Hari Himself.

50. Meru's peak will move away, and the earth and the sky as well; but Sitapati's servants, Jivan, will stand unmoved.

51. Janaki is our mother, Ram our father. Age after age I ask this, Jivan - rest in the company of the saints (satsang).

52. Our mother and father, Jivan, are the sadhu, the Sadguru and Ram. I ask for nothing else - give me Your lotus feet and Your own Name.

53. My father is Ramji, my mother a woman of virtue. Age after age I ask this, Jivan - that I may take human birth.

54. All the world is in sorrow, Jivan; only Hari's servants are happy. The one wastes away and dies over maya (illusion); the other stays detached at Ram's feet.

55. From His own lips He says: listen, Jivan - Raghupati is My Name. If I do not protect My people, then of what use is the bow I bear?

56. "I bear the conch and the discus, Jivan, for the sake of My own people. If I do not protect My servant, then My name is not Brijraj."

57. "I bind up all ten directions, Jivan, and give the pledge of Raghupati: He guards the road and the ford, and sets one free from the four kinds of birth."

58. "For the devotee's wish, Jivan, I take a crore of incarnations. What talk is there of a mere ten, when the devotee is the very support of My life?"

59. For the devotee's wish, Jivan, Hari takes all ten avatars. He eluded both king and rishi - the Lord's lila (divine play) is endless and boundless.

60. There has been none, nor will there be, Jivan, like the servant Kabir. Govind calls him the pillar of the devotees; he steadies the faltering step.

61. There has been none, nor will there be, Jivan, like the servant Kabir. He descends to save the world - the greatest hero among heroes.

62. O mother, bear such a son as the servant Kabir. Govind calls him the pillar of the devotees; he steadies the faltering step.

63. Sarang is the crown of ragas, Ram is the crown of names; and the crown of devotees, Jivan, appeared in the town of Kashi.

64. Among ragas, Sarang is the crown; among scriptures, the dhol (hymn-song) is the crown; among devotees, Jivana, the crown is he in whom is revealed the cowherd of Braj.

65. Among ragas Sarang is the crown, among the Vedas Shyam (the dark Lord) is the crown; among the forms of Krishna, Radhika is the crown - she who appeared in the village of Gokul.

|| Sakhi bhetki - couplets of the meeting ||

66. [unclear: "bamb bahro"] outside, Jivana - by wavering no work is accomplished. Either the rule of Kabirji, the servant who spun the wheel, or the rule of Padmanabh (the Lord).

|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki - couplets from the Lord's own mouth ||

67. For Devahuti's sake, Jivana, I became the incarnation of the sage Kapil; for Yadu I became Dattatreya - I, Padmanabh, the lord of riches.

68. Each recognized his own, Jivana - Padmanabh, the lord of riches. Master and servant met, and the work of the devotees was accomplished.

69. I am in the Ocean of Milk, Jivana, but my mind is in Gokul. Grieved by separation from my devotees I became sorrowful, for there no such devotee comes.

70. I am in the Ocean of Milk, Jivana, and for a long while I remain listless - my joy is in the bowers of Vrindavan, in the company of Radha.

71. I am a sacrifice to that woman who called me into Gokul. As the Bansi-bat (the banyan of the flute) is, Jivana, no other banyan's leaf is its equal.

72. In Vrindavan, Jivana, Raghuvir is in every single leaf. For many days he stayed hungry and then came to the bank of the Kalindi (Yamuna).

73. I was in Ayodhya, Jivana, but my mind was in Gokul; I had given my word to the sages' wives, and I do not forget that pledge of mine.

74. Leaving Ayodhya desolate, he came to the little village of Gokul. That is our Lord, Jivana - the Ram who slew Ravan.

75. The One became infinite and spread himself out, for love of his devotees - Raghuvir. For many days he stayed hungry and then came to the bank of the Kalindi.

76. The One became infinite and spread himself out, for love of his devotees - Raghuvir. He increased love, Jivana, on the bank of the Kalindi.

77. Now I shall do this, Jivana, holding the saints' word as authority: I shall be born as Nishkalank (the stainless one) and deliver all four orders of living beings.

|| Sakhi bhetki - couplets of the meeting ||

78. Serve the saints royally; the formless Name is the support. For love of his devotees, Jivana, Raghupati took incarnation.

|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki - couplets from the Lord's own mouth ||

79. Of the Raghu line and of the Yadu line, Jivana - the husband of Sita and the beloved of Radha - that Lord stands over our head, and his names are endless.

80. To abandon Sitapati Raghunath and take another's name - what other deed is there, Jivana, that would not give you a place in hell?

81. I offer my head as a sacrifice, Jivana, wherever the Lord's dear one is: he pardons the creature's fault and in an instant makes him blessed.

82. Fall into the path, Jivana, wherever the servants of Hari go out: stay in their company or let them take you along, and the heart's longing will be fulfilled.

83. The banner has been planted, Jivana - the true Name of Ram. It ferried Ajamil and the courtesan across; for us poor ones, then, how great a task can it be?

84. The elephant, the crocodile and the courtesan were ferried across, and Ajamil was carried over; by his feet Ahalya was redeemed - he is the support of Jivan's life-breath.

85. Son of mother Kaushalya, of Devaki, the delight of Yashoda - Kahan (Krishna); that is our Lord, Jivana - he who crushed the pride of Kali (the serpent Kaliya).

86. I give away body and mind, Jivana, wherever the servants of Sitapati are: with the mind absorbed in his lotus feet, they remain detached from the world.

87. Sutapa and Prishni performed austerity and fixed their meditation on Hari; that is our Lord, Jivana, who granted the boon of the unbroken ras (divine dance).

88. He fulfils the hope of the one who comes with self-interest, Jivana; but for the one who does bhakti (devotion) without self-interest, Raghupati becomes his servant.

89. No such one is met with, Jivana, with whom, on meeting, one might speak heart to heart - one who surrenders the ego, lifts it up and kicks it away.

90. When the demon grew terrible, he took the incarnation of Narsinh (the man-lion); he protected the devotee Prahlad - Jivana, hail to him through the ages.

91. I shall strike and tear him to pieces, as I ripped Hiranyakashipu apart; this is my sworn vow, Jivana - otherwise reproach would fall upon me.

92. To protect Prahlad, Jivana, consider a little in your own mind. Now this is the lesson taken for the saints' sake: [build] the embankment before the water comes.

93. Prahlad came into distress, Jivana, because there was delay on my part; now, says Raghuvir, I shall strike even before the enemy conceives the thought.

94. He stands holding bow and arrow, for the sake of all the saints. Jivana, my heart was drawn with longing when I heard some sound of it with my ears.

95. For the protection of his devotees, Jivana, Raghupati has two heroes - Anjani's son (Hanuman) and Lakshman - and the Lord himself stands there in person.

96. For the protection of his devotees, Jivana, Hari assumes the ten incarnations; now Haldhar (Balram) has taken up plough and pestle, and Gopal rides upon Garud.

97. Protect us, steadfast Raghuvir, lord of Anjani's son; this is the prayer of your servant Jivan - hear it, Lord of the world.

98. I have obtained the proof, Jivana - the true Name of Ram. It ferried Ajamil and the courtesan across; what use, then, is any other proof?

99. The proof of the Name of Parbrahm (the supreme Brahman) the Sadguru pointed out to me; every other proof, Jivana, crumbles away to nothing.

100. In some hearts Hari dwells, in some Shiv or Hanuman; in our heart, Jivana, dwells Das Kabir - that is our very own Name.

101. I count that I have found the wealth: the Name of Sitapati. Spending it, it is never exhausted - Jivana, all the world's other wealth is useless.

102. The upholder of the earth remained suspended, bound at Bali's door. What did Indra give, Jivana, and what did Bali take away by force?

103. The upholder of the earth remained suspended, bound at Bali's door. Bali offered up his all, Jivana, and Hari became absorbed in him.

104. When Shishupal hurled abuse, the discus then cut off his head; his light was absorbed into the Lord himself - he is the Lord of Jivan, his servant.

105. What has always been, Jivana, that surely shall be. The One whom Dhruv and Prahlad worshipped is the support of my life-breath.

106. Kahan (Krishna) crushed Kali (Kaliya) and brought down the pride of Indra; he severed Ravan's ten heads, Jivana - that very One is our Ram.

107. Sometimes Raghupati, sometimes Yadupati, sometimes the One resting on the couch of Shesh: all are one form, Jivana, only the names are different.

108. That Lord of ours is Ramji, who subdued the serpent Kali (Kaliya); may I always have the fortune, Jivana, of staying at his feet.

109. Behold the marvel, Jivana - the deed was done all the same. What merit had the hunter earned? [unclear: "kaha bal chalyo haram"].

110. Ajamil was a single great offender; he made his home with a courtesan. He committed many such deeds, Jivana - yet he had hope in the feet of Ram.

111. Ajamil and the courtesan were ferried across - he, Jivana, is our Ram; by his feet Ahalya was redeemed - he who is the abode of the ocean's daughter (Lakshmi).

112. You give me the word of your testimony, but there is no patience in my mind; this much is my prayer, Jivana - hear it within your heart.

113. Your servant Jivan is a sacrifice to the lord of Anjani's son; guard me on the road and at the landing-place, O king Raghupati.

114. That Lord of ours, Jivana, is the hero of the Raghu line and of the Yadu line; having played on the bank of the Saraju (Sarayu), he came to the bank of the Kalindi.

115. Countless disguised ones have raged, wanting to lay salt at your very root; but do not be afraid of them, Jivana - Kamalakanth (Lakshmi's lord) stands over your head.

116. Pride departs when one meets him, Jivana - hold Hari's Name in the heart. The ego shuddered and trembled, and then the Sun's son (Yam, death) was left empty-handed.

117. I abandoned Garud, Jivana, and ran to the rescue of the elephant; now, with conch, discus and Baldev, Garud my mount stands at the saints' door.

118. For the sake of Hari's devotees, Jivana, I would offer my life in sacrifice; the foolish mind does not understand, and reckons it a loss to its own dear ones.

119. The remembrance of Sitaram - whatever of it is done, that alone is profit; this chance of human birth, Jivana, will not be got again.

120. I have taken up conch and discus, Jivana, for the sake of my own devotees; how could I ever abandon this sworn vow? - so says Brijraj (the Lord of Braj).

121. I offer my life in sacrifice to the hero of the Jaman (Yavan) people; the Vedas were given up as an offering to him - that One, Jivana, bears the name Rahman.

122. From whose lotus feet there rains down always the light of love - to the servants of Sitapati, Jivandas is a sacrifice again and again.

123. Lanka was burnt together with its arched gateways, and not a hair of him was harmed; for Anjani's son, Jivana, Raghupati is always the helper.

124. Varaha lifted the earth upon his tusk and set the world at rest; he freed her from the torment of the demon - he is the support of Jivan's life-breath.

|| Here ends the Das ka Ang (the Canto of the Servant) ||3||
|| Here ends the Second Vishram (Resting-place), complete ||

sections.title_en: The Chapter of Awakening (Instructing Others)
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Prabodhaka Ang ||4||

Parghar jai prabodh kare | aape samjhe nahin ||
Aise moorakh Jivana | bohotek hai jag manhi ||1||
Mukh Hari Hari ochare | antargat kachhu aur ||
Kalptaru taj Jivana | take erandke ghaud ||2||
Haji haji mukh kahe | antargat kachhu aur ||
Ve apradhi Jivana | chaud lok nahi thaur ||3||
Sab santan mali Jivana | kino ek bichar ||
Sitapati bin aur kahe | take modhe chhar ||4||
Popat bahyo panjare | mar kahayo Ram ||
Chhand diyo jab Jivana | tab nahi Ram nam ||5||
Alarasi Jivana | tasu kaiso rah ||
Tan man arpe bhavsun | ta sir dije pay ||6||
Alarasi chakri | nishdin aave jay ||
Lekh lakhya bin Jivana | kodi kaise pay ||7||

Sir sate Sain mile | yun kahi Kabire das ||
Aur sab jootho pekhno | Jivan jag upahas ||8||
Sir sate Sain mile | e Jivan saheli baat ||
Dase sir sonpyo Shivkun | e Ravan bhoolyo ghat ||9||
E patra kupatra Jivana | Sadguru de batay ||
Nik sees Vibhishan namyo | tab bhaye Raghupati sahay ||10||
Lank Vibhishan thapiyo | Jivan jash akhand ||
E patra kupatre Jivana | sakh Ved kahe sant ||11||
Songhi soonthe Jivana | janyo na dekhun koy ||
Ja devne anusare | tanman mage soy ||12||
Sacha bola Jivana | avar na dekhun koy ||
Tan man arpi je rahe | sach kahave soy ||13||
Jootha bola Jivana | avar na dise koi ||
Sacha bola je rahe | te sat kahave soi ||14||
Tan man arpya tab janiye | jab jugthe rahe udas ||
Charan kamal man unmani | Jivan so nij das ||15||

Mohani mantra Jivana | Sadguru diya batay ||
Jine e mantra shravane sunyo | tine tanman arpyo aay ||16||
Shabad sacharachar dekhiye | chahudish mugat medan ||
Yun pand brahmand Jivana | so kahiye nij pran ||17||
Dehi darshan sab ko kare | shabad darshan nav hoy ||
Sabad darshan bin Jivana | par na pahoncha koy ||18||
Shabad darshan sabko kare | dehi darshan bhoolay ||
Raghupati kahe sun Jivana | taka sarbas jay ||19||
Brahma bhoolya Ved padhi | Vyas padhi Puran ||
Ranchi ek Shukdeve lahyo | so Jivan bhagat praman ||20||
Ram nam bhaj Jivana | je Gauripatiko dhyan ||
Ajamil gunaka tari | je setu bandhyo Hanuman ||21||
Amarikh gohare aaviyo | sundar Shyam swaroop ||
So Nand dware Jivana | je Dasharath kul bad bhoop ||22||
Amarikh gohare aaviyo | Hari dharyo natvar vesh ||
Sab jug bhoolyo Jivana | karat anek anek ||23||

Panch chor ghar bhitare | gyan ratan hari jay ||
Raghupati baheru Jivana | kun guhare dhay ||24||
Nagura mil bataan kare | kahe Ram Krishna avatar ||
Aur gali kaha Jivana | dhik tako parivar ||25||
Dhani vahuno dhor jyun | kis gohade jay ||
Yun gurumukh bahro Jivana | Sitapatikun dhay ||26||
Jit tit the marhi | jyon dhani vahono dhor ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | Jam padenge ror ||27||
Mat na jane manaskun | to putra pita kyon pay ||
Aise sab jug Jivana | Sitapatikun dhay ||28||
Manas kahiye Maharajkun | mat so hai Gurudev ||
Guruke vachane Jivana | kar Sadguruki sev ||29||
Mata hoy vyabhicharini | to auran kahiye tat ||
Mat pativrata Jivana | take tat Raghunath ||30||
Mata hamari Janaki | pita hamare Ram ||
Jug jug magun Jivana | sant sangat vishram ||31||

Pita hamare Ramji | mata satvanti nar ||
Jug jug magun Jivana | dhar manav avatar ||32||
Matapita hamare Jivana | sadhu Sadguru Ram ||
Aur kachhu magun nahi | dyo charankamal nij nam ||33||
Das avatarke dagdage | bhoolya sab sansar ||
Ko ek oogare Jivana | jine gurumukh kiyo vichar ||34||
Avatar apradhi kahe Jivana | jake nahi guru pir ||
Aad ant madhya Shamlo | nirgun Brahma sharir ||35||
Ram Krishna je Jivana | do sagun avatar ||
Andh dhandh kaha bhajun | je Ved na pave par ||36||
Kab Raghupati kab Jadupati | bhagat het avatar ||
Bemukh nav samjhe Jivana | e sab ekakar ||37||
Dase avatare Shamlo | chovise akhand ||

sections.translation:
Here begins the Prabodhaka Ang (the chapter on awakening others), the fourth.

1. He goes into another's house and preaches, but understands nothing himself. Such fools, Jivan, are plentiful in this world.

2. With his mouth he utters "Hari, Hari," but within him it is something else. Abandoning the wish-fulfilling tree, Jivan, he sets his eyes on a clump of castor plants.

3. With the mouth he says "Yes sir, yes sir," while inside is something else. Such offenders, Jivan, have no place in the fourteen worlds.

4. All the saints met together, Jivan, and reached one conclusion: whoever speaks of any other than Sitapati (Ram, the lord of Sita) — ashes in his mouth.

5. The parrot was kept in a cage, and by beating it was made to say "Ram." When it was let go, Jivan, then there was no name of Ram at all.

6. The half-hearted man, Jivan — what sort of a path is his? He who offers body and mind with true feeling — at his feet lay down your head.

7. Half-hearted is his service: night and day he merely comes and goes. Without the reckoning being written down, Jivan, how will he receive even a cowrie?

8. The Lord is met at the price of one's own head — so said the servant Kabir. All else is a false show; Jivan, the world is a mockery.

9. "The Lord is met at the price of the head" — Jivan, this you take for an easy matter. Ravan surrendered his ten heads to Shiv, and yet Ravan missed the point of it.

10. Who is a worthy vessel and who unworthy, Jivan — the Sadguru (true master) shows it. Vibhishan bowed his head rightly, and then Raghupati (Ram) became his helper.

11. He established Vibhishan in Lanka — unbroken is that fame, Jivan. This matter of the worthy and the unworthy vessel, Jivan: the Vedas and the saints bear witness to it.

12. Cheap as dry ginger, Jivan — I see no one who has come to know [the Lord] at so cheap a price. Whichever deity a man follows, that deity demands his body and mind.

13. Speakers of truth, Jivan — I see no other kind worth the name. Whoever remains having offered up body and mind, he alone is called truthful.

14. Speakers of falsehood, Jivan — I see nothing else anywhere. Those who remain speakers of truth, they are called sat (the true).

15. Body and mind are known to be truly offered only when a man remains detached from the world. With the mind in unmani (thought-free absorption) at the lotus feet — he, Jivan, is His own servant.

16. The enchanting mantra, Jivan, the Sadguru has revealed. Whoever heard this mantra with his ears came and offered up body and mind.

17. The Word (shabad) is seen in all that moves and does not move; in all four directions lies the open field of liberation. Thus in the body and in the cosmos, Jivan — call that one's own life-breath.

18. Everyone takes darshan (sight) of the body; darshan of the Word does not happen. Without darshan of the Word, Jivan, no one has reached the far shore.

19. If a man takes darshan of the Word but forgets darshan of the body [of the guru], Raghupati says — listen, Jivan — his all is lost.

20. Brahma went astray reading the Vedas, and Vyas reading the Puranas. Shukdev grasped one tiny particle of it — that, Jivan, is the measure of a devotee.

21. Chant the name of Ram, Jivan — that which is the meditation of Gauripati (Shiv). Ajamil and the courtesan were carried across by it; by it Hanuman built the bridge.

22. He came to Ambarish's cry for help in the beautiful dark form. He it is who is at Nanda's door, Jivan — he who is the great king of Dasharath's line.

23. He came to Ambarish's cry for help; Hari took on the guise of the player-dancer. The whole age has gone astray over it, Jivan, making him into many and many again.

24. Five thieves are inside the house, and they carry off the jewel of knowledge. If Raghupati is left outside, Jivan, who will run at your cry for help?

25. The guruless meet and make talk, calling Ram and Krishna [mere] incarnations. What else but abuse do they speak, Jivan — shame upon their whole family.

26. Like cattle without an owner — into whose fold does it go? So is the man who stays outside the gurumukh way, Jivan: run to Sitapati.

27. It is beaten from this side and that, like cattle without an owner. Without Sitapati, Jivan, the messengers of Yama will raise an uproar over him.

28. If the mother does not know her husband, how will the son find his father? So it is with the whole age, Jivan: run to Sitapati.

29. By "the husband" is meant the Maharaj (the Lord), and the mother is the Gurudev. By the guru's word, Jivan, do the service of the Sadguru.

30. If the mother is unchaste, then others are named as father. If the mother is devoted to one husband, Jivan, then her son's father is Raghunath.

31. Our mother is Janaki (Sita), our father is Ram. Age after age I ask, Jivan, for rest in the company of the saints (satsang, holy company).

32. Our father is Ramji, our mother the woman true to her vow [Sita]. Age after age I ask, Jivan, to take on a human birth.

33. Our mother and father, Jivan, are the sadhu, the Sadguru and Ram. I ask for nothing else — grant me the lotus feet and your own Name.

34. In the dazzle of the ten avatars the whole world has lost its way. Only some rare one is saved, Jivan — he who reflected on it as a gurumukh (one turned toward the guru).

35. He who has no guru and no pir (spiritual master) calls him only an avatar, Jivan, and is an offender. In the beginning, the end and the middle it is the dark Lord; the nirgun (formless) Brahman is his body.

36. Ram and Krishna, Jivan, are the two sagun (with-form) incarnations. Why should I worship blind confusion, which the Vedas themselves cannot fathom?

37. Now Raghupati, now Jadupati (Krishna) — incarnations for the devotees' sake. The turned-away man does not understand, Jivan, that all these are one and the same form.

38. In the ten avatars it is the dark Lord; through the twenty-four he is undivided. In all the sakhis (couplets), Jivan, he pervades a crore of universes.

39. The Veda gave up its blind confusion and came to the bank of the Yamuna, where the eternal Brahman is, Jivan — Ram and Krishna, the very root.

40. Raghupati studied the science of the bow; Jadunath held the flute. He slew the lord of Lanka, Jivan, and with that same hand he lifted the mountain.

41. Raghupati and Jadupati, Jivan, are like the moon [and its reflection] in the ocean. Radha's beloved and Sita's lord — why does the dull-witted man not worship them?

42. The Veda called him all-pervading; how then can he ever be effaced? The life of all living beings, Jivan — that is truly Raghupatiray.

43. The Veda called him all-pervading, but for us there is one Hari alone: of the line of Raghu and the line of Yadu, Jivan, together with Radha and Sita.

44. Meditate on the primal, imperishable one, who has neither form nor outline. He is the bridegroom in Nanda's house, Jivan — he whom Shankar and Shesh sing of.

45. In the forest of the Vedas, Jivan, the whole world has lost its way. Rite and religious duty became a hangman's noose; the qazi and the brahmin became death itself.

46. The Vedas have misled the whole age; you are not on our side. I will tear them to pieces, Jivan, if they come into my hands.

47. There was a shout of victory, Jivan, when the servant Kabir appeared. Cutting away all rite and religious duty, he made Raghuvir manifest.

48. Kabir of the [Ramkabir] line appeared, and the Veda took thought. It made a plea to the people of Hari: "Let us stay on in the world."

49. "Riddhi and siddhi (prosperity and occult powers) dwell in us; wherever they are asked for, we give them. People of Hari, worship Hari, Jivan — we ourselves say only 'neti, neti' (not this, not this)."

50. The brahmin committed adultery, Jivan, and kept company with drink. He cried out for his son's sake — was he carried across merely by the name Narayan?

51. He was not saved by calling out to his son, nor was he saved by the name of Hari [alone]. By the word of the Sadguru, Jivan, Raghuram came and met him.

52. The guruless meet and make talk, and they are false, Jivandas. They let the senses graze in every direction, and yet they hope for the fruit of worshipping Ram.

53. He carried on a love affair with another man's wife, Jivandas; he broke every Vedic duty — and still [claims] faith in the refuge of the Name.

54. Paradise is only the Lord's hospitality; the eighty-four [lakh births] are full of it. What are horses and elephants there, Jivan, to one who stands in Hari's own presence?

55. Even a blind man shooting an arrow does not miss the wall, Jivan. So a man cannot go to hell who worships Raghuvir even in simplicity.

56. He wore the sacred bracelet of Kedar and performed the Vajapeya sacrifice. But without Sitapati, Jivan, the name of Ram merely fell into his mouth [as empty words].

57. The chain came down from [unclear], and the age made a mockery of it, Jivan. Loss and gain were all thrown into turmoil when the servant offered up body and mind.

58. Each man warms himself at his own fire. Warm yourselves together, Jivan, so that devotion (bhakti) to Ram may grow firm.

59. What the Vedas and Puranas have told of — remember that Ram, Jivan. He it was who sanctified Panchvati, the same who is the abode of joy in Vrindavan.

60. I do not know the secret of the Vedas, nor do I know the shastras and puranas. I know Raghupati, Jivan — he who gave the gift to Sudama.

61. The father[s] of both [unclear]; Kaushalya and Nanda's wife [as mothers]. He is our Lord, Jivan — he who begged at Bali's door.

62. When Ramanand gave his teaching to Kabir, from that moment karma trembled, Jivan: "he has sent us into exile."

63. Karma hid itself away in Vaikunth, mingling in with heaven. All the ages of Satyug are gone, Jivan; Kaljug takes it into partnership.

64. Vaikunth (Vishnu's heaven) fell to weeping and heaven stood beating its head: their servants, Jivan, we have looted away in between (won them over to the Name instead).

65. The two cannot stand together, Jivan - the self (ego) and Hari's name. He who wipes out the self and worships Hari attains the state of rest.

66. All come running to meet, Jivan, but no one meets through bhakti (devotion). He who meets after wiping out the self - he alone is called a devotee.

67. So long as even one deed of doership remains, one does not turn back again. By his own self a man does not reach Hari, however much he worships Raghunath.

68. Raghupati says: listen, Jivan, this is our word - in exchange for the self one is let go from the eighty-four lakh wombs (all the species of birth).

69. Everyone speaks falsely, Jivan; they have no love for Hari's devotees. Not one such person is met with who is together with Sitaram.

70. I searched the whole world, Jivan - not one is truly yours. Every single one is pleased with his own station.

71. For the sake of a devotee of Hari, Jivan, I have looked through my own land and foreign lands. If a devotee meets me with love, I give him the teaching of love and devotion.

72. Such a hard-to-swallow thing it is, Jivan - caste, sub-caste and clan all go. It is a matter beyond all matters, one over which even Brahma and the gods are cheated.

73. Hari came at a single call, for Ajamil's sake. He comes uninvited, Jivan, wherever the devotee's rule holds.

74. In Ram's incarnation she was left a widow; in Krishna's he gave her wifehood. Brahma and the gods are left bewildered, Jivan, while the girls of Braj drink the nectar.

75. The chest splits, Jivan - devotion to Ram is not easy. When the heart falls broken to pieces, then one attains the state of nirvan (final release).

76. Worship Ram's name, Jivan; with anything else there is no business. Ajamil and the courtesan were carried across - by this same Ram, this same Name.

77. Worship Ram's name, Jivan; this chance comes only once. The days that have gone do not come back, O madman - death hovers over your head.

78. I know neither beginning nor end, and have no business with the middle. By the power of the Name even stones float - so, Jivan, remember Ram.

79. Beginning, end and middle is Shyam (the dark Lord); there is no second matter. He is our Master, Jivan - the one whom Bhrigu struck with his foot.

80. When Raghupati took up the bow, he struck off Ravan's heads. Madhav is beginning, end and middle - He is the Lord of the servant Jivan.

81. He held mount Govardhan on his hand for the sake of the whole region of Braj. He is our Master, Jivan - the one who gave Vibhishan a kingdom.

82. When He took up the bow, Jivan, terror seized the whole demon race. For the sake of his servant Vibhishan, Raghupati took exile in the forest.

83. A dream came to the young wife: "Why do you sleep, husband Ravan?" All ten heads will be cut off, Jivan - Vibhishan has gone over as a friend.

84. He had a young wife at home - then what need was there to carry off Sita? Ravan was no fool, Jivan; he was aiming at the seat of liberation.

85. When the navel was pierced with the shaft, then the ten heads fell. He set Vibhishan up in Lanka - such is the Lord of the servant Jivan.

86. The true Master is Ramji, who held mount Govardhan on his hand. Going to Janak's house, Jivan, he broke the bow and won Sita.

87. The true Master is Ramji, who breaks the heads of all the proud. Therefore worship the Name, Jivan - He who is the Lord of his servant Prahlad.

88. On the bank of the Yamuna the young Yadav, the child Gopal, plays. He who cut off the ten heads, Jivan, has now become the death of Kansa's clan.

89. On Sitapati Raghunath I offer body, mind and life-breath. By Him it is made easy [unclear], Jivan - even for one who was already on his way to the cremation ground.

90. Let some practise tantra and mantra, let some repeat Shiv and Hanuman. Ours is this one vow, Jivan: meditation on Sitapati (the husband of Sita, Ram).

91. Some hold a vow to Hari, some to Shiv and Hanuman. Ours is this vow, Jivan: the very Name held by the servant Kabir.

92. All those paths, Jivan, where the hope rests on rites and religious works - playing at a false game, the whole age goes away disappointed.

93. What is Ram's name good for? It takes away whatever sin there is. Repetition, austerity and pilgrimage, Jivan - all these belong to Death's own household.

94. At the last moment everyone wishes for Hari's name. But he who does not remember it while he lives, Jivan - that man is the offender.

95. No god or goddess is anything, and in my mind there is nothing of any of them. Jivan's mind holds this faith: that Ram is our Master.

96. No brother, no blood-kin is truly one's own, nor village nor place. I have searched the whole world, Jivan - be merciful, Raghuram.

97. Many a sakhi (couplet) and shabad (hymn) have been spoken, yet the mind will not hold steady. So Jivan makes his prayer: hear it, Ram and Kabir.

98. Hari came leaving Garuda behind, when the elephant cried out "Ram!" What anxiety can there be for the servant Jivan, who remembers Sitaram?

99. By Hari's name the elephant crossed over - then how much greater a matter is a man? That a man does not cross over, Jivan - that is the disaster.

100. Man drowns through pride; the elephant crossed over by crying out. Without the guru's grace, Jivan, who will speak and make it understood?

101. When the elephant was released the crocodile too was set free; Ahalya was delivered and even the parrot crossed over. Such is Raghupati, Jivan - yet the heartless man does not understand.

102. As one acts, so one suffers - that was so as long as there was no guru, no master. Change your course of religion, Jivan, at once, in this very body.

103. Ritual action is the very life of one's living; letting it go feels like dying. Yet without letting it go, Jivan, how is the supreme state to be reached?

104. Worldly business stands in the way, Jivan, without remembrance of Sarangpani (the wielder of the Sharanga bow, Vishnu). Without the name of Sitapati the whole world lies desolate.

105. Cowries tied round the neck - such is this world. People follow Gauripati (Shiv), Jivan, forsaking the husband of Janak's daughter (Ram).

106. The juggler has staged his show - such is this world. Standing in the middle of it and facing it, Jivan, Ram's name is the only support.

107. Pirs and prophets last five days; Allah alone is one and undivided. Neither the Vedas nor the kateb (the Semitic scriptures) have fathomed Him, Jivan - the One who fashioned the universe.

108. Where has that strength gone? The feet are worn out with running. This is the end of all, Jivan - the pauper's and the king's alike.

109. Among the fifty-two letters, Jivan, one letter is the essence of truth. Of the one written first as "ma", even the Vedas do not reach the far end.

110. He was born in the solar dynasty; Raghupati shone forth as light. He made his own father holy, Jivan - the hope is on those very feet.

111. In the fire of the womb, Jivan, it is Raghuvir who protects. He who leaves Him and worships another - call that man heartless.

112. Idle, idle - what does the idle man do? Do not be idle for even a moment. Without Sitapati, Jivan, no other far shore is to be seen.

113. Ram slew Ravan, and then the thirty-three (crore gods) were set free. He installed Vibhishan in Lanka - He is the Lord of the servant Jivan.

114. Our Master is Ramji, who broke down the fort of Lanka. What are all the others worth, Jivan, when even Ravan looks a pauper before Him?

115. Worship Ram's name, Jivan - He who as the Boar upheld the earth, and who, killing Narakasur, wedded sixteen thousand women.

116. Ram's name is the essence of truth - true, true, and beyond all doubt. Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over by it, and on it Shukdev fixes his meditation.

117. Throw off the load of karma, Jivan; this has been granted within the Kali age. Ramkabir pervades everything, and we too move about within Him.

118. The wife weeps, Jivan, and throws dust on her head: my husband has gone out of my hands - he has gone and grasped his own root (the Lord).

119. Mother and father together, Jivan, beat their breasts: our son has gone out of our hands - he has given his love to Hari's devotees.

120. In house after house the longings differ, and every day there are new colours. Without Sitapati, Jivan, all of it comes to ruin.

121. I have nothing against anyone, Jivan; every one of them is of my own kind. But as white cloth takes on dye, so the devotee of Hari has changed his hue.

122. Five elements and the three gunas (qualities) - in these all are of one kind with me. But the devotee of Hari is like this, Jivan: as milk and ghee are to buttermilk.

123. Duryodhan made his claim: we are of a great line, we are mighty kings. But Vidur's plain greens were taken, Jivan - Vidur, the son of a serving-maid.

124. He is no maid-servant's son, Jivan; the devotee is my very life. Whoever offers body and mind with love - him do I honour.

125. Honouring him I give my all; body, mind and life-breath I offer up. I keep nothing back from the devotee; meeting him I worship the Lord.

126. The feast is of Raghupati's name, and Hari's devotees eat of it till they are full. But he who turns his face away, Jivan, does not get to taste a single grain of it.

127. Blessed is Vidur, Jivan - I ate his unsalted greens. He made the tasted berries sweet - such is his love for his own people.

128. The yogi laid a curse upon the age; the land of Gujarat was steeped in pride. To lift that curse, O Jivana, the Lord took birth as Padmanabh.

129. In the land of Gujarat appeared the wise Gorakhnath; and Das Kabir, O Jivana, laid his hand upon his head.

130. At the awakening given by the wise one, Jivandas arose; leaving all other paths behind, he set his hope on Sitapati (the Lord of Sita, Ram).

131. Worshipping gods and great sages, everyone has beaten those well-worn tracks; the whole age has gone astray, O Jivana - Ram has thrown it all into an uproar.

132. Among all spiritual disciplines, O Jivana, the name of Ram is the very essence of truth; Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over by it - something the Vedas do not grasp in the least.

133. If Hari is obtained at the price of body and mind, know it to be cheaply had; in the end all will depart, O Jivana - the body of flesh ends either in hell or in nirvana (final release).

134. He slew the elephant Kuvalaya, O Jivana, and left Kans weeping. What could the poor father do? - the mother looked into the face of Kalayavan.

135. Having slain the elephant Kuvalaya and the wrestlers, he broke off Kans's head; he set Vibhishan upon Lanka - He is the Lord of His servant Jivana.

136. "I strike the mouth of the one who slanders My servant; I cast him out of Vaikunth" - such, O Jivana, is the vow (birad) He holds to for my sake.

137. In the blink of an eye, O Jivana, the whole world is a place of perishing; all that we see is a false game - true are Ram and Rahman.

138. He who repeats Ram and Rahman - he has a guru, a pir (Muslim spiritual master). Without guru or pir, O Jivana, the body is nothing but ghost and spirit.

139. The Sadguru (true master) made me understand, O Jivana, the name of Sitapati; Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over - take up that Name, O blind one.

140. Sisters, such an opportunity will not come a second time; wealth (maya) you will meet many times over, but the gathering of saints will not come again.

141. The senses are the offenders, O Jivana; they work a great deal of evil. What is a poor man's strength worth, when they fling gods and men alike into the pit?

142. Chant the name of Ram, O Jivana - He who is the Lord of Anjani's son (Hanuman); He wiped away the sin of slaying Lanka's lord - the lord whose heads were laid before Shiv as nirmalya (offerings made over to the deity).

143. Though a man give gold weighed out ten million times against his own body, it is only Shiv's cast-off offering, O Jivana, if he has no love for Hari's devotees.

144. Though he offer a Meru of gold and hand over his whole treasury - says Kabir - if he has turned his face away from the guru, how shall he reach the far shore?

145. What is gained by pride before the guru? He has cast aside his own true interest. Without the dharma of the soul, O Jivana, he has heaped up sin all over again.

146. Put your trust in Sitapati Raghunath and in no one else; if you hold Him false, O Jivana, from where can well-being come?

147. Hiding his sin within the house, he keeps his wealth concealed; in the end it is all laid bare, O Jivana - why not have done rightly at the first?

148. Jivana, let the world flow on by; make your love with Raghupati. So our Sadguru told us: the age of Kali runs contrary to all good.

149. From the one Allah the two came into being - one a horse, one a lord (mir); this is the bargain and the barter, O Jivana - and man, having no pir, does not understand it.

150. In a single instant He made everything - the three worlds and the twenty-one universes; but in the making of a devotee of Hari, O Jivana, ten or twenty days are spent.

151. People eat and drink their fill and make the self-interest of the senses their religion; without Sitapati, O Jivana, not a single karma is cut away.

152. The little dog walking in the cart's shadow thinks that he is the one pulling it; the remembrance of Hari is the ox that draws the load, O Jivana - so let no one fall into that delusion.

153. The mouth from which nectar drips - how should foul speech come out of it? Foul words are spoken, O Jivana, where guru and pir give no help.

154. Apart from Veda and Kateb (the Semitic scriptures), O Jivana, stand the servants of Hari; renouncing heaven, hell and Vaikunth alike, they long only for Hari's feet.

155. Everyone gives milk and rice, but no one gives up his own self (apa, egoity); while the ego stands there, O Jivana, the food is a ghost's fare.

156. All of it is the Jain path, O Jivana, wherever the hope rests in rite and merit; playing at that false game, the whole age goes away disappointed.

157. All of it is the Jain path, O Jivana, where there are no servants of Hari; work what rites and merit you please, the dwelling is still heaven or hell.

158. Rajasic, tamasic, sattvic - the world's bhakti (devotion) is bound to the three gunas (qualities of nature); to be free of the three gunas, O Jivana, is the Sadguru's gift of grace.

159. He hands over body and mind, O Jivana, into this hand and that; leaving the wish-granting tree, he embraces the thorny babul.

160. Though one keep vows and the ekadashi fast and bathe in the Ganga day after day, without Sitapati, O Jivana, death sits inside the heart.

161. I make ekadashi my maidservant and pilgrimage my slave; the Beloved (Ramaiya) plays before my eyes - it is to Him I make my salaam.

162. I know no ekadashi; everyone has fallen into delusion. If a man binds his mind to the twelfth-day rite, from where is liberation to come?

163. The vessel is broken, O Jivana, and the substance never comes to hand. The whole world has fallen into its business - without becoming Hari's devotee, how is one to reach Raghunath?

164. The soul was fashioned afterwards; it takes its rest inside the vessel of the body. He gave you a mouth and teeth, O Jivana - why then do you not repeat Raghuram?

165. People feel ashamed at the name of Hari, the treasury of compassion; the witless drift away, as a ship slips loose upon the water.

166. Take what is given, O Jivana, though it be lakhs and crores that he gives; what is not given is haram (forbidden) - do not take so much as a broken straw of it.

167. Lakshmi serves at His feet; He is the crown of the fourteen worlds - yet Hari stood at Bali's door, O Jivana, for the sake of three paces of ground.

168. As a man does, O Jivana, so it is done back to him; in tricking Bali He was Himself caught by the trick - so let no one practise deceit.

169. Give up delusion and its wanderings; take up the primal "I am He" (ohankar, soham). The Sadguru sat down and showed it plainly, O Jivana - there lies great good fortune.

170. Shame on the mother, shame on the father, shame on the whole family; shame on the village and the place, O Jivana, that calls Raghupati merely an avatar (an incarnation).

171. Sisters, old age is drawing close - remember Sitaram; while you romped at hamchi (a girls' folk game) with your friend, the birth has gone to waste.

172. By talk alone the fritters are already made, while the lentils are still in the merchant's shop; and even before that, O Jivana, the children have set up their clamour.

173. Some worship the four-armed one, some meditate on the eight-armed; chant the name of Ram, O Jivana - He who grazes the cows in Gokul.

174. By what karma was it, O Jivana, that Jadupati the king was nowhere to be found? When the father tormented Prahlad, Raghupati did not come to his aid.

175. With his tongue he calls it sin over and over, while inwardly he is its father [unclear]; such is the way of the world, O Jivana - son and daughter are a great sin.

176. Neither of the pair got across [unclear]; it is a game of faction against faction. Without pressing the sesame, O Jivana, how is the oil to come out?

177. Both were lost, O Jivana - the donkey's way and the celibate's; he never came to know devotion to Ram, and he abandoned the conduct of his lineage.

178. All splendour is ashes, O Jivana, where Hari's devotees do not dwell - be it horses, be it a hut, be it great Kailas itself.

179. Satsang (holy company) does not please him, yet he hopes for liberation. To whom shall the father tell it, O Jivana, when the son born to him has turned out a slave?

180. Ashtavakra and the rest, Brahma, Shukdev and Vyas - and on down to Kans's maidservant, O Jivana, every one of them became His servant.

181. It cannot be managed this way, O Jivana - breaking the lump of jaggery inside a little pot (doing it all in secret). Worship Hari at the price of your own self: that I take to be Hari's own covenant (kol).

182. Watch the spectacle, O Jivana, with your legs stretched out at ease; everyone jostles and harries the devotee of Hari - and such people are without the Creator's grace.

183. Looking at his horses and elephants, the lord (mir) grew heedless in his mind; it is all a covering of skin, O Jivana - and man, having no pir, does not understand.

184. Out of one wheat, O Jivana, a great many dishes are made; Sitapati is only One, though the names given Him are many.

185. The world says, O Jivana, "Stay close to the world." Our king is Ram, at whose feet Lakshmi has her dwelling.

186. Flee from the swelling of the ego; keep your household life in that way. Take the fruit of this human birth - make your dwelling in the company of saints.

187. Whoever does good does it for himself; whoever does evil must bear it himself. Apart from both, O Jivana, is the place where Sitapati's name is repeated.

188. The jackals sniffed at the mouth and let the corpse float away; if the mouth does not utter Ram, then, O Jivana, how is it to be trusted?

189. He slew the lord of Lanka, O Jivana, for the sake of gods and sages; and he set Vibhishan upon Lanka - one road, two errands done.

190. What has Raghuvir not done, O Jivana, to fulfil His devotees' longing! Sometimes He became pure light; sometimes He took on a body.

191. For Sita's sake, O Jivana, He slew the wretched Ravan; [unclear: "the nail bent under the force"] and gave Lanka over to Vibhishan.

192. O poor one, give up your pride; render service to the saints - those for whose darshan (sight of a holy one), O Jivana, gods, sages and celestials long.

193. The vessel breaks, O Jivana, and the substance never comes to hand; the kheer belongs to the whole panchayat, O Jivana - who is it that worships Raghunath in simple innocence?

194. He went blind in the pursuit of experience; through knowledge he never arrived at love. Devotion itself has turned into doubt, O Jivana - where then is the rule that leads to liberation?

195. It will burn away and be charcoal, and no one will care for it; chant the name of Ram, O Jivana - at this hour, on this very turn.

196. Out of the five elements and the three gunas the whole world came into being; and its maker, O Jivana, is He who herds the cattle in Gokul.

197. There is the radiance (noor) of my Beloved; wherever I look, there is the crimson Beloved. I went to look upon that crimson, and then, O Jivana, I myself became gulal (crimson powder).

198. There is the radiance of my Beloved; wherever I look, there is the crimson Beloved. Without bandagi (worship, prayer) how is He to be found, O Jivana - that crimson Beloved?

199. Singing Raghupati's glory, countless people have crossed over; Ajamil and the courtesan crossed too - O Jivana, fall in behind them.

200. He brought Nama's (Namdev's) cow back to life; He supplied Panchali (Draupadi) with endless cloth; He cut down the crocodile and freed the elephant - such, O Jivana, is Raghuvir.

201. He knew the plight of the elephant-king, and the Lord of Vraj came; first the shot, O Jivana, and only afterwards the sound of it.

202. The cry of "Ha! ha!" was heard by Kamala (Lakshmi) - it was the elephant-king who had cried it; first the shot, O Jivana, and only afterwards the sound of it.

203. To cut away karma, O Jivana, the medicine is the name of Ram; for a sore eye or a boil, the jujube and the babul will serve.

204. Knowing his own colour, he worshipped Shyam alone; [unclear: "gave him ghat and food"], O Jivana - such is Raghupati Ram.

205. He took the form of Vaman the dwarf, O Jivana, and pressed Bali down into the netherworld; He removed the distress of Surpati (Indra) - He who cherishes His own people and Vraj.

206. He slew the elephant Kuvalaya, O Jivana, and broke off Kans's head; He made Kubja young and fair again - He is the Lord of His servant Jivana.

207. As a little bird fills its beak and quenches its own thirst - so it is with the virtues of Hari, O Jivana: does the Ganga grow any less for it?

208. Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over; He has lifted up ten million fallen ones. Knowing this, O Jivana, take hold of the shelter of the Name.

209. Some wear themselves out and die at Kedar; some seek the pir at Mecca and Medina. Our Lord (Sain), O Jivana, is He who is the champion of Yavan and yati alike.

210. One man has the strength of his own arm; another has a strong champion. This is our strength, O Jivana - Sitapati Raghuvir.

211. The Triveni without Trikam, the world's beauty - all of it is ashes; on such a head, O Jivana, rests only the prop of rite and merit.

212. The Triveni without Trikam, its beauty - ashes for certain; without satsang, O Jivana, the whole world has drowned.

213. The yogi has turned into a messenger of Yam, O Jivana - hell is his domain; seeing God to be an easy mark, he has plundered the whole world.

214. The great rutting elephant has fallen into the pit, O Jivana; by his own strength he will not get free - not without the grace of the moon-like Guru.

215. Radha's beloved, Sitapati - He is the Lord of His servant Jivana; Gauripati (Shiv) remembers Him always - He whose foot came down on Kaliya's head.

216. Without a guru or pir, O Jivana, the hope of Allah-Ram is vain; Veda and Kateb both say this - all alike are in the grip of Kal (Death).

217. One man's guru is a yogi, another's is a dervish; but for the devotee of Ram, O Jivana - what do such men know of true teaching?

218. When the self is erased, calamity is erased and every disease departs; birth after birth, sing the glory of Sitapati Raghunath.

219. Chant the name of Ram, O Jivana - that Name set the stones afloat; the sin of Ravan's killing was taken away, and there is no other name to call upon, even at the dissolution of the world.

220. Sutapa and Prishni performed austerities and held their meditation upon Hari; that same Lord is ours, O Jivana - the unbroken ras (the divine dance) is His boon.

221. If there were no navel, how then Brahma? Without a mouth, how the Vedas? If there were no feet, how then Lakshmi? - O Jivana, this is difference and non-difference.

|| Here ends the Prabodh ka Ang (the Section of Awakening), 4 ||

sections.title_en: The Section on the Unfathomable One
sections.translit:
|| Ath shri Agadhaka Ang ||5||

Kabir aadya ant Hari ek hai | kahan sunankun doy ||
Pala the jal hot hai | jal the pala hoy ||1||
Aad ant sab ek hai | madhya maya vistar ||
Naam sharan jan Jivana | gun mein sab sansar ||2||
Jaise ka taisa Hari | aadi ant sab ek ||
Bhagat manorath Jivana | Hari dharyo gopko bhes ||3||
Nirakar aakar the | adbhut ek arup ||
So Sain hamare Jivana | je Sitapatiko rup ||4||
Nirakar nirdhar hai | aakare anand ||
God khelave Jashomati | so puran premanand ||5||
E rup arupe Shamalo | khele Nand dvar ||
Aadi Omkar upanyo | koti brahmand vistar ||6||
Omkar pahelo Jivana | sundar Shyam swarup ||
So Gokul manhe govaliyo | je Dasharath-kul badbhup ||7||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava | so Gokul manhi goval ||
Aadi Omkar upanyo Jivana | je koti brahmand vistar ||8||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava | so Gokul manhi goval ||
Mor pichchh shir ghunghchi | so Jivan Vraj pratipal ||9||
Aakar kahu to ang nahi | ang bin kaiso updesh ||
Var par nahi Jivana | Hari dharyo Natvar vesh ||10||
Nirgun sargun Jivana | so Brijkul chare gay ||
Sargun Vrishabhanki davdi | nirgun Jadupati Ray ||11||
Ashadh unamyo Jivana | aiso Shyam swarup ||
Bhitar chamke damini | so Radhajiko rup ||12||
Vrindavanki kunjmen | khelat gopi goval ||
So pran jivan mere Jivana | je Vrishabhansuta Nandlal ||13||
Ladu payo Radhika | ang bhari chumban det ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | so sab sakhiyanke het ||14||
Bhakti bharvadan bhavti | rachi pachi ho gaye ek ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | apne man vivek ||15||
Shesh sukhasan Jivana | Lakshmi charan nivas ||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava | so Nand ghar pive chhas ||16||
Kaun bhakti bharvad ki | paye rab aur chhas ||
Gau charave Jivana | bohotek kari uphas ||17||
Has vinode Hari mile | munijan rahe udas ||
Dhanya prit bharvadki Jivana | paye rab aur chhas ||18||
Krishnavatare kamini | Raghupati kino jog ||
Ved vachan kahe Jivana | nari lino bhog ||19||
Pativrata pichhe padi | je gopiye kiyo vyabhichar ||
Has vinode Jivana | milyo purvalo bharthar ||20||
Ladu badhu Nandko | trividh tap mit jay ||
Koi ek gurumukh Jivana | je Hari ras piye aghay ||21||
Ladu badho Nandko | Vasudev dino jay ||
Kodi badle Jivana | ratan diyo dharkay ||22||
Uchhino udhar kiyo | Jashomati ke Devaki ||
Bhur jat bharvad ki | pan samo lino olakhi ||23||
Penda Parbrahm namka | tin lok shir taj ||
Gokul govalo pragatyo Jivana | jine kiyo Ayodhya raj ||24||
Dashe avatare Shamalo | chovise akhand ||
Sab sakhiyanman Jivana | vyapo koti brahmand ||25||
Harie gau charavi Nandki | sab sakhiyanke updesh ||
Prem badhayo Jivana | na jane Shankar Shesh ||26||
Harie gau chari Nandki | sab sakhiyanke updesh ||
Varpar nahi Jivana | Harie dharyo gopko bhesh ||27||
Main dadhi mahi sate Jivana | payo Jadupati Ray ||
Sharir sompu aapano | to lila kaise thay ||28||
So Sain hamare Jivana | jakun Shankar dhay ||
So kali aay pragate | je Gokul chari gay ||29||
Sajan hamare Ramji | je Vrishabhan sutako dhyan ||
Taku dhyavat Jivana | so sajan praman ||30||
Kaustubh mani mukh morli | sundar Shyam sharir ||
Rup rekh vapu nahi Jivana | aise he Raghuvir ||31||
Nayan saluno Shamalo | Radhajiko dhyan ||
Jan Jivanko hirde baso | je Sagarsutako dhyan ||32||
Vaikunth chhandi Jivana | takyo Gokul gam ||
Sol kalasu Shamalo | sakal sevak sukh dham ||33||
Chhappan bhog puran bhaye | payo dudh aur bhat ||
Krishnavatare Jivana | aroge Raghunath ||34||
Purush nakaro jo kare | to nar tede tahan jay ||
Rishipatnipe Jivana | Jadupati bhaye sahay ||35||
Rishipatnipe pahuna | Hari bhaye Jivandas ||
Man vanchhit phal purke | puri abala aash ||36||
Mohe niki lagat Jivana | je gali det goval ||
Char ved Brahma padhe | so mere man kal ||37||
Bharuade bhale bholavyo | chaud bhuvanno Nath ||
Ranchi ek makhan karane | daman bandho hath ||38||
Damodar daman bandhiyo | makhan karan mat ||
Yamala-Arjun karane Jivana | koi na jane ghat ||39||
Damodar daman bandhiyo | jene kahyo je chhod ||
Bandhan take Jivana | kate chorasi kod ||40||
Bhagya bado te Jivana | je Mathura liyo avatar ||
Kaha pankhi kaha manavi | kaha gopi gay goval ||41||
Vrindavanman Jivana | sab pankhi karat kalol ||
Nandghar dulaho pragatyo | ham nirkhat jugal kishor ||42||
Nandghar dulaho pragatyo | mudit bhai sab gay ||
Sham sakha sang Jivana | mukh chumbat kanth lagay ||43||
Bhakti het bharvadki | Gokul charai gay ||
Kansasur maryo Jivana | Ugrasen diyo chhoday ||44||
Kot brahmandpati Kahanavo | so aayo Gokul manhi ||
Ven vajade Jivana | shri Bansibatki chhanhi ||45||
Ayodhyathi aaviyo | Gokul charavi gay ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | hath ghase kahe hay ||46||
Bhakti het bharvadki | pragate puran Brahm ||
Bhakt manorath Jivana | Hari kiyo ahirko karm ||47||
Mohane jag mohiya | Hari Vrajke pran ||
Vrindavanman Jivana | mare morliyan ban ||48||
Kachhuk kangaiman kaman kiyo | shish gunthat Brijnar ||
Tabthe Jadupati Jivana | dole ghar ghar dvar ||49||
Garud vahan Gopal taj | nagan panahi nahi pay ||
Bhakt manorath Jivana | Hari Gokul charai gay ||50||
Ratnakarki putri | aavi Vrikhbhanke dvar ||
Raghupati chhandi Jivana | so Shyame diyo vihar ||51||
Vrindavanman Shamalo | dadhi khay sab lut ||
Brahma chhal kiyo Jivana | navi jugati anup ||52||
Vrindavanman Shamalo | mukh morli ghanghor ||
Sab sakhiyanman Jivana | jay jay Jugalkishor ||53||
Nirgun sirgun Jivana | doy hamare Ram ||
Ved dharmman Raghupati | nirgun gopiko dham ||54||
Nand gharuni Jivana | hasi hasi chumban det ||
Nirgun the sirgun bhayo | so sab sakhiyanke het ||55||
Kar kamal lai Jivana | Kali nathyo Kahan ||
Brij mandal pavan kiyo | ahipati maradyo man ||56||
Jot swarupi vede kahyo | sakal bhakt pratipal ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | so khele bal Gopal ||57||
Vrindavanman Jivana | Shame bajavyo bansh ||
Bhakt het avatar liyo | pragate Mansarovar hans ||58||
Vrindavanman Jivana | dise kshir samudra ||
Sab sakhiyanman Radhika | jyun udghanman chandra ||59||
Vrindavanman Jivana | jit dekhun tit lal ||
So lali Hari namki | Radha lal gulal ||60||
Eh lila tab bhai Jivana | Vrikhbhansutake sang ||
Lalisun lali mali | tab nikaso rang sorang ||61||
Shesh Mahesh sab Jivana | Ved na pave par ||
Tathe sabthe chup bhali | gaiye Nandkumar ||62||
Shesh Maheshwar Jivana | nish din mokun dhay ||
Je ras pino gvalani | so bund na chakhan pay ||63||
Charan parsat taruni dhasi | kiya Kalindi su vichar ||
Huan kahet he Jivana | nishdin Vrajki lahar ||64||
Apne apne anumanmen | sab koi chatur sujan ||
Hari lilaye na rachyo Jivana | tathe dehi masan ||65||
Bhed batayo bhamini | Jamuna bhai do bhag ||
Vasudev dino Jivana | Jasomati param sohag ||66||
Param sohagi Shyamalo | Vasudeve dino jay ||
Gohan badle Jivana | chintamani dino dhay ||67||
Gulmalata ang modke | parsat Kalindi nir ||
Akhil manav bhaye Jivana | sansha mita sharir ||68||
Govardhan Girraj par | rajat hai Brijraj ||
Shakra mahochha mityo Jivana | e bhakt sudharan kaj ||69||
Ke Brij janki raksha kari | ke vacha baddh Hanuman ||
Ke rishi raksha kari Jivana | ke Indra utaryun man ||70||
Gau charave te govaliyo | these aayo pahan ||
Uthai algo karyo Jivana | Indra utaryun man ||71||
Mahi mandal Mathura nahi | adhar nirantar khel ||
Dhara kahat hai Jivana | ta sangat te mel ||72||
Kabir mahi mandal Mathura puri | tin lokman nahin ||
Sada akhandit Ramji | Bansivatki chhanhi ||73||
Dhar adhar sab Vraj jana | adhare dhar ramaye ||
E nirgun sirgun Jivana | Sadguru bhed batay ||74||
Ras mandal Girdhar rachyo | tahan dharo kyun samay ||
Dharo kahat hai Jivana | jahan Sadguru nahi sahay ||75||
Aap vyapak vyapi rahyo | trilok brahmand ekvis ||
E parmanu Parbrahm Jivana | kaha jane Viranchi Ish ||76||
Antar Hari Hari hot hai | mukhse kiyo anurag ||
O nar badbhagan Jivana | Shyame diyo sohag ||77||
Kanak patni karuna kari | batuk vilambi banhi ||
Vraj Vrishabhan bhaye Jivana | Radhe rasik jan jyanhi ||78||

|| Iti shri Agadhaka sampurna ang ||5||
|| Iti shri tritiya vishram sampurna ||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Ang (section) of Agadh, the Unfathomable One — the fifth. (Kabir's sakhis, couplets, addressed throughout to "Jivana" — the disciple Jivanji.)

1. Kabir says: at the beginning and at the end Hari is one; only in the telling and the hearing does He seem to be two. Out of ice water comes to be, and out of water ice comes to be.

2. Beginning and end are all one; only in the middle is the spread of maya (illusion). O Jivan, the servant takes refuge in the Name, while the whole world is caught up in the gunas (the qualities of nature).

3. Hari is exactly as He always was; beginning and end, all one. O Jivan, to fulfil the devotee's longing Hari put on the guise of a cowherd.

4. The formless took on form — wondrous, one, and without shape. O Jivan, that is our Lord (Sain), who is the very form of Sita's husband.

5. Formless, He is without any support; in form, He is bliss itself. Jashomati (Yashoda) dandles Him in her lap — that is perfect love-bliss.

6. This form of the formless, the dark one (Shyam), plays at Nanda's door. From Him the primal Omkar arose, and the spreading out of ten million universes.

7. O Jivan, before Omkar there was that beautiful dark form. He is the cowherd boy in Gokul, and He is the great king of Dasharath's line.

8. From the lotus of His navel Brahma came to be — and He is the cowherd in Gokul. O Jivan, from Him arose the primal Omkar and the spreading out of ten million universes.

9. From the lotus of His navel Brahma came to be — and He is the cowherd in Gokul. With a peacock plume and gunja berries on His head, O Jivan, He is the sustainer of Vraj.

10. If I call Him form, He has no limbs; and without limbs, what teaching could He give? He has no near shore and no far shore, O Jivan — and yet Hari put on the dress of Natvar, the divine dancer.

11. Nirgun (without qualities) and sargun (with qualities), O Jivan — He grazes the cows of the house of Vraj. The sargun is Vrishabhan's daughter; the nirgun is Jadupati, the king.

12. O Jivan, like the clouds rising in Ashadh (the monsoon month) is Shyam's dark form; the lightning that flashes within it is Radhaji's form.

13. In the bowers of Vrindavan the gopis and cowherds are at play. O Jivan, they are the very life-breath of me — Vrishabhan's daughter and Nanda's darling son.

14. Radhika has won the darling boy; she holds Him close and covers Him with kisses. O Jivan, Brahma and the gods are left bewildered — all of this is for the love of the sakhis (companions).

15. The bhakti (devotion) of the herdsmen is dear to Him; steeped and soaked in it, they became one with Him. O Jivan, Brahma and the rest forgot themselves — forgot their own pride and their discernment.

16. O Jivan, Shesha is His couch of ease, Lakshmi dwells at His feet, from His navel-lotus Brahma came to be — and He drinks buttermilk in Nanda's house.

17. What sort of devotion is this of the herdsmen, that He takes their gruel and their buttermilk? O Jivan, He grazes the cows and puts up with a great deal of mockery.

18. Through laughter and playfulness Hari is found, while the sages remain aloof and joyless. Blessed is the love of the herdsmen, O Jivan — for it He accepted their gruel and buttermilk.

19. In the Krishna avatar there were the loving women; as Raghupati (Ram) He held to yoga. O Jivan, the word of the Veda says it: in that form He took the enjoyment of woman.

20. The chaste wives were left behind, while the gopis were charged with adultery. Yet through laughter and playfulness, O Jivan, they found again the husband who had been theirs in a former birth.

21. Nanda's darling boy grows, and by Him the threefold suffering is wiped away. Only some rare gurumukh (one whose face is turned to the guru), O Jivan, drinks the nectar of Hari to his fill.

22. The darling boy grew up as Nanda's; Vasudeva went and gave Him away. O Jivan, in exchange for a cowrie shell he let a jewel slip from his hands.

23. Was it a loan given or a loan taken — by Jashomati or by Devaki? The herdsmen's caste is simple and unlettered, and yet she recognized Him for what He was.

24. The path is the Name of Parbrahm (the Supreme), the crown upon the head of the three worlds. O Jivan, He appeared as a cowherd in Gokul — He who once ruled the kingdom of Ayodhya.

25. In all ten avatars it is the same dark Lord; through all twenty-four He is unbroken. O Jivan, He is present among all the sakhis and pervades ten million universes.

26. Hari grazed Nanda's cows — and that itself was His teaching to all the sakhis. O Jivan, He made such love grow as even Shankar and Shesha do not know.

27. Hari grazed Nanda's cows — His teaching to all the sakhis. He has neither this shore nor that, O Jivan, and yet Hari put on the guise of a cowherd.

28. O Jivan, in exchange for curds and buttermilk I obtained Jadupati, the king. If I hand over this body of mine to Him, then how would His lila (divine play) go on?

29. O Jivan, that is our Lord, the one toward whom even Shankar runs. He has come and shown Himself in the Kali age — He who grazed the cows in Gokul.

30. Our beloved is Ramji, on whom Vrishabhan's daughter meditates. O Jivan, whoever meditates on Him — that one is a true and worthy person.

31. The Kaustubh jewel, the flute at His lips, the beautiful dark body — and yet He has no form, no outline, no body at all, O Jivan: such is Raghuvir.

32. The dark one with the lovely eyes is Radhaji's meditation. May He dwell in the heart of His servant Jivan — He on whom the ocean's daughter meditates.

33. O Jivan, He left Vaikunth and chose the village of Gokul instead. Complete with all sixteen kalas (portions of perfection), the dark Lord is the abode of joy for all His servants.

34. The fifty-six offerings were fulfilled when He was given milk and rice. O Jivan, in the Krishna avatar it is Raghunath Himself who eats.

35. When the husbands refused, the wives went where they were being called. O Jivan, Jadupati became the helper of the sages' wives.

36. Hari became the guest of the sages' wives, O Jivandas. Granting the fruit their hearts desired, He fulfilled the hope of those helpless women.

37. O Jivan, sweet to me are even the abuses the cowherds fling at Him. The four Vedas that Brahma recites — to my mind those are death.

38. How well the herd-woman coaxed the Lord of the fourteen worlds! For the sake of one scrap of butter His hands were tied with a rope.

39. Damodar was bound with a rope by His mother, on account of the butter. O Jivan, it was really for the sake of the Yamala-Arjuna trees — no one knew what He was about.

40. Damodar was bound with a rope; and whoever said "let Him go" — O Jivan, for that one the bondage of the eighty-four lakh births is cut away.

41. Great is their good fortune, O Jivan, that He took birth at Mathura — whether they be birds or human beings, gopis or cows or cowherds.

42. O Jivan, in Vrindavan all the birds are singing for joy. In Nanda's house the bridegroom has appeared, and we gaze upon the youthful pair.

43. In Nanda's house the bridegroom has appeared, and all the cows are glad. O Jivan, Shyam is among His companions, kissing their faces and clasping them to His breast.

44. For the sake of the herdsmen's devotion He grazed the cows in Gokul. O Jivan, He killed the demon Kamsa and set Ugrasena free.

45. Kanha, the lord of ten million universes, came into Gokul. O Jivan, He plays His flute in the shade of the holy Bansi-vat (the banyan of the flute).

46. He came from Ayodhya and grazed the cows in Gokul. O Jivan, Brahma and the gods missed it, and now they wring their hands and cry "alas!"

47. For the sake of the herdsmen's devotion the perfect Brahman appeared. O Jivan, to fulfil His devotees' longing Hari did the work of a cowherd.

48. The enchanter has enchanted the world; Hari is the life-breath of Vraj. O Jivan, in Vrindavan He shoots the arrows of His flute.

49. The women of Vraj worked some spell into the comb as they dressed His hair. O Jivan, ever since then Jadupati wanders from house to house, from door to door.

50. Gopal gave up Garuda His mount; bare, without even sandals on His feet. O Jivan, to fulfil His devotees' longing Hari grazed the cows in Gokul.

51. The daughter of the ocean came to Vrishabhan's door. O Jivan, she whom Raghupati had left behind was given the joy of His play by Shyam.

52. In Vrindavan the dark one eats the curds and plunders them all. O Jivan, Brahma played his trick on Him, and He answered with a new and matchless device.

53. In Vrindavan the dark one holds the flute to His lips, sounding deep as thunder. O Jivan, among all the sakhis — victory, victory to the youthful pair!

54. Nirgun and sargun both, O Jivan, are our Ram. In the dharma of the Vedas He is Raghupati; the nirgun is the gopis' own dwelling.

55. O Jivan, Nanda's wife laughs and laughs and kisses Him. The nirgun became the sargun — and all of it for the love of the sakhis.

56. With His lotus hands, O Jivan, Kanha subdued Kaliya. He made the whole circle of Vraj pure and crushed the pride of the serpent king.

57. The Vedas called Him the very form of light, the sustainer of all devotees. O Jivan, Brahma and the gods were left bewildered — and He plays about as the child Gopal.

58. O Jivan, in Vrindavan Shyam played upon His flute. For His devotees' sake He took birth — the swan of Mansarovar has appeared.

59. O Jivan, Vrindavan looks like the ocean of milk; and among all the sakhis Radhika shines as the moon does amid the drifting clouds.

60. O Jivan, in Vrindavan wherever I look, there is the Beloved. That redness is the redness of Hari's Name — Radha and the Beloved, red with gulal (coloured powder).

61. This lila came about, O Jivan, in the company of Vrishabhan's daughter. Redness met with redness, and then a colour of pure splendour came forth.

62. Shesha, Mahesh and all the rest, O Jivan — not even the Vedas reach His far shore. So silence is better than all speech: let us simply sing of Nanda's son.

63. O Jivan, Shesha and Maheshwar hasten toward me night and day; yet the nectar the cowherd women drank — of that they do not get to taste a single drop.

64. Touching His feet the young woman plunged in, and took counsel with the Kalindi (the Yamuna). There, they say, O Jivan, the waves of Vraj rise night and day.

65. In his own estimation every man is clever and wise. But the one who did not delight in Hari's lila (divine play), O Jivan — his body is no better than a cremation ground.

66. The secret was disclosed to the woman, and the Yamuna parted into two. O Jivan, Vasudeva gave Him away, and Jashomati gained supreme good fortune.

67. The dark one of supreme good fortune — Vasudeva went and gave Him away. O Jivan, in exchange for [unclear] he let the chintamani (the wish-fulfilling jewel) slip from his hands.

68. The bushes and creepers bend their limbs down to touch the water of the Kalindi. O Jivan, all of them became human, and the doubt that belongs to the body was wiped away.

69. Upon Govardhan, king among mountains, the king of Vraj shines in splendour. O Jivan, the festival of Shakra (Indra) was brought to an end — and this was done to set His devotees right.

70. Was it that He protected the people of Vraj, or that Hanuman was bound by his given word; was it that He protected the sages, O Jivan, or that He humbled the pride of Indra?

71. The cowherd boy who grazes the cows struck His foot against a stone. O Jivan, He lifted it up and set it aside — and so brought Indra's pride down.

72. Mathura does not lie within the circle of the earth; unsupported, its play goes on without ceasing. One may call it "earth", O Jivan — but the meeting comes only through such holy company.

73. Kabir says: the city of Mathura is not in the circle of the earth, nor is it in the three worlds. Ever unbroken, Ramji is there in the shade of the Bansi-vat.

74. Supported and unsupported alike are all the people of Vraj; in the unsupported the supported is made to play. This is the nirgun and the sargun, O Jivan — the Sadguru (true teacher) reveals the secret.

75. Girdhar arranged the circle of the rasa dance — how could earth find room in it? One calls it "earth", O Jivan, only where the Sadguru is not one's help.

76. He Himself, the all-pervading, pervades the three worlds and the twenty-one universes. This is the very measure of Parbrahm, O Jivan — what do Viranchi (Brahma) and Ish (Shiva) know of it?

77. Within her "Hari, Hari" sounds unceasingly; with her mouth she made her love known. That woman is greatly blessed, O Jivan — Shyam gave her the good fortune of His love.

78. Kanak the wife showed her compassion, and the young boy hung upon her arm. In Vraj He became Vrishabhan, O Jivan, there where Radha and the rasik ones (devotees who savour divine love) are.
