Here ends the complete Ang of Agadh, the Unfathomable One — the fifth. Here ends the complete third Vishram (resting-section).

sections.title_en: The Chapter of the Womb (The Hidden Origin)
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Garbhavalika Ang ||6||

Kabir sadguru kahe Govind jan | suno garbhagat gudh ||
Nishchal pad jene pamiye | vame sanshe mudh ||1||
Mansa devi upani | tathe bhayo Omkar ||
Ghat ghat vyapak Jivana | so khele Nand dwar ||2||
Aap vyapak hai Jivana | tej jot akash ||
Bin mundka chor hai | sab jug kiya garas ||3||
Aatam Parmeshwar pame nahi | Jivan kaho bichar ||
Shahuchor aage phire | sohi bade vatmar ||4||
Pahela dash avtar hai | duja Vaikunth jaan ||
Trijo Omkar Jivana | chotha ghatghat maan ||5||
Panchma Sanakadik hai | chhaththi Bhagirathi Ganga ||
Satmi ekadashi Jivana | jivkun baura kin ||6||
Sab Vishnu bhakti manhi mile | apne pad lai jaay ||
Motan olavadan Jivana | Parmeshwar nahi paay ||7||
Sapt shahuchor taje | tab Vishnu bhakti ja hoy ||
Tabhi aatam Jivana | male param pad soy ||8||
Jivan e jug parle jaat hai | Omkar bekaam ||
Rarankar nishchal rahe | sada nirantar dhaam ||9||
Omkarse upno | Jivan jug sansar ||
Rarankarse upno | so sadguru ko parivar ||10||
Omkarman aatle | sur Brahma munidev ||
Rarankarman Jivana | je laga sadguru sev ||11||
Omkarke aashre | bhula sab sansar ||
Ramnam bin Jivana | koi na pohota paar ||12||
Akshar akshar ek Jivana | Omkarki aad ||
Mama se raro bado | so sadguru kahyo vichar ||13||
Ek aksharthi Jivana | bhayo brahmand vistar ||
Raro rakhyo harijana | mamo bhayo sansar ||14||
Shiv Brahmadik aade | tin gunke aadhin ||
Ram bhagatkun Jivana | take ghar sab din ||15||
Trigun rahit gunman vase | so sadguru diyo batay ||
Nirgun brahm vede kahyo | so Vraj kul chare gaay ||16||
Nirgun brahmthe Jivana | so trigun bhayo vistar ||
Sakal gun seva kare | so aap rahyo nirdhar ||17||
Ko bhaje aakarkun | ko nirakar nij dhaam ||
Hamare e vrat Jivana | je Sitapatiko naam ||18||
Nij mul nij naam hai | dasi palove paay ||
So ghat ghat vyapak Jivana | je Vrajkul chare gaay ||19||
Shuk Sanakadik Jivana | dhyan dhare akash ||
Bal dware Vaman rahyo | te Lakshmi charan nivas ||20||
Shuk Sanakadik Jivana | jot swarupi dhaay ||
Radha Jashoda uchhange Shamlo | so kharak dekhavat gaay ||21||
Sar Sanakadik Jivana | chhodo Vaikunth manhe ||
Sitapati bhutal vase | sant samagam manhe ||22||
Shuk Sanakadik Jivana | dekhyo Gokul manhe ||
Antar pad chhute nahi | aap rahe sir naae ||23||
Aiso adbad Jivana | je ved bhaye chakdol ||
Shuk Sharad Narad thake | so nirkhat jugal kishor ||24||
Aiso adbad Jivana | jaat paat kul jaay ||
Or baatanki baat hai | jo Brahmadik chale thagaay ||25||
Budho kahu to badhuo | badhu kahu to pir ||
Jot swarupi Jivana | Sitapati Raghuvir ||26||
Sagarsuta charane rahe | sada akhandit jot ||
Ramnam bhaj Jivana | jahan paap pun nahi chhot ||27||
Jot swarupi Jivana | so khele Gokul manhi ||
Naach nachai gopika | pan ade aabhade nahi ||28||
Naam bharunso Ramko | Sitapati Raghuvir ||
Jot swarupi Jivana | Kalindike tir ||29||
Nama to sama rahya | kiyo Kabire bhel ||
Ranke vanke Jivana | kiyo jotsu khel ||30||
Ranke vanke Jivana | sevyo jot swarup ||
So Sain hamare Ramji | je Dasharath kul badbhup ||31||
Janam saphal kar Jivana | bhaj Sitapatiko naam ||
Jot swarupi vede kahyo | pan saryo na eke kaam ||32||
Jot swarupi Jivana | sadhu sadguru manhi ||
Kans nikandan Kahanuo | sab jag taki chhanhi ||33||
Pad chhutya bin Jivana | param pad kaise paay ||
Brahma surnar muni jan | sabhi chale thagaay ||34||
Munijan manav Jivana | sabhi ek bhaay ||
Radha ravankun chhandke | jot swarupi dhaay ||35||
Bali dware Vaman rahyo | to gau charave kon ||
Sab jag bhulyo Jivana | Brahmadik hi kon ||36||
Anhad manhi had hai | jahan Radha ras vilas ||
Guru kripa bin Jivana | sab hi gaye niras ||37||
Sab sakhiyanman Jivana | morli vahi Sham ||
Neti neti nigam kahe | pan kabahun na pave thaam ||38||
Jhalmal jhalmal ho raho | sab sakhiyanko shangar ||
E prem swarupi Kahanuvo | so Jivan Nandkumar ||39||
Ek mukhe ketiek kahun | Vrindavanki baat ||
Sharad Narad thake Jivana | Shankar pakhere haath ||40||
Antarjami aapno | rahyo Jivan so lau laay ||
Koi Himsutane anusare | koi Sagarsutane dhaay ||41||
So Sain hamare Jivana | Sitapati Brijraj ||
Dase sir chhed Girdharo | diyo Ugrasen Vibhishan raj ||42||
Antarjami aapno | sidhi raah chalaay ||
Tuje dukh kaha Jivana | samarne Raghupatiray ||43||
Garbhdhyan chinho nahi | kare harijansu vivad ||
Ant bhandi vado Jivana | kaha rachyo anhad naad ||44||
Utpat praley Omkarman | murakh na samjhe maram ||
Nyare harijan Jivana | jahan sada sanatan brahm ||45||

|| Iti Shri Garbhavalika Ang ||6||
sections.translation:
1. Kabir the sadguru (true master) says: listen, servants of Govind, to the deep secret of the womb - that by which the unshakeable state is attained. Cast off doubt, you fool.

2. The goddess Mansa (the power of mind and will) arose, and from her came Omkar, the primal sound Om. He who pervades every body, Jivan, is the one who plays at Nanda's door.

3. He Himself is the all-pervading one, Jivan - radiance, flame and sky. Yet there is a headless thief who has devoured the whole age.

4. The soul does not reach the Supreme Lord; Jivan, think it over and say why. The thief who walks ahead in the guise of an honest merchant - he is the great highway robber.

5. First there are the ten avatars; second, know Vaikunth (Vishnu's heaven); third, Jivan, Omkar; and fourth, count the indwelling presence in every body.

6. Fifth are the Sanakadik (the four sage-sons of Brahma); sixth, the Ganga of Bhagirath; seventh, Jivan, the Ekadashi fast (the eleventh-day observance) - and these have driven the soul mad.

7. All of these are met with inside Vishnu-bhakti (devotion to Vishnu) and each carries one off to its own station; but they are great screens, Jivan, and by them the Supreme Lord is not found.

8. When the seven thieves-in-honest-guise are given up, only then is there true devotion to Vishnu; and only then, Jivan, does the soul meet that supreme state.

9. Jivan, this age is passing into dissolution and Omkar is of no use. Rarankar (the sound "ra", the Ram-name) stands unshaken - the eternal, unbroken abode.

10. Out of Omkar arose, Jivan, this age and the world; out of Rarankar arose the family of the sadguru.

11. Within Omkar are contained the gods, Brahma and the sage-deities; within Rarankar, Jivan, are those who have taken up the sadguru's service.

12. Taking shelter in Omkar the whole world went astray; without the name of Ram, Jivan, no one has reached the far shore.

13. Letter by letter it is one, Jivan, and Omkar is the beginning; but the letter "ra" is greater than the letter "ma" - so the sadguru declared after reflection.

14. From a single letter, Jivan, the whole expanse of the universe came about: "ra" kept the devotees of Hari, and "ma" became the world.

15. Shiva, Brahma and the rest are subject to the three gunas (the qualities of nature); but for the devotee of Ram, Jivan, all of them are poor men at his door.

16. He who is free of the three gunas and yet dwells within the gunas - the sadguru has pointed Him out. The Vedas called Him the attributeless Brahman, and He is the one who grazes cows in the households of Vraj.

17. Out of the attributeless Brahman, Jivan, the whole three-guna expanse came forth. All the qualities serve Him, while He Himself remains without any support.

18. Some worship the form; some the formless, their own abode. Our vow, Jivan, is this: the name of Sitapati (Ram, the lord of Sita).

19. His own root is His own name, and the handmaid washes His feet. He is the one who pervades every body, Jivan - He who grazes cows in the households of Vraj.

20. Shuk and the Sanakadik sages, Jivan, fix their meditation on the sky; at Bali's door He stood as Vaman, and Lakshmi dwells at His feet.

21. Shuk and the Sanakadik sages, Jivan, run after the form of Light; but the dark one sits in the lap of Radha and Yashoda, showing the cows at the cattle pen.

22. The Sanakadik sages, Jivan, leave Vaikunth behind: Sitapati dwells on the face of the earth, in the company of the saints (satsang, holy company).

23. Shuk and the Sanakadik sages, Jivan, beheld Him in Gokul; still the inner distance does not fall away, and He Himself stands with head bowed.

24. Such is the wonder, Jivan, that the Vedas were set whirling; Shuk, Sharada and Narad grew weary - while they gaze upon the youthful pair.

25. Such is the wonder, Jivan, that caste, sub-caste and lineage fall away. It is a matter beyond all other matters, one by which even Brahma and the gods go on deceived.

26. If I call Him old, He is a young man; if I call Him young, He is the ancient elder. He is of the form of Light, Jivan - Sitapati, Raghuvir.

27. The daughter of the ocean (Lakshmi) stays at His feet, and the light is forever unbroken. Chant the name of Ram, Jivan - there where neither sin nor merit can touch.

28. He of the form of Light, Jivan, plays in Gokul; He set the gopis dancing, yet nothing touches or taints Him.

29. My whole reliance is on the name of Ram - Sitapati, Raghuvir; He of the form of Light, Jivan, on the bank of the Kalindi (Yamuna).

30. Namdev stayed facing Him, and Kabir made the union. To the destitute and the crooked alike, Jivan, He made a play of Light.

31. The destitute and the crooked, Jivan, worshipped the form of Light; and that Lord of ours is Ramji, the great king of Dasharath's line.

32. Make your birth fruitful, Jivan - chant the name of Sitapati. The Vedas called Him the form of Light, yet by that not one task of theirs was accomplished.

33. He of the form of Light, Jivan, is within the sadhu and the sadguru. Kanhaiya, the destroyer of Kansa - the whole world is His shadow.

34. Without the falling away of one's station, Jivan, how is the supreme state to be attained? Brahma, gods, men and sages - all of them go on deceived.

35. Sages and men, Jivan, are all of one kind: leaving aside Radha's beloved, they run after the form of Light.

36. If He stood as Vaman at Bali's door, then who is it that grazes the cows? The whole world went astray, Jivan - and who then are Brahma and the rest?

37. Within the unstruck sound (anahad) there is a limit; and there is where Radha's rasa and play are. Without the guru's grace, Jivan, every one of them went away disappointed.

38. Among all the sakhis (companions), Jivan, Shyam played the flute. The scriptures say "not this, not this" (neti neti), yet they never find His place.

39. All is shimmering and glittering - the adornment of all the sakhis. He of the form of love is Kanhaiya, Jivan, the son of Nanda.

40. With one mouth, how much can I tell of the story of Vrindavan? Sharada and Narad grew weary, Jivan, and Shankar washes his hands of it.

41. The Inner-Knower is our own, and Jivan has kept his love fixed on Him. Some follow the daughter of the Himalaya (Parvati); some run to the daughter of the ocean (Lakshmi).

42. That Lord of ours, Jivan, is Sitapati, the king of Braj: He cut off the ten heads, He lifted the mountain, and He gave the kingdom to Ugrasen and to Vibhishan.

43. The Inner-Knower is our own, and He leads one along the straight road. What sorrow is there for you, Jivan? Remember Raghupati Ray.

44. He has not recognised the meditation on the womb, and he quarrels with the devotees of Hari; in the end it is [unclear], Jivan - why have you become engrossed in the unstruck sound?

45. Creation and dissolution are within Omkar, and the fool does not grasp the secret. The devotees of Hari stand apart, Jivan, there where the eternal, everlasting Brahman is.

sections.title_en: The Chapter of the Longing Woman (Pangs of Separation)
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Virahinika Ang ||7||

Viraha dhunki Jivana | sant samagam manhi ||
Take hirde ham jayenge | jahan Das Kabirki chhanhi ||1||
Virah vimane Jivana | chadh chale sab sant ||
Prem padman mali gaye | jahan Raghupati naam anant ||2||
Virah agan bhai Jivana | man mero patang ||
Sant sangat kathi bhai | tab jalat na modyo ang ||3||
Virah aganman Jivana | diya premka tel ||
Twacha mans tan jal gaya | rahya Raghupatika khel ||4||
Virahini bilkhat phire | samare Sitaram ||
Sant sangat bin Jivana | janam gayo bekaam ||5||
Ja ghat virah na sampaje | ta ghat sada masan ||
Lalo pato kare Jivana | to kyon darpe Jamran ||6||
Virah nahi vairag nahi | nahi prem prakash ||
Swang pahero Jivana | jyun gatranda ghar vaas ||7||
Swapna manhi sundari | ang alingan det ||
Jab jagi tab Jivana | lag rahi take het ||8||
Darshan karan doheli | biraha Vaikunth manhi ||
Ko ek harijan mile Jivana | ham baithe taki chhanhi ||9||
Piyu bin kyun jivie | suno re Sainyan mit ||
Yun biraha bilkhe Jivana | aao Ram snehi kanth ||10||
Viraha viraha sabko kahe | kachhu virahaka sidhan ||
Antargat angithdi | so Jivan jan praman ||11||
Viraha viraha sabko kahe | kachhu virahaka sidhan ||
Ram Kabira ek kare | Jivan jan praman ||12||
Viraha bauri Jivana | jahan harijan tahan jaay ||
Sainyan ghat khojat phire | rahe Ram lau laay ||13||
Viraha bauri Jivana | atur haal sharir ||
Ram Kabira jab mile | tab pave man dhir ||14||
Viraha bauri Jivana | aur sakal sujaan ||
Ja ghatman viraha nahi | tahan bhut pret masan ||15||

|| Iti Shri Virahinika Ang ||7||
sections.translation:
1. Longing has drawn near, Jivan, in the company of the saints; into such a heart we shall go - there where the shade of Das Kabir is.

2. Mounting the chariot of longing, Jivan, all the saints rode away; they merged into the state of love, where the name of Raghupati is endless.

3. Longing became a fire, Jivan, and my mind became a moth; the company of the saints became the firewood - and then, burning, it did not pull its body back.

4. Into the fire of longing, Jivan, the oil of love was poured; skin, flesh and body burned away, and only the play of Raghupati remained.

5. The longing woman wanders lamenting, remembering Sitaram; without the company of the saints, Jivan, the birth has been spent for nothing.

6. The heart in which longing does not arise - that heart is a cremation ground forever. If one does [unclear], Jivan, then why should one fear Yamraj, the king of death?

7. No longing, no dispassion, no light of love - you have merely put on a costume, Jivan, like a widow keeping house.

8. In a dream a beautiful woman embraced his body; when he woke, Jivan, the love of her still clung to him.

9. Hard it is to win His sight, and the longing reaches even into Vaikunth (Vishnu's heaven); if but one devotee of Hari were met, Jivan, we would sit in his shade.

10. How am I to live without my beloved? Listen, my Lord, my friend. So the longing one laments, Jivan: come, Ram, my loving husband.

11. Everyone says "longing, longing" - but what is the mark of longing? A brazier burning within: that, Jivan, is the proof of a true devotee.

12. Everyone says "longing, longing" - but what is the mark of longing? It makes Ram and Kabir one: that is the proof of a true devotee, Jivan.

13. Longing is a madwoman, Jivan: wherever a devotee of Hari is, there it goes; it wanders searching the body for the Lord, and stays with its love fixed on Ram.

14. Longing is a madwoman, Jivan, and the body is in a restless state; when Ram and Kabir are met, then the mind attains steadiness.

15. Longing is a madwoman, Jivan, and all the rest are the clever ones; but the heart in which there is no longing - there are ghosts, spirits and the cremation ground.

sections.title_en: The Chapter of Death
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Kalka Ang ||8||

Kal kabade nisaro | kathi sab sansar ||
Ved kuhade Jivana | surnar khaye phar ||1||

Pita kaleja phephra | sava gajtal had ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | sovat jagayo Kal ||2||

Sikh sakh sabthe bada | khavave ladu bhat ||
Itni buri Jivana | je Jam na chhode sath ||3||

Dhen dhen dhingas mandiyun | khana pina mast ||
Ramnam bin Jivana | Jam karega kast ||4||

Kal kaleja manhe base | murakh jane dur ||
Kal Sitapati Jivana | doye sakal bharpur ||5||

Mala pahere Jivana | nae Andevkun shish ||
Jam pe lat maray hun | yun kahat hai Jagdish ||6||

Galkat phire gosainidi | ham hi sadhe jog ||
Ghar chhodyo jab Jivana | tab bhaye chhatise rog ||7||

Kal kutariye Jivana | sab jag khayo kat ||
Munijan par mitdi | Brahma melyo dat ||8||

Kashi karvat jai le | gale Himale had ||
Baher huto Jivana | so bhitar anyo Kal ||9||

Tarkas bandhe Trikam bin | nahi Sadguru jake sahay ||
Jam kinkar age Jivana | jyun gidad bhaga jay ||10||

Aur mar sab sahel hai | pandit karo vichar ||
Jan Jivan shrimukh kahe | moti Jamki mar ||11||

Divas gamayo bhatakte | sovat gai sab rat ||
Manav janam tho Jivana | pan gayo bhutanke sath ||12||

Manav janam moje diyo | janun hoygo mero das ||
Nar apradhi Jivana | so pade Kalke pas ||13||

Jam dvare Jivana | gade nirghosh nishan ||
Harijanku mil bichhde | taku e sanman ||14||

Jiv jane main jan thagya | sangat dini chhod ||
Tab samjhego Jivana | jab Ravisut padego rol ||15||

Matipanun man manhe | raheshe tarun bapda ||
Jab Jam grahse kesh | tyare bhajshe saghla aphra ||16||

Prachhi pachho na vale | Jam sarikho jor ||
Ram nam bhaj Jivana | kate chorasi krod ||17||

Marun tarun apanun re | kino gharki nar ||
Tabko Kaljug Jivana | betho chula bar ||18||

Kali ayo tab janiye | jab dvare ayo bambh ||
Mide huto Jivana | so bhitar ayo karm ||19||

|| Sakhi bhetki ||

Sakut brahman bhardiyo | Andevko khay ||
Sant sabhase Jivana | kaho je uthi jay ||20||

|| Sakhi Shri mukhki ||

Juthan jagatki khayke | sant sabhaman ay ||
Ravisut age Jivana | nirbhe khasdan khay ||21||

Jahan jahan pandit panv dhare | tahan tahan Jamka vas ||
Sant panv dhare Jivana | tahan Sitapati avinash ||22||

|| Sakhi bhetki ||

Bhand bhavai dumbdi | nat nagar nayaka gan ||
E nad sune Jivana | te Ravisutke nij pran ||23||

Pandit joshi vedgi | kavitane aru siddh ||
Te Ravisut ape Jivana | dharam puriman nidh ||24||

|| Sakhi Shri mukhki ||

Kali ayo tab janiye | vako e sedhan ||
Tan man arpi Jivana | pichhe hane pran ||25||

Sharir paniko budbudo | phutat na lage var ||
Ram bhaktiku Jivana | udharo kaiso gamar ||26||

Hath tali dei Jivana | gayo tarunapo chal ||
Pav palakke panch din | tun vege Ram sambhal ||27||

Budhapo ayo Jivana | shvet bhaye shir kesh ||
Tarunapo yun kahat hai | hamkun diyo videsh ||28||

Budhapo ayo Jivana | kampan lagyo shish ||
Antaryami yun kahat hai | ham samre nahi Jagdish ||29||

Budhapo ayo Jivana | galne lagyo nak ||
Panch lokman pat gai | pichhe nar dekhave kakh ||30||

Budha bhagatkun Jivana | mat koi pati ay ||
Nen ben shravan thake | ab kaise Raghuray ||31||

Tarunape Hari na bhajya | budhape kaisi ash ||
Sarovar suko Jivana | kyon kichad mite pyas ||32||

Bal budhapo Jivana | tarunapo de bahay ||
Ank bank bache sada | chhandi Raghupati Ray ||33||

Mala paheri Jivana | swami honekun taiyar ||
Nar jane karm chhodahu | pan Kal pasare dadh ||34||

Swamipanun salakya kare | huns rahi man manhi ||
Natho na ugre Jivana | Sumeru keri chhanhi ||35||

Tera koi nahi Jivana | jab Jam padego rol ||
Beta beti sahaliyan | sab rahenge ankhan chol ||36||

Gobar khaye jagatko | duniyan den sharap ||
Sant ninda kari Jivana | koi purvalo pap ||37||

Jal bal koyla hoyga | kute pite rand ||
Janam janam e Jivana | Hari vina hoygo bhand ||38||

Navdha bhakti nit nit kare | atam lag akhand ||
Jam dvare Jivana | mar kare khand khand ||39||

Prem thare nahi Jivana | jahan lag atam dharam ||
Jyun pay manhe kanji bhai | mar kare khand khand ||40||

Jam dvare Jivana | sabka chuke nyay ||
Harijan dekhi kam kame | so samajh Janakko dav ||41||

Vat mari jab Vithale | dadhi khayo sab lut ||
Janam mityo tab Jivana | tahan Kal rahyo shir kut ||42||

Dharampuriman Brahmapaur | mahajan diyo chadhay ||
Pahelo pandit Jivana | pichhe pote jay ||43||

Mat pita sab Jivana | mil kar kare kalol ||
Ko kahuka na hoysi | jab Jam padego rol ||44||

Apni apni janmen | sab koi bhaye laulin ||
Apo na chhute Jivana | jyun paniko min ||45||

Apni apni janmen | sab ho baithe mir ||
Ramnam bin Jivana | Jam dvare bhai bhir ||46||

Hari hiraku chhandke | kach kodiko dhay ||
Ante pachhtave Jivana | Jam ghasete jay ||47||

Jara kutti joban sassa | Kal ahedi lar ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | sab jag lina mar ||48||

Jantra bajayo Jivana | bole eke rag ||
Ajamil gunka tari | tahan Kal rahya shir phad ||49||

Mule mithun melvane | kopyo bhekh anant ||
Tun jin darpe Jivana | shirpar Kamla kanth ||50||

Jagat chaveno Kalko | khayo van mukh dadh ||
Harijan ubre Jivana | te keval nam adhar ||51||

Sab jag dhundhyo Jivana | bhai panditki dhad ||
Lakh chorasiman le gaye | na bhai bumb ne vahar ||52||

Ham hi lute Jivana | van viveki sadh ||
Vat chhod uvat chalo | tab Sadgurue dini dad ||53||

Pothi sab parpanchki | akshar lakhe banay ||
Prem akshar bin Jivana | Jam ghasete jay ||54||
Jit tit the mariyo | jem dhani vahono dhor ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | Jam padego rol ||55||

Date phadun khat pan | avar bhogvi chhutse ||
Jan Jivan jani kahun | pan akhar Jamra lutse ||56||

Harijan aye parona | uthi sove rand ||
Jam dvare Jivana | bohot hoegi bhand ||57||

|| Iti Shri Kalko Ang sampurna ||8||
sections.translation:
Here begins the sacred Kalka Ang (the Chapter of Death), the eighth.

1. Death has come out as a woodcutter, and the whole world is his timber. The Vedas are his axes, O Jivana, and he devours gods and men in plenty.

2. He drinks up liver and lungs and the bones a full yard and a quarter long. Without Sitapati (Ram, the Lord of Sita), O Jivana, Death has roused the man who lay sleeping.

3. Kinsfolk and connections are counted the greatest of all; they feed you sweets and rice. Yet so bad is this business, O Jivana, that Yama (Death) never leaves your side.

4. You have set up a loud and showy establishment, revelling in eating and drinking. Without the name of Ram, O Jivana, Yama will put you to torment.

5. Death dwells inside the very heart; the fool imagines it far away. Death and Sitapati both, O Jivana, are entirely present everywhere.

6. He wears the rosary, O Jivana, yet bows his head to the andev (the other, lesser gods). "I shall have Yama kick him," so says Jagdish, the Lord of the world.

7. The gosain (wandering ascetic) struts about saying, "It is I who practise yoga." When he abandoned his home, O Jivana, all thirty-six diseases came upon him.

8. Death is a bitch, O Jivana, that has bitten and eaten the whole world. Her eye is upon the munis (sages) as well; Brahma has laid down that decree.

9. One goes to Kashi and takes the ritual saw; another melts his bones away in the Himalayas. What was outside, O Jivana, he has thereby carried Death within himself.

10. He straps on a quiver but is without Trikam (the Lord), and has no Sadguru (true master) for his help. Before Yama's messengers, O Jivana, he runs away like a jackal.

11. Every other beating is easy to bear — consider it well, O pandit. The servant Jivan says from the holy mouth: the heaviest beating of all is Yama's.

12. The day was wasted in wandering, and the whole night went in sleep. It was a human birth, O Jivana, but it passed away in the company of ghosts.

13. "I gave the human birth freely, thinking he would become my servant. But man is an offender, O Jivana, and so he falls into the hands of Death."

14. At Yama's gate, O Jivana, the drum is beaten and the banner planted. He who meets the devotees of Hari and then parts from them — this is the "honour" that awaits him.

15. The soul thinks, "I have cheated the devotees," and has abandoned their company. He will understand, O Jivana, when Ravisut (Yama, the son of the Sun) makes his rout.

16. Your earthy pride will remain only in your own mind, poor wretch. When Yama seizes you by the hair, then all your swelling will burst.

17. He never turns back once he has been taken — such is the force of Yama. Recite the name of Ram, O Jivana, and eighty-four crore births are cut away.

18. "Mine, yours, ours" — such talk the wife of the house began. From that day, O Jivana, the Kaliyug (dark age) has been sitting just outside the hearth.

19. Know that Kali has come when the brahmin arrives at your door. What was once outside, O Jivana, that ritual karma has now come inside.

|| A sakhi (couplet) of the meeting ||

20. The shakat brahmin (the worldly, non-devotee brahmin) has gorged himself on what is offered to the other gods. From the assembly of saints, O Jivana, tell him to get up and go.

|| A sakhi from the holy mouth ||

21. Having eaten the leavings of the world, he comes into the assembly of saints. Before Ravisut (Yama), O Jivana, he will certainly eat blows of the shoe.

22. Wherever the mere pandit sets his foot, there is Yama's dwelling. Where the saint sets his foot, O Jivana, there is Sitapati the imperishable.

|| A sakhi of the meeting ||

23. Jesters, folk-plays, dancing women, acrobats and the songs of the city's courtesans — whoever listens to such sounds, O Jivana, is Ravisut's (Yama's) very own prize.

24. Pandits, astrologers, Veda-reciters, poets and siddhas (adepts) — these, O Jivana, Ravisut takes as his own hoard in Dharmapuri, the city of judgment.

|| A sakhi from the holy mouth ||

25. Know that Kali has come; this is its sign — a man first offers up body and mind, O Jivana, and afterwards strikes at the very life.

26. The body is a bubble of water; it takes no time at all to burst. Why then postpone bhakti (devotion) to Ram, O Jivana — what a fool you are.

27. Clapping its hands in mockery, O Jivana, youth has walked away. Life is five days of a quarter of a blink — take hold of Ram quickly.

28. Old age has come, O Jivana, and the hair of the head has turned white. Youth says this: "I have been sent away to a foreign land."

29. Old age has come, O Jivana, and the head has begun to tremble. The Antaryami (the indweller) says this: "Still he does not remember Jagdish."

30. Old age has come, O Jivana, and the nose has begun to rot away. Honour is gone among the five of the village, and then even his wife shows him her armpit in contempt.

31. Let no one hold the old man's devotion in esteem, O Jivana. Eyes, speech and hearing have all failed — how will he reach Raghuray (Ram) now?

32. In youth he did not worship Hari; in old age what hope is left? The lake has dried up, O Jivana — how shall mud quench thirst?

33. Childhood, old age and youth, O Jivana — he lets them all drift away. Crooked and bent he remains for ever, having forsaken Raghupati Ray.

34. He has put on the rosary, O Jivana, and is ready to be called a swami (master). The man thinks he has given up worldly action — but Death is spreading wide its jaws.

35. He parades his mastership while craving still sits in his mind. Though he flees he will not be saved, O Jivana, even in the shade of Mount Sumeru.

36. No one is yours, O Jivana, when Yama makes his rout. Sons, daughters and companions will all be left rubbing their eyes.

37. He eats the world's dung, and the world gives him curses in return. He has slandered the saints, O Jivana — this is some sin of a former birth.

38. Burnt up, he will become charcoal, while the widowed woman beats her breast. Birth after birth, O Jivana, without Hari he will be a mere buffoon.

39. He performs the nine-fold bhakti day after day without a break, yet it stays bound to the self. At Yama's gate, O Jivana, the beating breaks him piece by piece.

40. Love will not settle, O Jivana, so long as "self-religion" (piety serving the ego) lasts. Just as sour gruel falling into milk curdles it, so the blow breaks all to pieces.

41. At Yama's gate, O Jivana, no one's judgment is missed. He who shrinks back at the sight of a devotee of Hari — let him learn the winning move of Janak.

42. When Vitthal waylaid the road and plundered and ate all the curds — then birth itself was undone, O Jivana, and Death stood there beating its head.

43. In Dharmapuri (Yama's city) there is a brahmins' quarter, and the great men have been sent up into it. The pandit goes first, O Jivana, and the man himself follows after.

44. Mother, father and all of them, O Jivana, come together and make merry. But no one will belong to anyone when Yama makes his rout.

45. Each one is absorbed in his own notion of himself; all are sunk in it. Egoity does not let go, O Jivana, any more than a fish lets go of water.

46. Each in his own conceit has seated himself as a lord. Without the name of Ram, O Jivana, there is a great crowd of them at Yama's gate.

47. Letting go of Hari the diamond, he runs after glass and cowrie-shells. In the end he repents, O Jivana, as Yama drags him away.

48. Old age is the hound and youth the hare, with Death the hunter close behind. Without Sitapati, O Jivana, the whole world has been struck down.

49. The instrument was played, O Jivana, and it sounded one single tune. By it Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over, while Death stood there splitting its own head.

50. Over a trifle — a little salt to go with a radish — the endless orders of ascetics have taken offence. But you need fear none of them, O Jivana; over your head stands Kamla-kanth, the husband of Lakshmi.

51. The world is Death's fodder to chew; he devours it with neither mouth nor tooth. The devotees of Hari escape, O Jivana, and the Name alone is their support.

52. The whole world has been ransacked, O Jivana; the pandits came down like a raiding band. They carried men off into the eighty-four lakh births, and there was neither an outcry nor any rescue.

53. We too were being plundered, O Jivana, by sadhus without discernment. We left the beaten road and took the rough path — and then the Sadguru granted us redress.

54. All the books are books of deceit; men set down letters and make them up. Without the letter of love, O Jivana, Yama drags one away.

55. He is beaten from this side and that, like a beast with no owner. Without Sitapati, O Jivana, Yama will make his rout.

56. "I will tear the bond up with my teeth" — yet another man must live his karma out before he is free. The servant Jivan says this knowingly: in the end Yama will plunder him.

57. The devotees of Hari come as guests, but the worthless woman gets up and goes back to sleep. At Yama's gate, O Jivana, there will be great disgrace.

Here the sacred Kalka Ang, the eighth, is complete.

sections.title_en: The Chapter of the Brave
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Shuraka Ang ||9||

|| Iti Shri Shuraka Ang sampurna ||9||
sections.translation:
Here begins the sacred Shuraka Ang (the Chapter of the Brave), the ninth.

1. The bravest among the brave is Shyam, the dark Lord; among cowherds he is the cowherd supreme. Lovely in his play, O Jivana, he is the Great Death within death itself.

2. He is Shyam to blind Surdas, Girdharlal to Mira, the bearer of the bow to Kabir — he, O Jivan, is the support of my life-breath.

3. At an empty blast, O Jivana, the coward runs away. The brave man will not leave the field, though he be cut to pieces.

4. An empty vessel, O Jivana, makes a great deal of noise. If there is no bullet of the Guru's word in it, why should Yamraj be afraid?

5. In the brave man's house there is rejoicing; in the coward's house, the clamour of crows. The brave man goes forward to face it, O Jivana; the coward turns his face away and walks off.

6. Of the true hero, O Jivana, the vulture does not eat the flesh. Viraha (the pain of separation from the Lord) itself dries up the body of one who is Hari's own servant.

7. Those in whom the passions keep growing, O Jivana — they are no heroes at all. He whose head falls and who still presses forward, he is a hero in the true sense.

8. The brave man faces the foe, O Jivana, though he be cut to pieces. When head and trunk both go on fighting — he is a hero in the true sense.

9. With bow and arrow he has taken up patience, offering desire itself as oblation to Kanhan (Krishna). Over the head of the servant Jivan stands the true Ram-Rahman, the one Lord of Hindu and Muslim alike.

10. Now I shall do this, O Jivana: I shall set myself against the world. Whoever follows the andev (the other gods) — I shall root out his very trace.

11. The lovely Master Ramji — may he stay lodged in my heart. On the head of the other gods, O Jivana, set fire to their crown.

12. The ancient path, O Jivana, the Sadguru has pointed out to me. A shoe upon the head of the other gods — true is Raghupati Ray alone.

13. A shoe upon the head of the other gods, and a kick on the mouth of their servant — of him who, without the name of Ram, O Jivana, speaks of any second thing.

14. Young and old alike, O Jivana, have the hope of Ram's bhajan (worship). Yet the so-called heroes turn and run, with grass held between their teeth in surrender.

15. There are scoffers everywhere in the world, who talk behind a curtain. Against a devotee of Ram, O Jivana, such a one would even aim a kick at the head.

16. When the war-cry goes up, O Jivana, all the brave take up their weapons. He who while still a bachelor weds the battlefield — his face carries the nur (light).

17. Kabirji is the bearer of dharma, and he goes by his own measure. Like Janak the Videha, O Jivana, he came to redeem the beings of all four kinds of birth.

18. Kabirji, the bearer of dharma, has pulled out the pegs and will pull out yet more. Ramji will watch the spectacle, and will carry a crore of universes across.

19. Ram Raghupati, O Jivana, with brave Lakshman at his side — when trouble falls upon the devotee, the steadfast hero Raghuvir delivers him.

20. Ram's protection is granted, O Jivana, to whoever remembers Raghupati Ray. Anjani's son (Hanuman) and Lakshman are always our help.

21. The steadfast hero Raghuvir is ever at hand for the protection of his servants. Why then not worship Hari, O Jivana — he who gave Vibhishan a kingdom?

22. You will not get it a second time, O Jivana — the joy of a human birth. If you are brave, then make your search for the Sadguru's word now.

23. The brave man rides into battle, O Jivana, and never looks back at the road behind. Shame upon that human being who brings shame upon his Lord.

24. You have obtained the delight of a human birth, O Jivana; such a throw will not come again. Let the player play in such a way that the blow strikes the target.

25. The coward shudders, O Jivana, at the sight of the heroes' battle. Take weapon in hand and ride to the field — then Ram will be pleased with you.

26. The coward shudders, O Jivana, and not one task of his is accomplished. The hero does not leave the field — there where Kabir's Ram plays.

27. If you are brave, O Jivana, then wage war against the senses. He who for nothing makes his Beloved laugh at him — fie upon that sinful, undiscerning man.

Here the sacred Shuraka Ang, the ninth, is complete.

sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter on Love, the tenth.

1. Kabirji is the very form of love, and the Self is the name of Raghupati (Ram). To carry people across, says Jivan, he made his resting place in the age of Kali.

2. Raghupati is sagun (God with attributes), says Jivan, and his servant Kabir is nirgun (God without attributes). The one nourishes the universe; the other's body is the breaker of the qualities.

3. He has no form, no outline, no body at all - such is Raghupati the king. And such too, says Jivan, is the devotee of Hari, who sings the spotless glory of the Name.

4. His own action is his religion, his own form is his own Name. He alone is God's own servant, says Jivan, who remembers Sita-Ram.

5. The two stand equal, says Jivan - kings among devotees, steadfast in battle: Kabirji who dwells in Kashi, and Raghuvir on the bank of the Sarayu.

6. The two stand equal, says Jivan - kings among devotees, refuge of the throng of devotees. There Raghupati sanctified his father; here Ramanand and Kabir did the same.

7. Raghunathji renounced by renouncing; Shyam (Krishna) renounced while enjoying. This device he contrived, says Jivan - one form under two names.

8. To carry the world across, says Jivan, Kabir uttered "Ram." Among Ramanand's disciples, Kabir made Ram his very own name.

9. Three figures stand in Kashi, says Jivan - Shiv, Kabir and Ramanand. All three worshipped the one who is Govind in Gokul.

10. The cowherd boy in Gokul is himself the object of Shiv's and Shakti's meditation. Whoever meditates on him, says Jivan, that good man is proved genuine.

11. Kahanad (Krishna) loved the kadhi (buttermilk broth); he ate his fill of it. At the house of his servant Mira, says Jivan, he asked for a second helping.

12. The charming one drank buttermilk, says Jivan, drank until he was satisfied. With that strength he held the mountain up on his hand and slew the king of Mathura.

13. The servant Kabir reached into the light of that mass of radiance. That Lord is ours, says Jivan - Sitapati Raghuvir.

14. He never proves false, says Jivan - the unfathomable, imperishable form. He who grazes Nanda's cows is the great sovereign of Dasharath's line.

15. He never proves false, says Jivan - the wondrous one, single and formless. He in whom creation and dissolution merge when their time comes: that is Sitapati's form.

16. Finer than the fragrance of a flower is that light of love. It has no form and no outline, says Jivan - and there the servant is granted darshan (the sight of the divine).

17. The gopis drank the nectar of love and remained merged in Hari. Hari's devotees sing of that nectar - what more can Jivan now say?

18. Where the light of love-bhakti (devotion) shines, the four kinds of liberation are ground to nothing. There the servant is liberated while still living, says Jivan - where there is trust in the Sadguru's word.

19. He took an unbroken and generous vow: Sitapati is imperishable. All is the light of Brahm, says Jivan, as buttermilk is strained off clear after churning.

20. Whoever has told of such a wonder, in which there is neither form nor name - without Sitapati, says Jivan, all this is the house of Yama, the lord of death.

21. It is a steep and difficult pass, says Jivan, and much has to be given up. Not even an ant can get a footing there - how then is anyone to reach the far side?

22. Where the anhad (unstruck sound) sounds and the mind stands in unmani (thought-free absorption), there love shines forever. Jivandas is a sacrifice, again and again, to the form of Sitapati.

23. Where the unstruck sound sounds and the mind is absorbed, sun and moon both meet as one. Without the name of Ram, says Jivan, a man only makes sport with death.

24. In Ram's descent the tree was raised; in Krishna's descent it bore ripe fruit. The weaver (Kabir) tasted that fruit - and there Jivan was fastened to the drop of the Name.

25. To drink the nectar of love, says Jivan, is a task that costs one's head. Shesh and Mahesh (Shiva) hold their own rank by it - night and day they take the Name.

26. Gods and sages, says Jivan, longed to drink of that love. But the doubt of the body did not leave them, and so they went away disappointed.

27. Upon the form of Sitapati I offer body, mind and life-breath. Quicker than the blink of an eyelid, says Jivan, one is released from the four kinds of birth.

28. Doubt does not leave a man, O good friend, unless he remembers Sitaram. He who drinks the nectar of love, says Jivan - "saint" is his name.

29. Love and observance do not take root in the heart, though there be many utterances and many words. It is like welding iron to iron, says Jivan, or driving a peg into wood.

30. He broke the discipline of the Veda and still did not gain the bliss of love. What has the Sadguru done, Jivan? The man stayed caught in business upon business.

31. That round of business will end, says Jivan, when the craving of body and mind is let go. Become fearless, O devotee of Gopal, and worship the imperishable Sitapati.

32. In her mind she holds herself a faithful wife, though her husband has gone to a far country - and yet a son is born in her house. Such, says Jivan, is Gopal's teaching.

33. The gopi did not drink of love; some doubt still remained in her mind. Gods and sages began to watch her, says Jivan, and her shadow fell over them.

34. In all ten directions it surged up, says Jivan - dark clouds, thick and thundering. The gopis were drowned in love, gazing upon Nandkishor (Krishna).

35. As the rain-cloud gathers and the papaiya bird's thirst grows, so the devotees of Hari came, says Jivan, in the light of love-bhakti.

36. Both form and name were effaced, and only the light of love remained. Rare is the one who knows this, says Jivan - the servant of God's own servants.

37. Within sagun devotion, says Jivan, lies the nirgun Name of Raghupati. Nirgun and sagun both dissolved, and there remained a mass of love, the abode of bliss.

38. Erasing his own self in the Name, he made him his own servant. So Sitapati says, says Jivan: "He whose hope rests on me is mine."

39. Sut the reciter of the Puranas, says Jivan, and Sanjay, Shukdev and Vyas - above the heads of all of them stands the cowherd woman, where the light of love-bhakti shines.

40. The sugar has ripened, says Jivan, and rain has fallen as milk. All rites and duties came to a standstill when love was fixed on the devotees of Hari.

41. The Name is a savoury dish, and love and affection are its seasoning. Such fare is obtained, says Jivan, when the Sadguru is gracious.

42. Says Jivan: God's servant is seen to be a stranger to the world. Love and affection dwell within him, and apart from Hari he has no other hope.

43. In the age of Kali, says Jivan, the Name found its entry. By it Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over - this is the teaching of all the saints.

44. This is the petition of the servant Jivan - hear it, Kamlakanth (lord of Lakshmi): trusting in your Name, he counts all kings as paupers.

45. At the mere click of the cymbals, says Jivan, ten million karmas flee away - when a devotee of Hari strikes them with love and with no other intent.

46. He has no form and no outline, says Jivan - such is Raghuvir. Sitapati he was from the beginning, but now he has become the servant Kabir.

47. Do not abandon worship and love - so says Jivandas. Any other god is only a jackal seated beside the lion.

48. To serve out food to the whole universe, Ram showed his grace. Brahma and Shankar were left with the leavings, says Jivan - the devotees of Hari pointed the way.

49. Though ten million well-born men of Vyasa's line assemble, and two hundred and fifty million pandits with them, their heads do not weigh against the sandal of the devotee Supach.

50. Without a servant who is love embodied, Raghupati is not satisfied. At the Pandavas' sacrifice, says Jivan, it was Supach who made it sound.

51. Without love and affection, says Jivan, devotion never comes to hand. The whole world wanders about deluded, throwing its arms round the thorny babul tree.

52. Without love Hari is not met - think it over in your mind as you will. If there is no lamp in the temple, says Jivan, how is the darkness to be dispelled?

53. Everyone says "love, love," says Jivan, but who knows anything of love's fulfilment? Drunk with pride they wander about; the true mark is refuge in the Guru.

54. Through love and affection, says Jivan, he took a meal at Vidur's house; and Shabari performed her devotion well, serving him wild berries in the forest.

55. Through love and affection, says Jivan, he bore a great deal of mockery: at the cowherds' houses he drank with relish the buttermilk he loved.

56. Drink the nectar of love, says Jivan - blessed are the women of Gokul. Among the gopis in Vrindavan, Nanda's son dances.

57. To drink of love, says Jivan, gods and sages look on from the sky. Not having obtained the joy that a human being obtains, they weep age after age.

58. To drink of love, says Jivan, Brahma too pondered the matter. Nothing of his lineage or his deeds was undone, and that birth of his was lost in defeat.

59. Through love and affection, says Jivan, he stayed with the daughter of Vrishabhanu (Radha). He himself remained subject to her, placing his mind and his wealth in her hand.

60. Among all the sakhis (companions), says Jivan, Hari staged the rasa dance. He gave them the very fruit their hearts desired and fulfilled the women's hope.

61. In the festivity of Vrindavan, Brahma went away disappointed. The tale cannot be told, says Jivan - where is a hope to be found like the hope of Hari's devotee?

62. Where Shyam and his companions are, says Jivan, such wondrous play goes on that Sanak and his brothers were bewildered and went away sighing.

63. He who merely expounds knowledge is a madman, and he who begs for liberation is a fool. Without love-bhakti, says Jivan, the noose of Yama is strong.

64. The townsfolk gathered together, says Jivan, and debated about love. They made themselves out to be the doers - and Nanda's son was displeased.

65. Whoever practises love-bhakti (loving devotion), says Jivan - into his hands I am sold. My body and mind are his forever; wherever he pulls me, there I go.

66. The servant who binds me, says Jivan, steadfast in the battle of love-bhakti - to that servant I am subject: so says Balvir, the mighty Lord.

67. The gopis became love embodied; Jivan follows in their train. The Sadguru, the servant Gopalji, is the benefactor of all the saints.

68. The gopis became love embodied and remained merged in Hari. Hari's devotees sing of that nectar - what more can Jivan now say?

69. The mind, an elephant, is held fast, says Jivan, where Shyam and his mighty companion are. Doubled, trebled, fourfold, the chain of love has fallen upon it.

70. Kabirji is love embodied, and Jivan has drowned in it. Both name and form are effaced; the untellable cannot be told.

Here ends the Chapter on Love, the tenth.

sections.title_en: The Chapter on the Faithful Wife
sections.translit:
|| ath shri pativrataka ang ||11||

raj virajthi upanyo | udar rahyo dash mas ||
chunchi na chukhi Jivana | nij bhagat Rohidas ||1||
sab nari vyabhicharini | je samare Sitaram ||
pativrata te Jivana | je namrup nij dham ||2||
jarakh vahani jagat manhi | disat hai sab nar ||
Garud vahani Jivana | harijanki panihar ||3||
kapat bhekh Koli kiyo | nrup kanyake kaj ||
o nar bad bhagini Jivana | je Shame diyo sohag ||4||
pativrata meli bhali | kali kuchil kurup ||
pativrata par Jivana | varu koti swarup ||5||
pativrata fate lugde | kanth na ghali pot ||
sab sakhiyanman yun rahe Jivana | jyun udghanmen shashi jot ||6||
patiki gat jane nahi Jivana | so rahe dohagin dur ||
name sakhi sohagni | so rahsi sada hajur ||7||
bagde tako Jivana | je aandevko khay ||
jadip Hari na bhaje | pan aasha anat na jay ||8||
pativrata par Jivana | men varu tan man pran ||
piuki pate sada rahe | so nirbhe gade nishan ||9||
pativratako ek Jivana | vyabhicharini anek ||
o randi rohan rakshasi | jinkun nahi piuki tek ||10||
pativrata mile jo Jivana | main rahun taki lar ||
Lakshman sahit sang Janki | sada unki anuhar ||11||
man jane men pativrata | Hari sune nahi kan ||
lobh mohmen Jivana | shabd na lage kan ||12||

|| iti shri pativrataka ang sampurna ||11||
|| iti shri chaturth vishram sampurna ||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter on the Faithful Wife, the eleventh.

1. He was born of blood and seed and lay ten months in the womb, yet he never sucked at the breast, says Jivan - God's own devotee Rohidas.

2. All wives are unfaithful; she alone is the pativrata (the wife devoted to one husband), says Jivan, who remembers Sitaram - she for whom the Name and the form are her own home.

3. In this world all the women are seen riding upon the hyena. She who rides upon Garuda, says Jivan, is the water-carrier of Hari's devotees.

4. A Koli put on a deceitful disguise for the sake of a king's daughter. That woman is greatly blessed, says Jivan, to whom Shyam himself gave the honour of wifehood.

5. A faithful wife is good even when she is soiled - dark, unclean, ill-favoured. Upon such a faithful wife, says Jivan, I would sacrifice ten million beauties.

6. The faithful wife goes about in torn clothes and puts no ornament at her throat. Among all the companions she stands out, says Jivan, like the moon's light amid drifting clouds.

7. She who does not know her husband's ways, says Jivan, stays far off, an unloved wife. The companion whom the Name has made fortunate will remain forever in his presence.

8. He is ruined, says Jivan, who eats what has been offered to another god. Even if a man does not worship Hari, let him at least not carry his hope elsewhere.

9. Upon the faithful wife, says Jivan, I sacrifice body, mind and life-breath. She who always keeps her husband's honour plants her banner without fear.

10. The faithful wife has one alone, says Jivan; the unchaste woman has many. Those husbandless ones are [unclear] demonesses who have no steadfast hold on their husband.

11. If I meet a faithful wife, says Jivan, I will walk behind her. Janaki (Sita) with Lakshman at her side - it is her likeness I follow always.

12. In her mind she thinks, "I am a faithful wife," but her ears do not listen to Hari. Sunk in greed and delusion, says Jivan, the Word does not reach her ear.

Here ends the Chapter on the Faithful Wife, the eleventh.
Here ends the Fourth Vishram (resting-section).

sections.title_en: The Chapter on That Far Country
sections.translit:
|| ath shri undeshka ang ||12||

chal manua un deshde | jahan Sitapati Raghuvir ||
pun pavitra jahan Jivana | so aayo Kalindi tir ||1||
surat udani gagan par | umdi ja us tham ||
jahan sant samagam Jivana | tahan Sitapatika naam ||2||
surat udani gagan par | fod chali brahmand ||
Sitapatike rup par | Jivan jan makarand ||3||
moj maheraman Jivana | ulatchyo sindhu khir ||
mithe kharo metiyo | jyun dudhe dhoyo nir ||4||
roki rahe nahi Jivana | vani umgi aay ||
Sitapati Raghunathko | naam nirmal jash gay ||5||
chal manua un deshde | jahan Radha ras vilas ||
sant sangat bin Jivana | sab din gaye udas ||6||
chal manua un deshde | jahan ven bajave Shyam ||
Jivan jugte paiye | Vrukhbhan sutako dham ||7||
tun chal manua un deshde | jahan pavan nahin pravesh ||
sant samagam Jivana | adhar unka desh ||8||
ham aaye undeshthi | sab santanke kaj ||
koi jugat na jane Jivana | kaise mile Brijraj ||9||
ham aaye undeshthi | fir jano un desh ||
eh jugat banai Jivana | sab santanke updesh ||10||
un deshki Jivana | me kaha kahu samjhay ||
kahya koi mane nahi | sab duniya bharam bhulay ||11||

|| iti shri undeshka ang sampurna ||12||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter on That Far Country, the twelfth.

1. Go, my mind, to that far country where Sitapati Raghuvir dwells. Where merit and purity are, says Jivan - he has come there, to the bank of the Kalindi (Yamuna).

2. Consciousness has taken flight into the sky; surge onward to that place. Where there is the gathering of saints, says Jivan, there is the Name of Sitapati.

3. Consciousness has taken flight into the sky, bursting through the shell of the universe. Upon the form of Sitapati the servant Jivan is honey-nectar.

4. Joy is a great ocean, says Jivan; the sea of milk has surged and overturned. The sweet has wiped out the salt, as water is washed clean away by milk.

5. It cannot be held back, says Jivan - the vani (utterance) comes surging up, singing the spotless glory of the name of Sitapati Raghunath.

6. Go, my mind, to that far country where Radha's rasa dance is played. Without the company of saints, says Jivan, all one's days pass in sorrow.

7. Go, my mind, to that far country where Shyam plays upon his flute. By the right means, says Jivan, one attains the abode of Vrishabhanu's daughter (Radha).

8. Go, my mind, to that far country where not even the wind can enter. In the gathering of saints, says Jivan, is that country of theirs, suspended without support.

9. We have come from that far country for the sake of all the saints. No one knows the means, says Jivan, by which the Lord of Braj is met.

10. We have come from that far country, and to that country we shall go again. This device was contrived, says Jivan, as instruction for all the saints.

11. What can I say of that far country, says Jivan, to make it understood? Though it is told, no one believes it - the whole world is lost in delusion.

Here ends the Chapter on That Far Country, the twelfth.

sections.title_en: The Chapter of the Religious Garb
sections.translit:
|| ath shri Bhekhka ang ||13||

mala tilak Jivana | e Vishnuka bhekh ||
sharire shobha dekhiye | pan Hari vina pura pret ||1||
dou barabar Jivana | swangi aur sansar ||
bhekh banayo bhagatko | mito na unko aahar ||2||
sabar mathe singdan | aiso mala bhekh ||
jhujh kaiso tahan Jivana | jahan rajbansi nahi rekh ||3||
mala bharunse Jivana | gayo janmaro banjh ||
Sitapati Raghunathki | swapne nahi avaj ||4||
hath katun ta daaska | jo mala bandhe mand ||
Ram naam bin Jivana | bhekh kiyo sab bhand ||5||
mala paheri be char | manman harakhe murkha ||
e gatrandani naar | phokat deve pharadka ||6||
lambo japmalo Jivana | duniyakun dekhlay ||
adha naamsun kaam hai | je Sadguru diya batay ||7||
tilak tulsi bharunse tare | te jug to koi aur ||
ab Kaljug kahe sun Jivana | mere naam bina nahi thaur ||8||
pani pahele Jivana | tun mojan mat utar ||
Ram naam rude nahi | to kyon chhute sansar ||9||
paras bin parse nahi | jyun lohakun pashan ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | phokat bhekh aur gnan ||10||
bhagal vidya sab bhekhman | aap kahave daas ||
Brahmadik khele Jivana | ante gaye niras ||11||
tak trevad Trikam bin | kaiso jog vairag ||
o naar dohagan Jivana | je Shame diyo sohag ||12||
banjh piyare putrakun | hasi hasi mangal gay ||
maat putraki Jivana | mukh mudi muskay ||13||
kaun karmase Jivana | banjh bhai je naar ||
Jashodae jayo davdo | mangal na gaye dwar ||14||
bhekh banayo bhagatko | nahi naam pratit ||
banjh mangal jyun Jivana | aan putra par prit ||15||
sakh shabd ko kare | nahi na Raghupati naam ||
hunsh ghevarki Jivana | ane gaanth na kodi daam ||16||
thagal thigal sab koi kare | do do akshar jod ||
gudli vanaje Jivana | kyun paiye lakh kod ||17||
it utathe Jivana | shikh lai do char ||
aage jai pandit bhayo | so kabahu na pave paar ||18||
man guru charane arpiye | tan he kul pach manhi ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | yun Harijan kahavat nahi ||19||
aiso ajar hai Jivana | jaat paat kul jay ||
aur baatanki baat hai | Brahmadik chale thagay ||20||
hani puni Jivana | sab koi dhare vairag ||
jaise ke taise bhaye | mukh muchh shir pagh ||21||
Kaustubh mani kote dhare | bich bich kukar haad ||
Ram bhaktiman Jivana | Anadev sanskar ||22||
vairagi vivek bin | mange ghar ghar bhikh ||
sarvas Hari de Jivana | jo mane guruki shikh ||23||
juthan chate jagatki | manman dhare abhiman ||
e gurukripa nahi Jivana | jem ghar ghar bhatke shwan ||24||
man mundchyo nahi Jivana | to shir munde kaha hoy ||
gatrandasa dekhiye | nahi purush nahi joy ||25||
mund mundaye kaha bhayo | kaha badhave kesh ||
aapo na mite Jivana | van Sadguru updesh ||26||
tilak dhare de bandagi | lal chhadi le hath ||
e Jam govalo sun Jivana | le chalo sab sath ||27||
jyun nimala puchhka | tyun nimala muchh ||
Ramnaam bin Jivana | aisi modhe muchh ||28||
Ram naam sab ko kahe | apne apne unman ||
aapo na mite Jivana | kyon chhute chare khan ||29||
Gorakh sab jogi kahe | sanyasi kahe Datt ||
aatam dharam bin Jivana | doye baat galat ||30||
Datt digambare kab kahyo | je lambo tarkas tir ||
Kalikalman Jivana | bhekh bhayo bepir ||31||
mans gali gali bhuy pade | twacha haad tan jay ||
man gale bin Jivana | Raghupati nahi sahay ||32||
man maskhari chhand de | Sadguru ray sujan ||
bhut pret kaha Jivana | chhodave Jam ran ||33||

|| Iti Shri Bhekhka Ang sampurna ||13||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter of the Religious Garb ||13||

1. The rosary and the tilak mark, Jivan - that is the garb of Vishnu. On the body it makes a fine show, but without Hari the man is a mere corpse.

2. The two are alike, Jivan - the play-actor and the world. He has put on the garb of a devotee, but his appetite has not ceased.

3. Like horns on a sambar's head, such is the garb of the rosary. What sort of fight can there be, Jivan, where there is no mark of warrior blood?

4. Trusting in the rosary, Jivan, the whole lifetime went barren. Of Sitapati Raghunath there was not so much as a sound in a dream.

5. I would cut off the hand of that servant who makes a display of tying on a rosary. Without Ram's Name, Jivan, the garb has made buffoons of them all.

6. He puts on two or four rosaries and the fool rejoices in his heart. She is a widow - for nothing she flaunts her charms.

7. A long rosary of japa (repetition of the Name), Jivan, is paraded before the world. Our business is with half a Name - the one the Sadguru pointed out.

8. The age in which men crossed over by trusting in the tilak and the tulsi was some other age. Now in the Kaljug it is said - listen, Jivan - without My Name there is no place of rest.

9. Do not pull off your shoes, Jivan, before you have reached the water. If Ram's Name is not in the heart, how shall the world let go of you?

10. Without the philosopher's stone there is no transmuting touch - a common stone does nothing to iron. Without Sitapati, Jivan, both the garb and the learning are in vain.

11. All this garb is a conjuror's trick, and he calls himself a servant of God. Brahma and the rest played that game, Jivan, and in the end went away disappointed.

12. Without Trikam (the Lord) as your reckoning and your resource, what sort of yoga and renunciation is it? That woman is the unloved wife, Jivan; it is Sham (the dark Lord) who gives the good fortune of wifehood.

13. The barren woman fondles another's son and laughing, laughing, sings the songs of blessing; but the boy's own mother, Jivan, closes her mouth and smiles.

14. By what karma, Jivan, did that woman become barren? Yashoda has borne a son, and yet no song of blessing is sung at her door.

15. He has put on the garb of a devotee, but he has no faith in the Name. It is like the barren woman's blessing-song, Jivan - love lavished on another's son.

16. He recites sakhis (couplets) and shabads, but Raghupati's Name is not in them. It is a craving for ghevar (a rich sweet), Jivan, with not a cowrie's worth of money in the purse.

17. Everyone stitches together a patchwork, joining two syllables to two. By trading in lumps of jaggery, Jivan, how shall one earn lakhs and crores?

18. Picking up two or four lessons here and there, Jivan, he goes forth and becomes a pandit; such a one never reaches the far shore.

19. Offer the mind at the Guru's feet; the body stays among the five elements and the clan. Brahma and the rest go astray in this, Jivan - that way one is not called a Harijan (a devotee of Hari).

20. This is a hard thing to swallow, Jivan - that caste, sub-caste and lineage should go. It is a matter beyond all other matters; even Brahma and the rest went away cheated of it.

21. When loss and gain come, Jivan, everyone takes to renunciation; and then they became just what they were before - moustache on the face, turban on the head.

22. He wears the Kaustubh jewel at his throat, and among it, here and there, a dog's bones. So it is, Jivan, when in the devotion of Ram one keeps the impressions of other gods (Anadev).

23. The renunciate without discrimination begs alms from door to door. Hari gives everything, Jivan, to the one who takes the Guru's teaching to heart.

24. He licks up the world's leavings and carries pride in his mind. This is not the Guru's grace, Jivan - it is a dog wandering from door to door.

25. The mind has not been shaved, Jivan; then what is gained by shaving the head? He looks like a widow - neither a man nor a woman.

26. What is gained by having the head shaved, or by letting the hair grow long? The "I" does not go, Jivan, without the Sadguru's teaching.

27. He wears the tilak, offers his salutations, takes a red staff in his hand: this is Yama's herdsman, listen Jivan - he drives the whole herd along with him.

28. As the tuft of hair on a tail, so is the moustache. Without Ram's Name, Jivan, such is the moustache on his face.

29. Everyone utters Ram's Name, each by his own reckoning. But the "I" does not go, Jivan - how then shall one escape the four kinds of birth?

30. All the yogis speak of Gorakh, and the sannyasis speak of Datt. Without the religion of the soul, Jivan, both claims are false.

31. When did Datta the naked one ever tell them to carry a long quiver and arrows? In the Kali age, Jivan, the religious garb has grown shameless.

32. The flesh may rot away and fall to the ground; skin, bone and body may all go. But without the mind melting, Jivan, Raghupati does not come to help.

33. O mind, give up your mockery; the Sadguru is a wise king. What are ghosts and spirits, Jivan - he sets you free even from Yama the king.

|| Here the Chapter of the Religious Garb is complete ||13||

sections.title_en: The Chapter of Anadev (the Other Gods)
sections.translit:
|| ath shri Anadevka ang ||14||

kalpadrum tale baith kar | phod hingoran khay ||
gurumukh hoke Jivana | Anadevkun dhay ||1||
ladsadto lakad Jivana | lage gooda manhi ||
Harike daas kahayke | aur Anadevkun dhay ||2||
Ram bhaktiman Jivana | vali Anadev upas ||

|| Iti Shri Anadevka Ang sampurna ||14||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter of Anadev - the other gods ||14||

1. Sitting under the kalpadrum (the wish-fulfilling tree), he cracks hingora nuts and eats them. Having become a gurumukh (one who has turned to the Guru), Jivan, he still runs after other gods.

2. A stick swung loosely, Jivan, strikes one's own knee. Calling himself a servant of Hari, he yet runs after other gods.

3. In the devotion of Ram, Jivan, and worship of other gods along with it: he longs to eat kheer (milk pudding), but he mixes milk and buttermilk together.

4. He holds other gods equal, Jivan, even while he remembers Sitaram. They may give the fruit of liberation, but not rest at the lotus feet.

5. Raghuvir at your side, Jivan, is like having a lion with you. The other gods are jackals - and shameless men go on remembering them.

6. Jaggery and an ant, Jivan - such is this world. It follows after other gods, forsaking the husband of Janak's daughter.

7. A buffalo yoked to a cart, Jivan - tie it as you will, brother, it will not do. He wants to reach the supreme state, and he bows his head to other gods.

8. Jivan, those who remember Sitaram are beyond the reach of the age. Other men, who look toward paradise, have mouths that are a home for frogs.

9. Leaving the elephant that is Hari, the boor climbs onto a donkey. It follows after other gods, Jivan - such is this world.

10. Speech has been scattered, Jivan; it has burst out in all ten directions. Without Sitapati Raghunath it has become Yama's plunder.

11. What can poor Saraswati do, where the Guru's word is not taken as authority? Without Sitapati, Jivan, one wanders through the four kinds of birth.

12. A nought is set down, Jivan, if I serve other gods. The Sadguru declared the true essence: the real God is Raghupati.

13. My nose is rubbed in the dust, Jivan, if I do such a deed - forsake Sitapati and take the name of other gods.

14. My nose is rubbed in the dust, Jivan, if one runs after other gods - leaving King Raghupati, he makes earth of a corpse.

15. Like watering the root of some barren tree - such is the service of other gods; like plastering a wall with chaff, Jivan. So Shukdev gives his witness.

16. I have searched and searched, Jivan: apart from Hari there is no other. The other gods have their own place, but Hari is the crown upon the head.

17. He offers body and mind to the sant, and keeps other gods in his heart. That assembly becomes a gallows for him, Jivan, though he sits in the shade of the wish-fulfilling tree.

18. It fouls the place and then kicks, Jivan - such is this world. It follows after other gods, forsaking him who is the adornment of Janak's daughter.

19. The greedy priest and his wife, Jivan, eat what is offered to other gods. Their rites arrive at Dharampuri (the city of Dharma), and in the end they are cooked in hell.

20. Licking and lapping, Jivan, he eats the leavings of other gods. He danced attendance on the goddess of poverty, and then Sham (the Lord) turned His back on him.

21. The tulsi is betrayed, Jivan, having taken in the leavings of other gods. Therefore the beloved does not accept it; the Lord has turned His back.

22. The rosary is at fault, Jivan, for it has eaten the leavings of other gods. The creature makes a great many efforts, but the Lord has turned His back.

23. Give up desire, Jivan; now take the Name of Hari. All other gods are only ritual action; apart from the devotees of Hari there is no resting-place.

24. The onion crackles in the seasoning pan - such is this world. And in the midst of it, Jivan, the brahmin who is called discerning: such is his Veda, such is his reflection.

25. Now I shall do this much, Jivan - set myself against the world: whoever follows after other gods, his trail I will hunt out.

26. The Lord, the lovely Ramji, has stayed fixed in my heart. On the head of other gods, Jivan, I would set the skull alight.

27. The ancient path, Jivan, the Sadguru has pointed out. A shoe on the head of other gods - the true one is King Raghupati.

28. A shoe on the head of other gods, and a kick on the mouth of their servant - on any who, without Ram's Name, Jivan, speaks of a second thing.

29. If a lake could be made by the wind alone, Jivan, who would go off to a far country? If other gods could give liberation, who would run to Sitapati?

|| Here the Chapter of Anadev is complete ||14||

|| Iti Shri Bhram Vidhvanska Ang sampurna ||15||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Chapter of the Destruction of Delusion ||15||

1. The uncarved image, Jivan - only some rare sant serves that. Those who flutter after the chiselled one stay without the grace of the Lord.

2. Is the temple image true, Jivan, when it takes the blows of the chisel that shaped it? They set it on a base and fashioned a pedestal for it, and led the whole world into delusion.

3. Seeing the temple, Jivan, delusion fell upon the mind. If a man became a king by offering his head there, is liberation to be found in that?

4. He offered his heads to Shiv, and was given the kingdom of Lanka. It was hell entire, Jivan, without remembering Brijraj (Krishna, the lord of Braj).

5. Seeing the temple he trembled, and worshipped there for the first time. Jivan, the pandit seated inside it - it is he who fastened death upon him.

6. In the temple the bells were rung - water and stone, and nothing more. The pandit is a hunter, Jivan, who shoots the arrows of ritual works.

7. Wherever the pandit sets his foot, there is Yama's dwelling. Where the sant sets his foot, Jivan, there is the imperishable Sitapati.

8. Serving the shaligram (the sacred stone), the devotee of Hari is not filled. If the sant is not satisfied, Jivan, all the service goes fruitless.

9. I do not serve the shaligram; I have no business with the carved form. The Sadguru made me understand, Jivan, the Name of Sitapati.

10. The devotees of Hari are the shaligram - those for whom the Guru's mouth alone is the one authority. All other garb is a mockery, Jivan, and full of holes.

11. The garb is a mockery, Jivan, and full of holes. Know him alone to be a devotee of Hari for whom the Guru's mouth is the one authority.

12. Know her to be a faithful wife (pativrata) who holds to her husband alone. The garb is a mockery, Jivan, and full of holes.

13. He took hold of the tail and the water, Jivan, and let all the holy fords float away. The brahmin who is called discerning keeps it up, and has led the whole world into delusion.

14. Without the religion of the soul a man is blind, stumbling again and again. Making pilgrimages and vows, Jivan, he goes to Yama's door.

15. Kashi has set off for Kailas; the Triveni (the confluence of the rivers) has snapped. In the Kali age, Jivan, the Name of Ram is there for the taking.

16. Kashi set off for heaven, saying, "I have borne many a blow." Now she cannot stay, Jivan - Kabir has taken birth there.

17. Kashi says: listen, Jivan - in the Kaljug the work is not mine. Magahar has become the field of liberation, where Kabir took his rest.

18. Trusting in the Ganga, Jivan, the whole world has gone astray. He from whose feet she sprang - Him they have not remembered even once.

19. She rose from Hari's feet, and her stream fell upon Shiv's head. She came down to the world of death, Jivan - and the whole world forgot.

20. She will go back to where she came from, the Ganga of the bright stream. Without Ram's Name, Jivan, no one has reached the far shore.

21. The Ganga's water is only the water greens are washed in, Jivan, for one in whose heart is Raghuvir with Lakshman and Janaki beside him.

22. The Ganga has gone off to Kailas, to the abode of Gauri's lord. The earth was made pure, Jivan; what remained was the Name of Ram.

23. Trusting in the Ganga, Jivan, the lifetime went barren. Of Sitapati Raghunath there was not so much as a call in a dream.

24. They are all Yama's nooses, Jivan - japa, austerity, pilgrimage and charity. Tossed to and fro between heaven and hell, the pandit has found his rest.

25. Calling himself a devotee of Hari, he bows his head to other gods. That is a false game, Jivan; the Lord of the ages forsakes such a one forever.

26. Everyone speaks of other gods, Jivan; there is some trace of the other gods in them. He who, having become a devotee of Hari, wavers - his house is a cremation ground forever.

27. He points out other gods from a distance, and has himself become an "other god". Where there is no company of sants, Jivan, there is forever the service of another.

28. "There is no other god besides" - and he has made himself the Creator. In this way, Jivan, by his own hand he will go to Yama's door.

29. By reading the books he became a pandit; by reading the scripture, a qazi. Such a one is outside the harijans (the devotees of Hari), Jivan - his is forever the service of another.

30. The mind is his own, of his own making - a limb of the other gods. Without the mind given to the Guru, Jivan, this breaking-apart came about.

31. Without the mind given to the Guru, Jivan, egotism has grown very great. He set himself up as a devotee of Hari, and he drowned in the current of worldly existence.

32. He repeats Ram's Name and stays turned away from the Guru's feet, and calls himself a sant. That will not do, Jivan; such a one is called the son of a harlot.

33. The company of sants does not please him, and yet he joyfully sings the praises of Hari. That is the same as worshipping other gods, Jivan; bound, he goes to the city of Yama.

34. What can other gods do, Jivan, when the Name is the lion (panchanan, the five-faced one)? Crores of jackals fall away empty-handed; no one can overpower him.

|| Here the Chapter of the Destruction of Delusion is complete ||15||
