|| Iti Shri Mayaka Ang sampurna ||16||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Limb of Maya (illusion), 16.

1. The Lord's maya, who from the very beginning ruled all, has now become the servant of the saints - in the sacred region of Kashi, O Jivana, where Kabir appeared as light.

2. The primal maya of the Lord, O Jivana, stands as a handmaid at the saints' door; but to the rest of the world she is the master, riding even upon sages.

3. Someone's wife, someone's mother, someone's daughter, someone's sister - it is all one single form, O Jivana, only the manner differs in each.

4. Somebody's boy, somebody's girl - she takes their hands and joins them; where there was no enmity she has made enmity. O Jivana, this business is nothing but havoc.

5. She has climbed onto the heads of Shiv and Brahma; sages have given up defeated. Only Hari's devotees escape, O Jivana - gods and men she tears apart and devours.

6. She mounted the head of the sage Shringi, and struck down Parashar; but before the devotee of Ram, O Jivana, she became a handmaid at his court.

7. Before the loincloth-girt renunciant she became a slave-girl, though to all the rest maya became lord and master. The one who runs away is not saved, O Jivana, without remembering Ramkabir.

8. Worldly happiness has proved to be a dream; the joy of Hari has neither shore nor limit. Upon His lotus feet, O Jivana, offer up body, mind and wealth.

9. He bears the Satguru's mark, O Jivana, who has rooted out the family's old failing; Radha's beloved, the lord of Sita - there he sports day and night.

10. O Jivana, say "Krishna" a million times, remember Raghuvir always; the body's pain itself is undone if with your mouth you say "Ramkabir."

11. Maya has caused a rupture and snapped the bond of love with Hari; in the guise of woman, O Jivana, a man has become a ghost.

12. She bites gold with her teeth, nectar on her head and betel in her mouth; but without Sita's lord, O Jivana, crows will tumble on that head.

13. Wide awake for gold and silver, in the mind twist upon twist; the age of Kali is a bitch, O Jivana - without Hari it is a great defect.

14. A red-toothed demoness, she has torn and devoured the whole world; Hari's devotees escape, O Jivana, by calling out the name of Ram.

15. The woman puts collyrium in her eyes and fits the arrows of desire; she strikes down sages, O Jivana - she even made Shankar let go of his dignity.

16. With maya, O Jivana, meet and come to terms; she unites Hari's devotee with Hari, and to all others she gives a kick.

17. Maya is our body-self, meant for the body's actions; but our Supreme Self, O Jivana, is Sitapati, the Lord of Braj.

18. "Mine, yours, ours" - this is maya's whole dealing; to Ram's devotee, O Jivana, everything appears as one.

19. The kettledrum of victory sounds over the fifty-six realms for him in whose heart is Hari's name; maya is false, O Jivana - in the end she is of no use.

20. As maya is, O Jivana, know sleep to be the same; these two together have set the soul wandering through the four kinds of birth (womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, sprout-born).

21. Drowsiness is a guilty woman, O Jivana - she sets you at odds with Hari; knowledge and meditation are all forgotten, and of them no news or trace remains.

22. Drowsiness is the shameless one of the soul - consider it well in your mind; if there is no lamp in the temple, O Jivana, how can the darkness be dispelled?

23. Drowsiness buries a man in a bundle, drowsiness ruins a fortress; Hari's devotee escapes, O Jivana, when he seizes the shelter of the Name.

24. Drowsiness turned into wakefulness where the light of loving devotion shone; then all becomes the light of Brahm, O Jivana, like buttermilk poured off clear of its dregs.

25. Drowsiness and sloth, O Jivana, are the two nooses of Yama; the devotee has neither drowsiness nor sloth - seeing that, the Sun's son (Yama) wept.

26. If Hari were as dear to us as sleep is, then in this age of Kali, O Jivana, no one at all would go to hell.

27. The mind went off in maya's company - with delusion, envy and pride; Hari's devotee is delivered, O Jivana, by calling out Ram's name.

28. Bone and gum, no teeth in the mouth - a strange yogini's form; the devotees struck her on the lips, O Jivana, that cheat who had devoured the whole world.

29. They look like drunkards, sunk in maya and in sleep; without Ram's name, O Jivana, the shadow of Death holds sway.

30. In Hari's kirtan (hymn-singing), O Jivana, one to whom sleep comes - Vibhishan's pledge was made to Ram; on such a one delusion can still spread [unclear].

31. In one kind of sleep Kumbhkarn slept, wholly carefree, O Jivana; in another kind of sleep Ahalya lay, holding Kamlakant in her heart.

32. As the gathered heap of one's karma is, know one's sleep to be of that kind; through it, O Jivana, the soul has been set wandering through the four kinds of birth.

33. Sleep is pitiless, O Jivana - it finds no resting place anywhere; but in the heart of the man who has no taste for the company of saints, there it takes its rest.

34. The cold has set in now, O Jivana, and the whole world has gone off to warm itself at the fire; without the name of Sitapati, maya is one great fire.

35. Collyrium in the eyes, O Jivana, bare-headed with hair twisted up, empty hips twitching in display - such is the man who leaves Hari and worships another.

36. She knows nothing of true from false, and goes barking about day and night; the woman is mad, O Jivana - she has gone off with the ghosts.

37. By what karma, O Jivana, did she become the woman Gandhari? Having sent Raghupati away to the forest, she sang songs of rejoicing at her door.

38. Maya is our little country, meant for the body's business; but our mind, O Jivana, is there where Sitapati, the Lord of Braj, is.

39. In the wastrel's house there is no cow and no calf; in the wastrel's house there is nobody at all; there is not a single child, O Jivana - where then would even a fly come from?

40. He dozes and performs kirtan at the same time, as though cutting grass at forced labour; drinking water in a dream, O Jivana - how can thirst be quenched by that?

41. To display herself the beautiful woman puts on the sixteen adornments; those are Yama's nooses, O Jivana - the world has become a trapped deer.

42. Look at the self that lies dozing - its face is like a corpse's; without Sitapati, O Jivana, the misery of Death is not ended.

43. With Hari's hammer, O Jivana, pound maya and break her to pieces; if you worship Hari there is deliverance, and if not, then at least worship Hari's devotees.

44. Let work and household all be snatched away - true is the meditation on Raghupati; in this world, O Jivana, the ones worth looking for are those on whose head is the Satguru's name.

45. Sons and daughters, O Jivana, are just this - Yama's noose; they make a man give up the company of saints. Hold a stone against your breast.

46. Endless forms, endless anxiety, wholly absorbed in maya; with Hari's devotees, O Jivana, always remain in submission.

47. Maya has stripped the pride from heaven, earth and the netherworld alike; but on seeing Hari's devotees, O Jivana, she herself stands beaten and head-bowed.

48. Maya stands there, O Jivana, and speaks words of submission: "Where the elixir of Ram is, O Jivana, in that house I am a humble servant."

49. Maya is ours, O Jivana, when she is near loving devotion; she unites Hari's devotee with Hari, and the rest she swallows up.

50. Maya comes and meets him, O Jivana, and standing there gives her blessing. My one support is Your name - when will You meet me, O Lord of the world?

Here ends the Limb of Maya, 16.

sections.title_en: The Limb of the Sakut (the worldly, un-devout man)
sections.translit:
|| Athshri Sakutka Ang ||17||

Sakutki sabha rachi | tahaan jan bethan jay ||
Ek gohade kyon bane | rojh gadha or gay ||1||
Sakutansu Jivana | kaiso rag anurag ||
Sant sangate sada raho | jake Hari sohag ||2||
Aap svarath Jivana | sakutaan gher jay ||
Nya olgi Hari bhaje | so bandhe jampur jay ||3||
Sakutansu Jivana | kaha kije parsang ||
Kari bare dhoie | kabhu na lage rang ||4||
Sakutansu Jivana | kaha kije parsang ||
Ape bude dharmaan | or sathi le sang ||5||
Sakut sarjya Jivana | so parninda karant ||
Parki aag bujhayke | ape aap jarant ||6||
Jivana jag sab bahe gaya | kul kriya ahambhev ||
Brahmadikse bharmiya | kaha Vyas muni Shukdev ||7||
Sakut mata Jivana | bharte dei bahay ||
Apne svarathkun taki | Raghupati hi ban pathay ||8||
Sakut meheri Jivana | kabhu na kije sang ||
O bhutansu bhatkat phire | hot bhajanmaan bhang ||9||
Aap aapmaan Jivana | sab ho baithe sant ||
Aap mate garji rahya | so van kripa bhagvant ||10||
Sakut bhaiya Jivana | kabahun na kije prit ||
E kel berkun kyun bane | ehi bat viparit ||11||
Aap aapni tapni | tapat hai sab koy ||
Mil kar tape Jivana | jo sadguruka hoy ||12||
Sakut sab kahe Jivana | kachhu sakutaan sidhan ||
Harijansun jutho pade | nahi guru vachan praman ||13||
Pandit padi vatdi | Vishnu bhagatko ghat ||
Jugat jani yun Jivana | mari sakutaan lat ||14||
Kavya chaturai Jivana | bhasha rag prabandh ||
Sakut mrigo mariyo | kal ahedi phand ||15||
Sakutaan sang Jivana | kabahun na kije rodh ||
O apni khalakmaan khushi | tun apno man parmodh ||16||
Sakutse salil bura | kabahun na pave Ram ||
Apne svarath Jivana | sare na eke kam ||17||
Sakutaan taj Jivana | piyo prem rasayan das ||
Papihra jyun piu piu kare | kabahun na mite pyas ||18||
Sakutansu Jivana | het kari mukhhi na bol ||
Salil bhagatsun mun grah | aninsun antar khol ||19||
Sharir sakutaan paraste | gun gaanthko jay ||
Raghupati risave Jivana | to harijan kaise sahay ||20||
Sakut sakut sab ko kahe Jivana | kachhu sakutaan sidhan ||
Ninda karvekun shurma | nahi guru vachan praman ||21||
Jam dvare Jivana | sakutanke juth ||
Harijanki ninda kare | so jamkul bade saput ||22||
Bhat bhalera dekhiye | sakutke sardar ||
Karm gohade Jivana | ghalyo sab sansar ||23||
Bhat bhalera dekhiye | sakutke sardar ||
Kirat banse Jivana | maryo sab sansar ||24||
Yun bane nahi Jivana | avla savli mel ||
Purusha puje Ramkun | sakut nari gher ||25||
Jantra baje Jivana | bole ek hi rag ||
Nandakku nandak mila | tab jane badbhag ||26||
Banki banki paghdi | ne tedhe tedhe nen ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | mukh ghuvadke ven ||27||
Chiknai kiye Jivana | Harki karuna nahin ||
Nirdave nirbhe rahe | sant charanki chhaanhi ||28||
Dhik padyo te Jivana | jahaan na ave Harike das ||
Sakutsu rachipachi rahe | ta kul jalu ghas ||29||
Santko adar na kare | deve jagatkun man ||
So sakut so salil hai | so gurudrohi jan ||30||
Jivat sant na seviya | muve mohochha mand ||
Ochhav nahi e Jivana | e dharmrayko dand ||31||
Jiv na jane Jivana | Ram milanki prit ||
Je rite Harji mile | ehi bat viparit ||32||
Sab taj man nyaro rahe | taje kulki kan ||
Jivana jugat ehi bin | Hari na paie nirvan ||33||

|| Iti Shri Sakutka Ang sampurna ||17||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Sakut (the worldly man turned away from God), 17.

1. An assembly of sakuts was got up, and people go and take their seats there; how can they be kept in one cattle-pen together - the blue-bull, the donkey and the cow?

2. With sakuts, O Jivana, what fondness or attachment can there be? Stay always in satsang (the company of the holy), where the good fortune of Hari is.

3. For his own selfish ends, O Jivana, a man goes to the sakuts' house; he who dances attendance there and (still claims to) worship Hari goes bound to the city of Yama.

4. With sakuts, O Jivana, why keep any association at all? Wash a black blanket twelve times over - the colour will never take.

5. With sakuts, O Jivana, why keep any association at all? He drowns himself in mid-current, and drags his companions down with him.

6. He who is made a sakut, O Jivana, spends himself slandering others; trying to put out another man's fire, he burns himself up.

7. O Jivana, the whole world has been swept away by family rites and the sense of "I"; even Brahma and his kind were led astray - what then of Vyas the sage, or Shukdev?

8. A sakut mother, O Jivana, lets her own be swept away in the flood; looking only to her own advantage, she sent Raghupati himself into the forest.

9. A sakut wife, O Jivana - never keep her company; she goes wandering about with ghosts, and one's worship is broken by it.

10. Each wrapped up in himself, O Jivana - let them all sit as saints; they go on roaring in their own opinion, and so they are without the Lord's grace.

11. A sakut brother, O Jivana - never form an affection for him; how can the plantain and the thorny ber tree go together? The thing is against nature.

12. Everyone warms himself at his own separate fire; but let him warm himself together with others, O Jivana, who truly belongs to the Satguru.

13. Everyone says "sakut, sakut", O Jivana - but what is the mark of a sakut? He proves false to Hari's devotees, and for him the Guru's word carries no authority.

14. The pandit laid out a little path - the landing-place of Vishnu's devotees; knowing that this is the right way, O Jivana, I gave the sakuts a kick.

15. Poetic cleverness, O Jivana - fine language, melody and composition: by these the sakut deer was killed, in the snare of the hunter Time.

16. In the company of sakuts, O Jivana, never set yourself to argue them down; he is happy in his own world - you, instruct your own mind.

17. Worse than the sakut is the salil (the lukewarm, half-hearted devotee); he never attains Ram. Bent on his own interest, O Jivana, not one of his purposes is fulfilled.

18. Leave the sakuts, O Jivana, and drink the elixir of love, O servant; like the papiha bird crying "piu, piu", whose thirst is never quenched.

19. With sakuts, O Jivana, do not utter even one word out of affection; keep silence with the half-hearted devotee, and open your heart only to the single-minded.

20. When the body keeps touching sakuts, the knotted store of one's virtue is lost; and if Raghupati is displeased, O Jivana, how can Hari's devotees help you?

21. Everyone says "sakut, sakut", O Jivana - but what is the mark of a sakut? He is a hero at slandering, and for him the Guru's word carries no authority.

22. At Yama's door, O Jivana, stand the herds of sakuts; whoever slanders Hari's devotees is a great and worthy son of Yama's clan.

23. The bards look fine enough, the chieftains of the sakuts; but into the cattle-pen of karma, O Jivana, they have driven the whole world.

24. The bards look fine enough, the chieftains of the sakuts; but with the arrow of their doings, O Jivana, they have slain the whole world.

25. It will not work, O Jivana - the yoking of the weak with the strong; the man worships Ram, while the sakut woman runs the house.

26. The instrument plays, O Jivana, and sounds only the one tune; when slanderer meets slanderer, then he thinks himself greatly blessed.

27. Turbans tied at a jaunty tilt, and eyes all crooked; without Sitapati, O Jivana, the mouth utters the cry of an owl.

28. For all his oily flattery, O Jivana, Hari's compassion is not to be had; free of claims and free of fear he lives who stays in the shade of the saints' feet.

29. Cursed is that place, O Jivana, where Hari's servants never come; whoever stays steeped and mingled with sakuts - burn that family like grass.

30. He who shows no honour to the saint and gives his honour to the world - know him for a sakut, know him for a salil, know him a traitor to the Guru.

31. While the saint lived he did not serve him, and on his death he stages a grand feast; that is no festival, O Jivana - that is the punishment of Dharmaraj.

32. The soul does not know, O Jivana, the love that meets Ram; the way by which Harji is met - that matter runs quite contrary to the world's.

33. Let a man renounce all and keep his mind apart, and let go of the constraint of family custom; without just this method, O Jivana, neither Hari nor final release is attained.

Here ends the Limb of the Sakut, 17.

sections.title_en: The Limb of the Salil (the Half-Hearted Devotee)
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Salilka Ang ||18||

Salilpe sakut bhalo | je kabahuk pave par ||
Salil buda kichmen | Jivana jaisi jal bin nav ||1||
Salil bhagatkun Jivana | mat koy patiay ||
Kabahun sant sangat kare | kabahu sakutan mil jay ||2||
Hathi buda kichmen | nahin uthanki ash ||
Hath pakhere Jivana | bhavjal bude das ||3||
Kanbi kulman Jivana | vansh na dise koy ||
Dina das bhakti kare | ante fenhe hoy ||4||
Bharado bhagat nahi Jivana | Kanbi or Sonar ||
Adha dhundha hoyga | koe Sadguruke upkar ||5||
Salil sakutan brahmanan | so khade bhelabhel ||
Yun bane nahi Jivana | jyun erandiyu fulel ||6||

|| Sakhi bhetki ||
Sakutan ghar betdi | na byahie Jivandas ||
Vahiko man rakhatan | hoy dharmako nash ||7||

|| Sakhi Shri Mukhki ||
Mit milave Jivana | rude na tadhun thay ||
Sukar kukarko besvo | rat divas mali gay ||8||
Kushal na puchhun Jivana | Harijan na aye dvar ||
Narak sam buro nahi | jam sami nahi dhar ||9||
Kamal na vikase Jivana | Harijan aye dvar ||
Bhath pado te manavi | kaha purush kaha nar ||10||
Chhatisun chhati mile | jake rude Harinam ||
Or duniyasun Jivana | apne kam bekam ||11||
Anin bhagatke jaiye | taj salilko sang ||
Anin majith rang Jivana | salil rang patang ||12||
Bhakti kare nav angsun | atam lang akhand ||
Mukti deuga Jivana | yun kahat hai Kamalakanth ||13||
Man kari kari Hari ochare | tan rahe kul pach manhi ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | so Harijan kahavat nahin ||14||
Ram upasi jo mile | tasun maliye dhay ||
An upasi Jivana | ta mukh dekhe balay ||15||
Bhakti kaisi Jivana | salil sakutan bhel ||
Jaise khara nirmen | pay diya sab thel ||16||
Kabahu bajave dakalun | kab ho baithe sadh ||
Nahi jami asmanmen | jaise untko pad ||17||

|| Iti Shri Salilka Ang sampurna ||18||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Salil (the half-hearted, divided devotee), 18.

1. Better a saakat (a godless, worldly man) than a salil, for the saakat may some day still cross over; the salil is sunk fast in the mire, O Jivana, like a boat left without water.

2. Let no one put faith in a salil devotee, O Jivana: one day he keeps satsang (holy company), the next day he goes off and mingles with the saakats.

3. An elephant sunk in mire has no hope of getting up again; flailing his hands, O Jivana, that servant drowns in the ocean of worldly existence.

4. In the Kanbi (farmer) caste, O Jivana, no line of true devotees is to be seen; they perform bhakti (devotion) for ten days and in the end come to [unclear].

5. The Bharado (Brahmin), the Kanbi and the Sonar (goldsmith) are no devotees, O Jivana; one or another turns out half-blind and half-formed, and if any is saved it is only by the Satguru's (true master's) grace.

6. Salil, saakat and Brahmin - they all stand jumbled together. This will never work, O Jivana, any more than raw castor oil becomes perfumed hair-oil.

|| The sakhi (couplet) of the meeting ||

7. Do not give a daughter in marriage into a saakat's house, O Jivandas; in keeping such a man's mind contented, one's own dharma is destroyed.

|| The sakhi from the holy mouth ||

8. Though glances meet, O Jivana, the heart does not grow cool by it; it is like the sitting together of a pig and a dog, mixing and howling night and day.

9. I ask after the welfare of no house, O Jivana, to whose door the harijan (devotee of Hari) does not come; there is nothing worse than hell, and no blade sharper than Yama's (death's).

10. If the lotus of the heart does not open, O Jivana, when a harijan comes to the door, into the furnace with that human being - be it a man or a woman.

11. Meet breast to breast with the one in whose heart is the name of Hari; with the rest of the world, O Jivana, our dealings are useless.

12. Go to the ananya (single-minded, exclusive) devotee and give up the company of the salil; the ananya's dye is the fast dye of madder, O Jivana, while the salil's colour is safflower that fades.

13. Do bhakti with all nine limbs of devotion, the soul unbrokenly attached: "I shall grant liberation," O Jivana - so says Kamalakanth (the Lord, husband of Lakshmi).

14. With his mind he utters Hari's name while his body stays bound in caste and family custom, and he strays away after Brahma and the other gods; such a man, O Jivana, is not to be called a harijan.

15. If a worshipper of Ram is met, run and embrace him; but one who worships another, O Jivana - to look upon his face is a calamity.

16. What sort of bhakti is this, O Jivana, mixed up with salils and saakats? It is like pouring milk into salt water - the whole of it is thrown away.

17. One moment he beats the dakalu (the little drum of goddess-rites), the next he sits as a sadhu; he is neither on the earth nor in the sky, O Jivana, but like a camel's wind.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Salil, 18. ||

sections.title_en: The Limb of the Adulteress (the Unfaithful Wife)
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Vyabhicharinika Ang ||19||

Pahele pativrata hoyke | pichhe kare vyabhichar ||
O nar dohagin Jivana | karat jar par jar ||1||
Harijan sathe unmuni | gherliyalsun prit ||
O pativrata nahi Jivana | vyabhicharinki rit ||2||
Antahkaran algun rahe | baher dekhave bhav ||
Ve pativrata nahi Jivana | khele apno dav ||3||
Nari varansi Jivana | madda upar mod ||
Ram bhaje nahi bapdi | je sohago rahe bhav kod ||4||
Hari bhakti hanse kare | van pan van partit ||
Dhumar varse Jivana | kyun rat pave sip ||5||
Put jaye bin Jivana | pid na jane koy ||
Vanjh piyare putrakun | nish din bethi roy ||6||
Piu rat jani nahi | or kahave sohagan nam ||
O pativrata nahi Jivana | apne kam bekam ||7||
Ape sohagan ho rahi | or piya na dekhe chhanhi ||
O pativrata nahi Jivana | vanjh rat fal nahin ||8||
Ram bhakti kiye Jivana | manman an vichar ||
Kyon kar puge murkha | Sainyake darbar ||9||
Harijansun ruthyo fare | ane manman moda mod ||
O pativratakun Jivana | Sainya seti hod ||10||

|| Iti Shri Vyabhicharinika Ang sampurna ||19||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Adulteress, 19.

1. She who was first a pativrata (a wife faithful to one husband) and afterwards turns to adultery - that woman is a dohagin (a wife bereft of her lord's love), O Jivana, taking one paramour after another.

2. With the harijans (devotees of Hari) she sits withdrawn as though in trance, while her love is for the folk of her own household; she is no pativrata, O Jivana - this is the way of an adulteress.

3. Her inner heart stays apart while outwardly she makes a show of feeling; such a one is no pativrata, O Jivana - she is playing her own game.

4. The woman is [unclear], O Jivana, and yet sets the bridal crest upon a corpse; the poor wretch does not worship Ram, by which her wedded good fortune would last for ten million births.

5. He performs Hari's bhakti (devotion) in jest, without vow and without faith; when only a mist drizzles down, O Jivana, how shall the oyster receive the true raindrop?

6. Until a son has been borne, O Jivana, no one knows that pain; the barren woman longs for a son and sits weeping night and day.

7. She has never known her husband's love, yet has herself called a suhagan (a happily wedded wife); she is no pativrata, O Jivana - all her doings are in vain.

8. She has set herself up as a suhagan and has not so much as seen her husband's shadow; she is no pativrata, O Jivana - the barren woman's season bears no fruit.

9. He performs the bhakti of Ram, O Jivana, with other thoughts in his mind; how shall such a fool ever arrive at the Lord's court?

10. He goes about sulking with the harijans, with knot upon knot in his mind; such a "pativrata", O Jivana, is setting himself in contest with the Lord.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Adulteress, 19. ||

sections.title_en: The Limb of the Lustful Man
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Kamika Ang ||20||

Parnarisun pritdi | jab tab hoy vinash ||
Ant vichhoho Jivana | hoy jagatman has ||1||
Gher narisun rusno | parnarisun prit ||
Ape samjego Jivana | jab andho athdego bhit ||2||
Nari sathe nehdo | kare so bado gamar ||
Lalopato kare Jivana | pan ant uthave kal ||3||
Nari sathe nehdo | te nar yahan na avsho ||
Apo raheshe tahan | abhadchhet na lavsho ||4||
Parnarisun pritdi | jaiso aganko nir ||
Gharki nari Jivana | shital gher gambhir ||5||
Jarakh lautani Jivana | par triyasu prit ||
Gadho na jane bapdo | jo chandan ladyo pith ||6||
Kukar chate had jyun | bhare larsu pet ||
Aiso jano Jivana | par triyasun het ||7||
Kami kapat taje Jivana | to pame Harika dham ||
Ape ap vagoiyun | pan saryo na eko kam ||8||
Kami narkun Jivana | Hari kabahun na deve thav ||
Bhitar rachi pachi kamini | baher dekhave bhav ||9||
Nari neh ja dakhavi | piyako chit hari ley ||
Bhav jalman bore Jivana | ta par paththar dey ||10||
Jab tuhi dahudash gai | rahu sant samagam sar ||
Sadguru sabde Jivana | utariye pele par ||11||

|| Iti Shri Kamika Ang sampurna ||20||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Lustful Man, 20.

1. Love for another man's wife brings ruin sooner or later; in the end comes separation, O Jivana, and one is made a laughing-stock in the world.

2. Sulking with the wife at home and loving another man's wife - he will understand it himself, O Jivana, when the blind man walks into the wall.

3. He who makes love with another's woman is a great fool; he fawns and flatters, O Jivana, but in the end death carries him off.

4. The man who has love-dealings with another's woman - let him not come here; let him keep his own self over there and not bring his defilement in.

5. Love for another man's wife is like water turned to fire; one's own wife at home, O Jivana, is cool and deep and steady.

6. Love for another's woman, O Jivana, is a hyena's wallowing; the poor donkey never knows that it is sandalwood loaded on its back.

7. As a dog gnaws a dry bone and fills its belly on its own drool - know such to be, O Jivana, affection for another's wife.

8. If the lustful man gives up his deceit, O Jivana, he attains Hari's abode; by his own doing he has disgraced himself, and not one purpose of his has been fulfilled.

9. To the lustful man, O Jivana, Hari never grants a place; inwardly he is steeped and soaked in the woman, while outwardly he displays devotion.

10. The woman only makes a show of love and steals away her lover's mind; she sinks him in the ocean of worldly existence, O Jivana, and lays a stone on top of him.

11. When the cry of "Thou, only Thou" has gone out in all ten directions, abide in the essence, the company of the saints; by the Satguru's shabd (word), O Jivana, one crosses to the farther shore.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Lustful Man, 20. ||

sections.title_en: The Limb of the Brahmajnani (the Knower of the Formless Brahman)
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Brahmajnanika Ang ||21||

Sitapati Raghunath bin | ko kahuko dhariye dhyan ||
Dhua dharhar jyun Jivana | aiso brahmajnan ||1||
Sitapati taj Jivana | rahyo Brahmasu lag ||
Rui mandirmen paith kar | dvare lagai ag ||2||
Sitapati taj Jivana | dhyan dhare akash ||
Pragat godko chhandke | kare garbhki ash ||3||
Pragat Harijan chhandke | dhyan dhare akash ||
Ve jan jug jug Jivana | Ravisutke nij das ||4||
Brahmajnani anusare | ghat ghat vyapak Ram ||
Hamare yun vrat Jivana | je Sitapatiko nam ||5||
Bud panth sab Jivana | jap tap tirath dan ||
Sitapatikun tyagke | je kathe brahmajnan ||6||
Trikuti sanjam Jivana | Brahm jot prakash ||
Sitapati Raghunath bin | svarg narkman vas ||7||
Adhyatam vidya unmuni | kare so kotha khol ||
Ramnam bin Jivana | e sab jamka kol ||8||
Mul dvare edi dai | pavan valove akash ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | svarg nark manhi vas ||9||
Ingla pingla sukhmana | ravi shashi donun mel ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | jamsun karvo kel ||10||
Ashtadal kamal je koi jape | koi dhyan dhare akash ||
Bhaj Sitapati Jivana | Lakshmi charan nivas ||11||
Ankh michine andhlo | dhyan dhare akash ||
Sitapati bhutal Jivana | jahan sant sangat nivas ||12||
Gadhe linde Jivana | papad pitho thay ||
To andevne anusari | jagat mukti fal pay ||13||
Jugat bani e Jivana | sab ho baithe sadh ||
Ape ap thadhe bhaye | janam gamayo bad ||14||
Ghat ghatman Hari lekhve | ape ho rahyo Brahm ||
Mide hato Jivana | te shir par lino karm ||15||
Jyun jalmen pratibimb hai | tyun ghat ghat vyapak Ram ||
Guru prasade Jivana | paie mul chandrako dham ||16||
Sainya seti Jivana | kabahun na kije rosh ||
Ape ghat ghat le rahyo | ape banayo ghosh ||17||
Shruti smriti kahe Jivana | raho nam sharan vishvas ||
Apmate uthayke | bhavjal dube das ||18||
Ghat ghat to Hari janiye | pan Sainya santo pas ||
Dhua dharhar Jivana | tame kaiso vas ||19||
Jan jane Hariki gati | Hari jane janki ghat ||
Aras paras e Jivana | or na duji bat ||20||
Vishva pokhan Hari sabe kare | or vishva pokhe sabe ap ||
Aise vyapak Jivana | kyon mite tretap ||21||
Sain lahe sab jivki | Sainki lahe na koy ||
Sainki lahe je Jivana | jake sant samagam hoy ||22||

|| Iti Shri Brahmajnanika Ang sampurna ||21||
|| Iti Shri pancham vishram sampurna ||
|| Iti Shri Jivanji Maharajni sakhio sampurna ||
sections.translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Brahmajnani (the claimant to knowledge of the formless Brahman), 21.

1. Apart from Sitapati Raghunath (Ram, the lord of Sita), on whom is one to fix meditation? Like a mansion built of smoke, O Jivana - such is that brahmajnan.

2. Forsaking Sitapati, O Jivana, he has fastened himself upon the formless Brahman; it is like entering a house of cotton and setting a fire at its door.

3. Forsaking Sitapati, O Jivana, he fixes his meditation upon the empty sky; he leaves the lap that is plainly there and longs for the womb again.

4. Leaving the manifest harijans (devotees of Hari), he fixes his meditation upon the sky; such men, age after age, O Jivana, are the very servants of the sun's son (Yama, the lord of death).

5. The brahmajnani follows after "Ram pervading every heart"; our vow, O Jivana, is this - the name of Sitapati.

6. All those paths are drowned, O Jivana - japa (repetition), austerity, pilgrimage, charity - where a man forsakes Sitapati and expounds brahmajnan.

7. The trikuti (the point between the brows), the disciplines, the blaze of Brahman's light, O Jivana - without Sitapati Raghunath they end only in a dwelling in heaven or hell.

8. Spiritual lore and the unmuni trance, by which he throws open chamber after chamber within - without the name of Ram, O Jivana, all of it is a bargain struck with death.

9. Pressing the heel against the root-gate, he churns the breath up into the sky; without Sitapati, O Jivana, it is a dwelling in heaven or hell.

10. Ingla, pingla and sushumna, the joining of both sun and moon - without Sitapati, O Jivana, it is playing games with death.

11. Some repeat the mantra on the eight-petalled lotus, some fix meditation on the sky; worship Sitapati, O Jivana, at whose feet Lakshmi dwells.

12. Shutting his eyes, the blind man fixes his meditation on the sky; Sitapati is here on the face of the earth, O Jivana, where the company of the saints abides.

13. If out of donkey-dung, O Jivana, papad-flour could be made, then indeed the world would get the fruit of liberation by following other gods.

14. This is the contrivance now, O Jivana: everyone has sat himself down as a sadhu; of their own accord they have set themselves up, and have wasted their birth for nothing.

15. He reckons Hari to be in every heart and takes himself to have become Brahman; he was a mere cipher, O Jivana, and has taken karma upon his own head.

16. As a reflection lies in water, so does Ram pervade every heart; by the Guru's grace, O Jivana, one attains the abode of the original Moon.

17. With the Lord, O Jivana, never be angry; He Himself has taken up residence in every heart, and He Himself has made all this clamour.

18. Shruti and Smriti say, O Jivana: abide in the refuge of the Name with faith; rising up in his own self-will, the servant drowns in the ocean of existence.

19. Hari is indeed to be known in every heart, but the Lord is present beside the saints; a mansion of smoke, O Jivana - what dwelling can there be in that?

20. The devotee knows the ways of Hari, and Hari knows the inmost turn of the devotee; it is mutual, O Jivana - there is no second matter to it.

21. Hari does all the nourishing of the universe, and the universe in turn nourishes Him; by such a pervading alone, O Jivana, how shall the threefold affliction be removed?

22. The Lord knows the state of every living being, but no one knows the Lord's; he alone comes to know the Lord, O Jivana, who has the company of the saints.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Brahmajnani, 21. ||
|| Here ends the fifth Vishram (rest-section). ||
|| Here end the sakhis (couplets) of Jivanji Maharaj. ||

sections.title_en: The Couplets of Shri Jivanji
sections.translit:
|| Ath Shri Vaishnav Jivandasna Doha ||

Mathura mahalo desh | Kathiyavade katamb vase ||
Aayo Gurjar khand | Santo tane melavade ||1||

Jot julaho pragatyo | Kiyo nam prakash ||
Ved mathi makhan liyo | Pandit pive sarva chhas ||2||

Kalima Krishna ke Kabir | Jene vat ughadi vedo tani ||
Chalyo saghalo sath | Chhipo Pipone Rohilo ||3||

Raghvir dije eh | Jene Dasharath tano daladra hanyo ||
Andha tano aparadh | Nivari nishchal karyo ||4||

Hari haththi ma mel | Aa var aapanpu dakhavo ||
Tote vadhe tuj | Aatam algo kaha jase ||5||

Jam sarikho sadh re | Jota koy dise nahi ||
Aatam tano aparadh | To doshan kahasu dakhavo ||6||

Laj kaha gai rand | Motai masana kam hase ||
Tan jali jase chhar re | Tare saga sambandhi kaha jase ||7||

Bag bagicha chit dhare | Chhand diyo anurag ||
Hari charan vimukh padyo | Svang dharyo verag ||8||

Antargat adar nahi | Mukh kahat hai aav ||
Daman bandhi ladiya | Gadheka svabhav ||9||

Adar van agha dhase | Shvan swarupi sadh ||
Mandir teh masan | Mada dhandhole murakha ||10||

Bhat bhane je duhada | Man motai Mira tani ||
Maram nav jane murakha | Masana jam dhani ||11||

Mira motaiya chhand de | Dhar bandagisu chant ||
Van bandagi kyau paiye | Piu purvala mant ||12||

Aatam ola le | Nigal Narayan tana ||
Panagi pap tani | Bhitar bhijes nahi ||13||

Rajput rano rane | Khatravat vana sahu khatari ||
Nahi Jagdishni jot | Jam ujad deval patari ||14||

Harijanku hushe male | Ninda kare gumar ||
Kot kalp narake pade | Vako var na par ||15||

Guru malyo gumar | Karma eke nav kato ||
Vat malyo vatpad | Vahar deyanta mukh dato ||16||

E daive didho dand | Jug sacharachar bholavyo ||
Jap tap tirath dan | Tame sab jug rolavyo ||17||

Kanto hath Kabirke | Sakal dharma taha toliyo ||
Jap tap tirath dan | Ta mule mitho choliyo ||18||

Kabir kede pragate | Jagma Jivandas ||
Dhaja bandhi dharma dridhaviyo | Jam kinkar pame tras ||19||

Trikam tahare nam | Tribhuvan tatkshan tare ||
Akaran karan avinash | Daman bandhyo rade ||20||

Damodar tu dayal | Jene giri Govardhan kar dharyo ||
Baliko sarvas le | Shu vipra Sudama ghar dharyo ||21||

Damodar daman bandhiyo | Makhan karan mat ||
Jamala Arjun karane | Te koe na jane ghat ||22||

Hari bhajane hushiyar | Pachho pag nar ka kare ||
Bhage kaiso adkar | Je pret joni avatare ||23||

Dant kadhe daladriyo | Hari bhaje jase rog ||
Rahya khand khand mahe vyap re | E bhuta tana sanjog ||24||

Parmeshvar tanu praman | Te sant samagame pamiye ||
Maya moh ahankar | Tethi vedana vamiye ||25||

Maru taru aapanu | Ehane eh aparadh ||
Maya thorki thor hai | Phokat khanche bhar ||26||

Hari sambhare hath bharase | Taharo manavi ||
Maya amulyak mal | Jam machh jhile Jahnavi ||27||

Hu tale Hari nam | Aaphanie tare aavashe ||
Kot janmana karma | Te sant sangat mukavashe ||28||

Indri tana aparadh | Pranme pachha phare ||
Grath na lage kai | To murakh man sanso kare ||29||

Matipanu man mahe | Rahese taru bapada ||
Jab jam grese kesh | Tare bhajase saghala aaphara ||30||

Aapo aatama aap | Jam sadguru charane ugare ||
Tare nathi kaso bhar | Jam marjivo dariye pade ||31||

Manani moti uk | Janu mune Madhav male ||
To Prahlad keso aparadh | Je sant sangatma nav bhale ||32||

E shu kidhu andh | E samvad te shane karo ||
Chhari Hari motai | Jiv motai ko ugaro ||33||

Hari kirtan hushe kare | Hansi kare gumar ||
Hathi kero navano | Mathe ghale chhar ||34||

Parbrahmsu kare prit | Aatam sudho she na kare ||
Marvu chhe nirvan | To andha algo shu phare ||35||

Khoto e sansar | Manma nayan na aavate ||
Ko mehari ko may | Em sahu ko pachi mare ||36||

An bole to aapharo | Bahu bole bahu karma ||
Hasi bole Hari dassu | To kahiye gurugam ||37||

Jo Hari bhagtansu het | To nagan hoy nachavo ||
To chhute sansar | Nahintar kanye pachi mare ||38||

Kukar kotak var | Aa var manav avataro ||
Ram bhaje to par | Nahintar ehaj avasaro ||39||

Udharo kaiso abujh | Jo guru sabad shravane sunyo ||
Kori dharti bij | Pan meh vuthe mahi ma phalyo ||40||

Ochhi nadi nir | Bhadarve sabe bhari ||
Tyu kal kaleja mahe | Maram na jane manavi ||41||

Vichhan tano vivachar | Mritti mahethi upaje ||
Maram na jane kai | Achet budhe thayo andhalo ||42||

Kukar kapali ka kare | Ram kahene sadh ||
Pet tana parpanch | Sikh sakha upadh ||43||

Bhajananand bhule pade | Sanakadik dei sadh ||
Ajamil kushal padi | Gaj gunaka aur vyadh ||44||

Duniya sab daladri bhai | Hari chali Hari nam ||
Dasi kero betado | Kun palav pakade Sham ||45||

Makhan chhande murakha | Valove sarav chhan ||
Nam Gangodak chhar kare | Mutar kare osan ||46||

Matha upar mand | Jam chhatra chhaya kare ||
Janu motero thay | Kaj amaru to sare ||47||

Kukar katako nankhate | Shu purvaj tara pamashe ||
Harijansu kar het | Je vedana saghali vamashe ||48||

Davo kare so daladri | Rude nahi vishvas ||
Ek nardave Narhar bhaje | So kahie nij das ||49||

Suto saghalo sath | Dharan mahe ghughuve ||
Rakha kare Rughnath | Upar jam kankar phare ||50||

Matha upar mand | Jam kankar chhaya kare ||
Jane motero thay | Kaj amaru to sare ||51||

Malatu malatu aane | An malatu arano kare ||
Avali savali ser | Phogat ka e pachi mare ||52||

Mata to Sita khari | Or mata maho mai ||
Agha le bolayke | Pichhe mele khai ||53||

Mat bhai kamat | Bandhav bel koi nahi ||
Put bhayo kaput | Kul lajayo kamani ||54||

Katamb dise kod | Pan Sham snehi koi nahi ||
Ka e abhadave aap | Bheti murakh manavi ||55||

Andhare ujed | Je sant samagam manavo ||
Ujede andhakar | Je aandevsu manavo ||56||

Murakh nahe Jahnavi | Aabhadchhet algi kare ||
Aabhadchhet aapa mahe | Tuj sarikhado tetale ||57||

Nari sathe neh | Te nar yaha na aavasho ||
Aapo rahese taha | Aabhadchhet na laavasho ||58||

Nari nirbal rup chhe | Pan puri parpanch mahi ||
Sant virodhe kubada | Puri chhandi tahi ||59||

Nari narsu ruthi phire | Bhagtansu virodh ||
Nathi kahi na ugare | Jam pendelo khoj ||60||

Sapan jaise phuphave | Nari murakh mudh ||
Je je vachan nikase | Te padase tahane mund ||61||

Puthe apradhan ka padi | Murakh nar achetan ||
Sant sangat Hari bhajan bin | Bhale jamake khet ||62||

Nari neh na todiye | Bhala bura tohe kanth ||
Pativrata piuku bhaje | Vyabhichari anant ||63||

Nari kidhi tag | Mundiye karyu matipanu ||
Pichhe aave vaj | Je antaskaran mahethi utari ||64||

brahman na dije bethne | prit de lagay ||145||
kunkumka tika kiya | bhardako so ang ||
kulkarni chhute nahi | jyun bhagtan bhele bhand ||146||
tirath sab sanse padyan | jan ave mat koy manhe ||
karma hamne lagsi | jo pade viprki chhanhe ||147||
anant kot vasidado | sakal pakhka mul ||
narsingh ghat ghat pekhiye | gaya te sanse sul ||148||
sapt dvip navkhandlu | vyapak jaka rup ||
shankh chakra su dekhiye | narsingh anopam rup ||149||
narsingh nirbhe sitapati | manman soch bichar ||
bharme bhulyo atma | pan sadguru sabde par ||150||
narsingh nirbhe koy nahi | jake bhram guncha bhel ||
sab kari dese ekatun | jaise ghritman tel ||151||
prahlad kaj pravesh | khambhman khunkhariyo ||
na ayo bhagtansu bhid | shun budho thayo ke hari gayo ||152||
sabki jivan ramji | ram santanke das ||
e barad tabko liyo | jab narsingh bhaye prakash ||153||
shankhasur karan shurmo | peth gayo patal ||
nir udadyo puchh kar | tab dariye mani har ||154||
dhruv avichal raj | ekvisme brahmand tape ||
sant tano mahimay | e kahiye mahatam te khape ||155||
kalo muhdo kan e | hanuman taro kyam thayo ||
e lagyo apradh | je natarang jova rahyo ||156||
ram kahat shi laj | mukhthi na bole murkha ||
jare jam grahese kesh | kem bubadi padesh bapda ||157||
shaligram seve sada | man kherka khut ||
atho por lado paro | jyun maruko unt ||158||
sakhi sabdi het kar | mil kar gaiye git ||
rab roto mil paiye | e parmeshwarni prit ||159||
panthi chalyo panthsir | joi godad khat ||
pau palakke panch dinman | uth chalege bat ||160||
ghano na ghales bhar | brahman vaniya dubla ||
am tan kaise jor | sahej sanjage je mala ||163||
vaniyo kare vyapar | agho pachho osre ||
kripanath kripal | jane male nav male ||162||
je ape adar kari | god pasari leu ||
vast thorki thor hai | trikha hoy so piu ||163||
bhikhari bhagvantka | tuka de so khau ||
man apman kachhu nahi | harkhe hari gun gau ||164||
mala tilak tano mahimay | tribhuvanman sancharyo ||
janak jam tano vivad | tare e pragat karyo ||165||
mala pahere ek | bahu mala te shun kare ||
bhramar jive sab vas | phul khay te aphare ||166||
tadh nashe tapne | tem hari name apradh ||
rat divas na meliye | sant samagam sadh ||167||
gadh lidho kahe gumar | chhatrapati ko na vaso ||
sarav sarikhdo sath | ek bhastan sahu bhaso ||168||
baher tyagi dekhiye | manhe mayani bhukh ||
do do batan kyun bane | jam golman chuk ||169||
maya brahma nahi jujvan | jyun paniman dudh ||
murakh pive ek kari | koy sant valove sudh ||170||
padmani pichhe padi | kubja agel kod ||
tuti luli pangli | pan pakdi hariki ot ||171||
mansa devi upni | tathe bhayo omkar ||
ghat ghat hari vyapi rahyo | so khele nand dvar ||172||
brahma ved vistar te | shukdev shrimukh boliyo ||
nirakar nij rup | so dvare dvare doliyo ||173||
damodar dayal | je ap bandhave damne ||
jamla arjan karne | bandhyo bandh ja chhodve ||174||
bijo kalo barne | kale kalo je tare ||
kalo kamlakanth | kale kele ko tare ||175||
baiyan biji var | nahi ave aiso davdo ||
maya malse kani var | pan nahi hoy sant melavdo ||176||
kahane kidhu kaher | al sarikho aniyo ||
sahuko jane pindar | pan tribhuvannath na janiyo ||177||
baio kero betdo | dhoyo pana bai ||
kali kutumbman jivna | vaishnavjini sagai ||178||
thorun bolethi rahese | vade so avichal ven ||
dridh kachha kar varsna | sakhi tohe tharanda nen ||179||
uttam jansu prit kar | jyun prem badhanto thay ||
nich sangat akhar sabad | so ghatat ghatat ghat jay ||180||

|| iti shri vaishnav jivandasji na doha sampurna ||
sections.translation:
Heading: Here begin the dohas (couplets) of Shri Vaishnav Jivandas.

1. The land [of his origin] lies within Mathura; his family dwells in Kathiawad. He came to the Gujarat region, to the gathering-place of the saints.

2. The Light appeared as the weaver [Kabir]; he made the Name shine out. He churned the Vedas and took the butter, while the pandits all drink the buttermilk.

3. In the Kali age Krishna is Kabir, who threw open the road of the Vedas. The whole company walked it after him: Chhipo (the cloth-printer), Pipo and Rohilo.

4. Give this [praise] to Raghuvir, who destroyed Dasharath's destitution. He warded off the offence against the blind ones and made [him] unshaken.

5. Do not let go of Hari's hand; this time show that you are His own. If you fall short, the loss grows against you — where can the soul go, apart [from Him]?

6. Look where you will, no sadhu of that measure is seen anywhere. The offence belongs to the soul itself — so on whom will you lay the blame?

7. Where has your shame gone, wretched one? What use is greatness at the burning-ground? The body will burn to ashes — where then will your kin and relations be?

8. He sets his mind on gardens and groves and has cast off loving devotion. He has fallen away from Hari's feet and put on renunciation as a costume.

9. Within there is no respect, yet the mouth says, "Come in." Roped up and loaded with burdens — that is the donkey's nature.

10. Unhonoured, he pushes himself forward — a sadhu in the shape of a dog. That temple of his is a burning-ground; the fool rummages among corpses.

11. The bard recites his couplets, his mind full of the grandeur of a lord. The fool does not know the secret: he is master only of the burning-ground.

12. O lord, give up your grandeurs; set your thought on worship. Without worship, how is it to be gained — the Beloved, the ancient mantra?

13. Let the soul take shelter — [nigal, unclear] that of Narayan. Then the scum of sin will not soak you within.

14. A Rajput lord stands in battle; without true kshatriya-hood all his assurance is empty. Where the light of Jagdish (Lord of the world) is absent, it is like a dancing-girl in a deserted temple.

15. [One man] meets Hari's devotees with eagerness; the arrogant one slanders them. He falls into hell for a crore of kalpas — for him there is neither shore nor end.

16. He found a guru who was himself arrogant, and not one karma was cut away. On the road he met a highway robber, and while he cried for help his mouth was stopped.

17. Fate has laid down this penalty: the whole world, moving and unmoving, has been deluded. In japa, austerity, pilgrimage and charity the whole age has been tumbled about.

18. The balance is in Kabir's hand, and there all the dharmas were weighed. Japa, austerity, pilgrimage and charity — at their root the sweet [Name] was sifted out [choliyo, unclear].

19. After Kabir, Jivandas appeared in the world. He raised the banner and made dharma firm, and Yama's servants are seized with terror.

20. O Trikam (Krishna), by your Name the three worlds cross over in an instant. Doer of the undoable, imperishable One — bound with a rope, you wept.

21. Damodar, you are compassionate, you who held up Mount Govardhan on your hand. You took away the whole of Bali's wealth — and what did the brahmin Sudama keep in his house?

22. His mother bound Damodar with a rope for the sake of butter. It was for the sake of the twin Arjuna trees; no one knew that design.

23. Be alert in the worship of Hari; why does a man draw his foot back? What claim is left in his lot, who is born into the ghost-birth?

24. The wretched one bares his teeth [in mockery]; but worship Hari, and the disease will go. It has spread through region after region — this is the company of ghosts.

25. The proof of the Supreme Lord is obtained in the company of saints. Maya, delusion and egotism — the anguish that comes of them is cast away.

26. "Mine, yours, ours" — this very thing is the offence. Maya stays in its own place; for nothing a man drags the load.

27. Remember Hari and your hands will be filled, O man of His. Maya is merchandise of no worth — [live] as the fish swims in the Ganga.

28. When "I" is removed, Hari's Name will come to you of its own accord. The karmas of a crore of births — the company of saints will make you lay them down.

29. The offences of the senses turn back before a bow of salutation. Not a knot of it clings to you — yet the fool's mind goes on doubting.

30. Your self-importance will stay only inside your own mind, poor wretch. When Yama seizes you by the hair, all your swagger will break.

31. Give your own self away, as one is saved at the Sadguru's feet. Then there is no weight upon you, as the pearl-diver plunges into the sea.

32. The mind's great longing is, "may Madhav meet me." Then what offence was Prahlad's? [unclear] — he who does not mingle in the company of saints [gains nothing].

33. What have you done, blind one? Why do you carry on this argument? Having thrown away Hari's greatness, who was ever saved by the greatness of the jiva (individual soul)?

34. [One man] sings Hari's kirtan (hymn) with joy; the arrogant one laughs at it. It is like an elephant's bath — afterwards it throws dust on its own head.

35. Make love with Parbrahma (the Supreme); why not make the soul straight? Death at the end is certain — then, blind one, why do you wander apart?

36. This world is false, yet it does not settle in the mind or before the eye. One says "my wife", another "my mother" — and so everyone frets himself to death.

37. If he does not speak, it is stiff pride; if he speaks much, it is much karma. If he speaks smilingly with Hari's servants, then we call it gurugam (the understanding received from the guru).

38. If you have love for Hari's devotees, then dance stripped bare [of pride]. Then the world lets go of you; otherwise why fret yourself to death?

39. A crore of times you were born a dog; this time you are born a man. Worship Ram and you cross over; otherwise this was your one chance.

40. What deliverance is there for the dull one, though he heard the guru's word with his own ears? [It is] seed on dry ground: the rain fell, but nothing bore fruit in the earth.

41. A river low in water is brimful in the month of Bhadarva. So death sits within the heart, and man does not know the secret.

42. Consider the scorpion: it is born out of the earth itself. [Man] knows nothing of the secret; with unheeding wit he has gone blind.

43. Why play the dog and the skull-carrying ascetic? Say "Ram", O sadhu. These are frauds for the belly's sake; such teaching, friend, is only trouble.

44. Even Sanaka and the others, called sadhus, fell away from the bliss of bhajan (devotional song). Yet Ajamil fared well, and so did the elephant, the courtesan and the hunter.

45. The whole world has been made destitute; it has lost and walked away from Hari's Name. [But] the serving-maid's son — who else caught hold of Shyam's hem?

46. The fool leaves the butter and churns the dregs alone. He turns the Name, water of the Ganga, into ashes, and takes urine for his refreshment [osan, unclear].

47. Set [Him] above your head, as a parasol casts its shade. I think: let Him be reckoned the greater, and then our work is accomplished.

48. By throwing scraps to a dog, will your forefathers receive anything? Give your love to Hari's people — that will drive away all your anguish.

49. He who makes claims is a pauper; there is no faith in his heart. He who worships Narhar with one sole claim [on Him] — call him His own true servant.

50. The whole company is asleep, snoring in its worldly hold. Raghunath keeps watch, while above, Yama's messengers prowl.

51. Set [Him] above your head, as Yama's servants cast their shadow. He knows he is made the greater, and then our work is accomplished.

52. What comes to hand he gathers in; over what does not come he makes a quarrel. Lanes crooked and straight — why does he fret himself to death for nothing?

53. True motherhood is Sita's; other mothers are mothers only within [maho mai, unclear]. They call you forward with sweet words, and then drop you into the pit.

54. The mother has turned unmotherly; no brother is a support. The son has turned unworthy; the woman has shamed the family.

55. The family looks a delight, but there is not one who loves Shyam. Why defile yourself, foolish man, by embracing them?

56. Light within darkness — that is to enjoy the company of saints. Darkness within light — that is to take pleasure with other gods.

57. The fool bathes in the Ganga and holds others off as untouchable. The defilement lies within your own "I" — and you are just that much.

58. The man whose love is bound to woman — let him not come here. Your "self" will stay behind there; do not bring that defilement [here].

59. Woman is weak in form, but she is complete in guile. Those crooked ones who set themselves against the saints — the city [puri] was abandoned there [unclear].

60. A woman goes about angry with her husband and hostile to the devotees. Though she flees she is not saved at all — she is tracked like a footprint already pressed in.

61. As a she-serpent hisses, so does the foolish, dull woman. Whatever words come out of her will fall back upon her own head.

62. Why have you fallen behind as an offender, foolish and senseless woman? Without the company of saints and the worship of Hari, one is mingled into Yama's field.

63. O woman, do not break the bond of love; good or bad, he is still your husband. The faithful wife worships her lord alone; the unfaithful one has endless [men].

64. The woman has cut the thread; the shorn one took on airs of self-importance. Afterwards the blow comes back on her, who has fallen out of the inner heart.

65. Outwardly He appears to be without attributes (nirgun); inwardly He is a storehouse of every quality. Gold is a cold thing, O Jivan, and yet it sets the whole world on fire.

66. Male and female are seen everywhere, the forms of woman and of man; but they are dolls made of the five elements — the soul is of one single nature.

67. Wherever Brahman spreads Himself out, there maya (illusion) is yoked to Him as well. One man binds it round his neck and drowns; another parts from it and is free.

68. See all as one with each other, if no separation is left within. If a creature lives only by the conjunction of its karma, then whatever the Doer does, that alone comes to pass.

69. Bali's sacrifice was made holy when Vaman entered it. But the one who does not offer his own self as the oblation is not saved — Yama seizes him by the hair.

70. The whole company has lost its way, blind to this offering of the self. If the soul itself has no fitness (adhikar) for it, what is the fool worshipping in an image?

71. All this deceit is for the belly's sake — speaking truth and falsehood by turns. Such a life is a boat with no boatman, tossed about among the waves.

72. Listen to the Vedas and the Puranas, from the blessed mouths of Shukdev and Vyas: Ajamil was carried across by the Lord's own qualities — then why should His servant drown in the water of worldly existence?

73. As the water-bird lives in the water — so the devotee of Hari lives in the midst of maya: the same outside as within, and it lifts off and flies into the sky.

74. The elephant does not pull the plough, the lion does not eat grass, the swan does not peck at fish — just so, the Lord's servant speaks of nothing other than Him.

75. He lays claim to mastery, while the craving still sits inside his mind. One who runs away is rescued nowhere — not even in the shade of Mount Sumeru.

76. The soul's wavering does not cease — not for Sanaka and the rest, right from the beginning. The company of saints (satsang) is attained only by one of great good fortune.

77. The sannyasis all know Shiva; the yogis, Gorakhnath. The brahmin worships for the world of Brahma; the devotee worships Raghunath alone.

78. I have found the secret of the Vedas; in the kateb (the Semitic scriptures) there is nothing further. Ram is the knower of the innermost heart — remember Him there, within the mind.

79. Beautiful, dark-hued in colour: come to recognize the soul. Ram is none other than your own self; then [unclear — "to pavak dhan pakde vali"].

80. I serve Sita's Lord always, whose dwelling is the ocean of milk. That same One plays in Nanda's courtyard — He who is the light of the perfect Brahman.

81. The formless One rests on no support; taking form, He is bliss itself. He whom Yashomati dandles in her lap is the perfect supreme joy.

82. With form and without form is the dark-hued One who plays at Nanda's door. From Him arose the primal Omkar, out of which millions of universes spread wide.

83. Three crore women are Yours, with handmaids and servants at Your door to behold. And this family of ours — Vitthal may sell it off and give it away as He pleases.

84. May Your household be well: this is our blessing. O dark-hued, discerning One — so speaks Jivan, the beggar at Your door.

85. These couplets (dohas) are Yours, Damodar — who else has the power to utter them? Draw as You think best: the string is in Your own hand.

86. Damodar, You are the one who sent these couplets — so what fault of ours is it? Forward or backward, in the end it is only a useless weight upon my head.

87. Grant it this once, this time; Father, do not cast me off. In Nanda's court even Kuber's worthless sons are ferried across.

88. The soul's service is small, yet its expectation in the mind is so large. Vitthal gives away Vaikunth itself — Krishna gives it simply because He was asked.

89. I bow to the Name of Narhari, by which the account kept by Yama is settled. Repetition, austerity, pilgrimage, alms-giving — what purpose is served by these?

90. [unclear — "badhu beaj var, buchat brahman Narhare"]. In Nanda's court, lineage counts for nothing there.

91. To please the Shaligram (the sacred stone form of the Lord), keep the company of saints. In the charnamrit, the water of Hari's feet, drink the nectar-juice within.

92. One alone pervades every heart, but where there is no love He withdraws again. The fool chews at bamboo — what purpose of sugarcane is served by that?

93. They roam about like ghosts, the brahmin no less than the renunciate. Not having known the Name of Ram, what great fortune is won by going on pilgrimage?

94. A whole age has gone by in pondering, and it is still the first day. Either the company of saints is worn out and worthless, or your own mind is false.

95. They go about noseless and mutilated — holy men with no chosen deity (ishta) of their own. They are shrines with no image in them: there is no way such worship can be offered.

96. If Sarasvati's favour comes, it is the dark-hued One who brings it. Radha's rasa-dance and delight — let the mind hold no sourness about it.

97. Speech, word and discernment have no beauty without the dark-hued Lord. There is true water in the well, yet the blind man falls into the ruined, dry well of death.

98. [unclear — "khadha khadha"]; all are one, and if you know this, then own it. The forests of karma — cut them down with the name of Trikam.

99. In that easy, natural drift they all float along — king, nobleman and faqir alike. Just as a log floats easily down the river and never once reaches the bank.

100. Why should a coward take up the work? He has strayed onto the field of heroes. Those who have died are the living; the living are the very ghosts.

101. A woman not devoted to her husband — I see no fitness (adhikar) in her at all. Such are a realm with no Yama for its king, and a human being with no head.

102. The pandit reads the Puranas and makes his own self out to be something great. It is all in order to fill his belly — what purpose is served by that?

103. The true meaning of the Veda was spoken by Shukdev. The offence of the royal sage fell away the very instant it was heard with the ears.

104. Why do you make it hard for yourself, O servant? Remember Ram, and it turns easy. As for the toll Yama levies — He will tear up the bond on your whole caravan.

105. At this hour, this one time, let a man remember the dark-hued Lord. No one at all will come along with him at that gathering at the cremation ground.

106. Separation from the beloved — will there be a meeting again, or will there not? The Sadguru's arm is the only support; some rare one will still be there at that meeting.

107. The string is in Your hand, Trikam, to draw the three worlds along. The fault is mine and mine alone — will You then let go and abandon me, Mavji?

108. If You do set me down, set me down among Your devotees. Then only that one thing rests upon You — Madhav, what will it cost You to let go?

109. In the market and on the road Hari is seen; no place at all is empty of Him. The fool does not know this secret — the Lord rests in the heart of the saint.

110. He has come to rest in the knowledge of Brahman, and has made all ritual action void. With ghosts everything is on credit; here it must all be taken in ready cash.

111. Sita's Lord is that same dark-hued One: as Raghuvir He carries the bow; and He sounds the flute at His lips and sports as a cowherd.

112. The devotee ate his plain rice; the Lord of the universe kept company with the rustic. The poison-draught of maya — some rare saint has drunk it down.

113. The Lord Himself turned beggar, who begged at Bali's door. And the cowherds' fresh butter — that He tasted, stealing it again and again.

114. He falls short not even once: the perfect Brahman remains full. Yet He steals the butter and eats it — in order to make the incomplete ones complete.

115. The verses (richa) and the Upanishads, limbs of the Veda, are claimed as one's own. Win Him over with bhakti (devotion) — why leave that aside and go elsewhere?

116. The woman went about her work, mindful of husband and elders. Then Vitthal sounded His bamboo flute — and she was enchanted by that sound.

117. This humming in the heart is no vanity: Damodar was bound with a rope. Let the Vedas consider it — in the loosing of that knot the world was set free.

118. Such is the power of His grace (prasad) that all seven sons were called back to mind. [unclear — "shri chandvo Kahan"]; by Nanda's son they were delivered.

119. You are the manifest proof — You who held up Mount Govardhan upon Your hand; Lord who swallowed the forest fire, by whose Name Ajamil was delivered.

120. Our path is an intricate one; only some rare person ponders it from the Guru's own mouth. Some turn to the mosque, some to the temple — the whole world has lost its way.

121. Make the heart an ocean in which He is present; let wisdom raise up the pir (spiritual guide) within. Make the mind a murid (disciple) and take up the sword — so a man goes on his way having conquered the world.

122. One sees a house of unbelief here — where is the Hindu, where the Muslim? Belonging neither to the faith (din) nor to the world, they have thrown this pride of theirs into the ashes.

123. Some say Ram, some say Rahman, some say Khuda. But if there is no sight of Him within the heart, from where will paradise be got?

124. Musalman, show a little mercy (meher); give up all this talk of wrath. Stay steadily with your own faith — and paradise will stretch out its hand to you.

125. They recite the kalima of Mahmud, and everyone gives his blessing. One man cries out in God's name — and offers up a head for slaughter.

126. He performs namaz three times over, [unclear — "tatak piyari pith"]. He will go bound to hell, having forsaken the Prophet's own way.

127. The Musalmans have become like cockerels; the qazi and the brahmin are death itself. The Veda and the kateb have turned into a hangman's noose, and the whole world has been brought down.

128. In earlier times they worshipped the Prophet, and by that one intention they attained the One. Then they grew greedy for six small coins, and afterwards came to disgrace.

129. Everything is seen as one single form; but for the blind man the veil of adjuncts (upadhi) never lifts. Strung on one thread they are all one, yet each amla bead stays separate.

130. As a river is without water, so is religious garb without Hari. He lost the original seed and sowed a dry field.

131. The fool has been snared by charms and mantras; by his own [mis]understanding he turns into a ghost. Whatever infatuation has seized, he will not let go, like a Marwari's camel.

132. Every wearer of religious garb claims liberation, while leaning on the world for support. The fool does not know the secret; he has merely spread out a tidy display.

133. What discrimination is there in outward garb, when even Sanaka and the other sages fell into doubt? Claiming the authority of their chosen deity, they have measured everything by their own selves.

134. He wears two or four rosaries and the fool rejoices inwardly. He is [like] a woman of Gatrada [unclear], making empty flourishes for nothing.

135. It is the harlotry of a prostitute: he hears many words with his ears and is not carried across even a little, like a woman without desire in the act of love.

136. Why did you squander yoga? Not one of the senses came to rest. This offence has clung to you: the blind man has ruined his own soul.

137. The wife says "he is my husband (mati)," the mother says "he is my son." Clay (mati) merged back into clay; the soul remained an avadhut, untouched.

138. A woman is blameless if a devotee of Vishnu is born of her; otherwise she has littered like a sow, and [her offspring] wander roaming from jungle to jungle.

139. In the name of the guru's glory he eats his bread and gruel; it is the fraud of the belly - he has made a "mother" of house after house.

140. For this offence, why should the foolish man be cast off? The waters of a river, once they enter the Ganga, become good.

141. Look to the earlier tradition, from whose mouth the Vedas spread out. Behold Him within this body-vessel - He is the support of the soul.

142. The bard does not sing of God; it is all the fraud of the belly. The fool serves human beings and abandons Kamalakanth (Lakshmi's lord, Vishnu).

143. The bard has laid out his road: he has waited upon the goddess of poverty. The true giver is the Creator, yet he goes about the open lanes and alleys [unclear].

144. Why is the Gadhvi (bard) so crazed that he mocks the devotees of Hari? The dolt has lost the road; Yama's servants follow at his heels.

145. Better than a brahmin is the bharda who begs his fasting-grain and eats it. Do not seat the brahmin beside you and give him your affection.

146. Marks of kumkum have been made all over the bharda's body. His hereditary calling will not leave him, like a buffoon mixed in among devotees.

147. All the places of pilgrimage have fallen into doubt; let no one go inside them. Karma will cling to us if we fall under such a brahmin's shadow.

148. Endless crores [of appearances] are so much sweepings; the root of every sect is one. Behold Narsingh (Narasimha) in every heart, and the thorn of doubt is gone.

149. The seven continents and the nine regions - His form pervades them all. He is seen with conch and discus: Narsingh, of matchless form.

150. Narsingh is the fearless one, the lord of Sita; reflect and consider this in your mind. The soul has strayed in delusion, but by the Satguru's word it crosses over.

151. None is fearless like Narsingh; for the one whose delusion is a tangled knot, He will make all things one, as oil merges into ghee.

152. For Prahlad's sake He entered the pillar and roared out of it. No hardship ever fell upon His devotees - has He now grown old, or has He been defeated?

153. Ramji is the life of all; Ram is the servant of His saints. He took this vow from the time when He shone forth as Narsingh.

154. For the sake of Shankhasur the hero went down into the netherworld. He flung the waters up with his tail; then the ocean admitted defeat.

155. Dhruv's kingdom is unshakable; he shines in the twenty-first sphere of the universe. Such is the greatness of a saint - it is worth telling, and telling it serves its purpose.

156. Hanuman, why did your face turn black? This fault clung to you - that you stayed on to watch the dance-show.

157. What shame is there in saying "Ram"? The fool will not utter it with his mouth. When Yama seizes him by the hair, how will you howl then, poor wretch?

158. He worships the shaligram stone always, but his mind is a stump of hard khair wood. All eight watches of the day he goes about loaded down, like a Marwari's camel.

159. With love [sing] sakhis (couplets) and shabads; let us meet and sing the song together. Let us share gruel and bread together - this is the love of the Lord.

160. The traveller has set out on his road, having seen [only] a quilt and a cot. In the blink of an eye, within five days, he will rise and walk his way.

163. [printed number; the sequence indicates 161] Do not load on too heavy a burden - brahmins and banias are frail. What strength has a body like ours? Whatever comes together comes of itself, naturally.

162. The bania drives his bargain, going forward and drawing back again. The gracious Lord of mercy - who knows whether He will be found that way or not.

163. Whatever is given with respect, I take with my lap spread open. The thing stays in its own place; let the one who is thirsty drink.

164. I am God's beggar; whatever crumbs are given, that I eat. Honour and insult are nothing to me; joyfully I sing Hari's praises.

165. The glory of the rosary and the tilak has spread through the three worlds. In the dispute between Janak and Yama, this was made manifest.

166. Wear one rosary - what will many rosaries accomplish? The bee lives entirely on fragrance; the one who eats the flower is left bloated.

167. As cold is driven off by a fire, so are sins driven off by Hari's name. Night and day do not let go of satsang (holy company) and the company of sadhus.

168. In his conceit he says "I have taken the fort," though the sovereign's rule is not his at all. The whole company is of one kind: when one barks, all bark.

169. Outwardly he looks a renunciate, but inside is a hunger for maya. How can these two go together? The slip lands one in Yama's snare.

170. Maya and Brahman are not two separate things, like milk in water. The fool drinks them mixed together as one; some rare saint churns out the pure.

171. The padmini, the perfect beauty, was left behind; Kubja's longing went ahead. Broken, crippled and lame she was, yet she caught hold of Hari's shelter.

172. From the mind (mansa) the goddess arose, and from her came Omkar. Hari pervades every heart, and He is the one who plays at Nand's door.

173. The expanse of Brahman and of the Vedas - Shukdev spoke it from his own blessed mouth. The formless One, in His own nature, wandered from door to door.

174. Damodar the compassionate, who let Himself be bound with a cord - for the sake of the twin Yamalarjun trees He was bound, only to loosen their bondage.

175. Another dark one stands at the door; by the Dark One the dark is carried across. Dark is Kamalakanth; by a mere dark plantain who can cross over? [unclear]

176. Sisters, such an occasion will not come a second time. Maya will be met with many times over, but a gathering of saints will not come again.

177. Kanha (Krishna) worked havoc; He was keen as a needle's point. Everyone took Him for a herdsman, but no one knew Him as the Lord of the three worlds.

178. He is the women's little boy; [unclear]. In the household of the Kali age, Jivan says, kinship is with the Vaishnavs.

179. If one speaks little, what is spoken will stand as unshakable words. Make your resolve firm and let it rain down [unclear]; then, friend, your eyes will find rest.

180. Make friendship with the highest people, so that love goes on increasing. In low company the letter and the word keep dwindling, until they dwindle away to nothing.

|| Here end the dohas of Shri Vaishnav Jivandasji, complete. ||

sections.title_en: The Word Itself Is God
sections.translit:
kabir sabad sabad sab ko kahe | sabadku hath na panv |
ek sabad okhad kare | ek sabad kare ghav ||1||

shabad brahma re parbrahmasu rato e | mato e tahra nam su e ||2||
- Vadu Dhol

brahma ja bole brahma ja sambhale | brahma dekhne parbrahma jape e ||3||
- Ved Puran

anvar shabad brahma su magun e | hun nathi nishche ek tuhaj ag e |4|
- Prithvi Dhol

sahasra athasi sarsa brahma ved bhane jo re |
jahan lagi hato kunvarado parbrahma vanino bharthar re |
tahan lagi sankasht bandhan sukh nahi ek var re ||5||
- Vani

indra ishwar brahma ved vanche | tahan nirgun narayan keme na rache ||6||

kavi shabad brahma vinve | parbrahma ray avdhar ||
tun agal ko jan nathi | hindola re atmane lyo have par ||7||
sections.translation:
1. Kabir: the word, the word - everyone speaks of the word; yet the word has neither hands nor feet. One word works as medicine; another word inflicts a wound.

The word, speech, has no hands or feet, yet fitting speech uplifts us and unfitting speech drags us down.

Vachan, the spoken word, is the principle that instructs. Adhyaruji calls the word Brahman; Jivanji calls the word Parmeshwar (God).

2. The word is Brahman, absorbed in Parbrahman; it is intoxicated with Your name. - from the Vadu Dhol

The word, speech, is absorbed in Parbrahman, and it is intoxicated with the Lord's name.

3. Brahman alone speaks, Brahman alone listens; Brahman is the one who sees, and He does japa (repetition of the name) of Parbrahman. - from the Ved Puran

The one who speaks the word is Brahman, God Himself, and the one who hears the word is Brahman too; Brahman is the seer, and God Himself is the one who repeats the name.

4. Unwed, I ask this of the Shabda-Brahman; I cannot be certain - You alone are before me. - from the Prithvi Dhol

In the Prithvi Dhol it is said that this request is made of the Shabda-Brahman, the Supreme Self: just as a sakhi (a bride's companion) goes along with the married woman, so speech, the word, stays as a companion with Brahman, the Lord. But I cannot decide whether my pride in reaching You through the Vedic word or the mantra-word is well founded or not.

5. Though eighty-eight thousand [rishis] and Brahma himself recite the Vedas so well - as long as Parbrahman, the husband of speech, has remained unwed, so long there is bondage and distress, and not even once the joy [of union]. - from the Vani

Eighty-eight thousand rishis and beings like Brahma recite the Vedic word, and even so Parbrahman, the lord of speech, remains unwed - because while the bonds of ritual action (karmakand) persist, the joy of attaining God is not obtained.

6. Indra, Shiva and Brahma read the Vedas, yet there the attributeless Narayan takes no delight at all.

In the Sant Sohago it is said: Indra, Shiva and Brahma recite the Vedas, but the attributeless Brahman, God who is beyond all qualities, is not pleased by the Vedic word.

7. The poet makes his plea to Shabda-Brahman: O king Parbrahman, take heed. There is none who knows [anything] before You; O Hindola, now carry this soul across.

In the Hindola, Adhyaruji, who sings twenty-eight kirtans (hymns), prays to the Supreme Self who becomes manifest in the form of speech: Lord! You alone must decide - before You no one can know the secret of Your Shabda-Brahman; but accept the words spoken through these kirtans and deliver us.

Closing words: In Jivanji's vani (utterance), in Adhyaruji's vani, in the vani of the saints and in Kabir's vani, the Shabda-Brahman resides; and so Adhyaru's kirtans and Jivanji's sakhis (couplets) and dohas stand manifest before us as Parmeshwar Himself. May we attain this Supreme Self through the word from the guru's own mouth - that is the wish.

Wishing well-being to the community of devotees who are the recipients of the grace of Namdev and Kabir - with the respectful love of Swami Jagdish. Ramkabir.
